And when Bela was dead, Jobab the son of Zerah of Bozrah reigned in his stead. [44]

Jobab (Gen 36:33): a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "a cry." He was the son of Joktan [23], and it is not known where this Arab tribe dwelt. One of the kings of Moab also bears the same name (Gen 36:23-34; 1 Chr 1:44-45).
And when Jobab was dead, Husham of the land of the Temanites reigned in his stead. [45]
Husham (Gen 36:34): a Hebrew name meaning "haste" and "emotion." A man from the land of the Temanites, who succeeded Jobab as king over Edom.
And when Husham was dead,
Hadad the son of Bedad, which smote Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his stead: and the name of his city was Avith. [46]

Hadad or Hadar (Gen 36:35-36): a Semitic name meaning "brave," a king of Edom; his father's name was Bedad, and his capital was Avith. There is another Edomite king with the same name (Gen 36:39), whose capital was Pau or Pai.
Avith (Gen 36:35): an Edomite name meaning "ruin," an Edomite city, the birthplace of King Hadad. Perhaps it is today "Mahal el-Juthth" near Maan.
And when Hadad was dead, Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his stead. [47]
Samlah (Gen 36:36): a Hebrew name meaning "garment." The name of one of the ancient kings of Edom. He reigned before there was a king in Israel, and the capital of his kingdom was Masrekah.
Masrekah (Gen 36:36): an Edomite name, perhaps meaning "vineyard," a city in Edom, the birthplace of Samlah king of Edom, which is on Mount Mishraq, which lies twenty-two miles south of Maan.
And when Samlah was dead, Shaul of Rehoboth by the river reigned in his stead. [48]
Shaul of Rehoboth (Gen 36:37): Shaul is a Hebrew name meaning "asked of God." He was one of the kings of Edom, from Rehoboth, which lies on the River Euphrates (Gen 36:37).
And when Shaul was dead, Baal-hanan the son of Achbor reigned in his stead. [49]
Achbor (Gen 36:38): Achbor is a Semitic name meaning "mouse"; he was a king of Edom.
And when Baal-hanan was dead, Hadad reigned in his stead: and the name of his city was Pai; and his wife's name was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab. [50]
Mehetabel the daughter of Matred (Gen 36:39): a Semitic name meaning "one to whom God is kind." The daughter of Matred and wife of Hadad king of Edom.
Hadad died also. And the dukes of Edom were;
duke Timnah, duke Aliah, duke Jetheth, [51]
Duke Aholibamah, duke Elah, duke Pinon, [52]
Aholibamah (Gen 36:41): a Hebrew name meaning "my tent is a high place," a duke in Edom.
The wife of Esau bore the same name, the daughter of Anah the Hivite (Gen 36:2), and she was also called Judith.
Elah (or Elath): a Hebrew name meaning "oak tree," a duke in Edom (Gen 36:41).
Pinon (Gen 36:41): a duke in Edom, who perhaps dwelt in the city of Punon, lying on the eastern side of the Arabah about five and a half miles east of Khirbet Nahas.
Duke Kenaz, duke Teman, duke Mibzar, [53]
Kenaz (Gen 36:42): a Semitic name, perhaps meaning "hunting." He was the son of Eliphaz the son of Esau (Gen 36:11), and became a duke in Edom.
Teman (Gen 36:42): a Hebrew name meaning "the right-hand or the southern," the firstborn of Eliphaz the son of Esau, who became a duke in Edom.
Mibzar (Gen 36:42): a Hebrew name meaning "fortress," a duke in Edom.
Duke Magdiel, duke Iram.
These are the dukes of Edom. [54]
Magdiel (Gen 36:43): an Edomite name meaning "glory of God," a duke in Edom.
Iram (Gen 36:43): a Hebrew name meaning "watchful," a duke in Edom.
A genealogy, or a journey with God?!
v By Your Holy Spirit open my eyes, that I may enjoy the sweetness of the joyful journey of life with You!
I stand in perplexity, with wondrous amazement at the works of Your love!
I see in the genealogy (1 Chr 1-9) a delightful journey in Your company.
I will not begin it unless I throw myself into Your embrace and feel Your company with me.
I see that You are the beginning of the journey and You are its end, and You are the One who carries my depths, so I rest upon Your shoulders all along the way!
v The Jews cared to record the genealogies, that every believer might know to which tribe he belongs!
And might know his portion of the Promised Land in Canaan!
But as for me, I reckon myself as though I belong to the tribe of the heavenly ones!
I look for nothing but the heavenly Canaan, my eternal inheritance!
You are my portion, my wealth, my treasure, my joy and my crown.
Grant me to meet some of my fathers, and to enter with them into a frank conversation of love, that I may enjoy the journey of my life.
I meet Adam, and see him rejoicing and happy!
I hear him say: "Since my God gave me Seth as a son, I was comforted.
I saw him bearing my image as I was before the corruption, to some degree.
I saw him as a type of the new Adam, my Savior and the Savior of my offspring.
I was comforted together with the partner of my life, and we no longer remembered Cain, the killer of his brother.
I no longer saw him trembling and terrified, as though all creation were against him.
I no longer grieved over Abel, whose blood cries to heaven!
I saw You, my Savior, and I rejoiced because my offspring clung to You.
By Your blood, O Lover of mankind, You repaired what I had corrupted in the life of all my offspring!
v I went on from Adam and Eve to their grandson Enosh!
I rejoiced when I saw him, and understood what the prophet Moses wrote about him:
Then began men to call upon the name of the LORD" (Gen 4:26).
I saw him distinguished, for he was the first to praise God without ceasing.
His heart was aflame with love for You, so he praised You by day and by night.
He became the first teacher of the life of praise!
He longed that all the offspring of Adam would share with the heavenly ones their praises.
v The personality of his grandson Mahalaleel drew me; his life is in harmony with his name, he does not cease to rejoice in You.
His heart, which knows nothing but thanksgiving and praise to God, presented to us from his offspring "Enoch," who was found worthy to be translated by the Lord to Himself.
Let me repeat with the wise man: "He was snatched away lest evil should change his mind...
He was living among sinners and He translated him" (Wis 4:10-11).
Enoch flew on the wings of love, when he was caught up to heaven (Gen 5:24).
v Enoch passed quickly through the days of his exile, and the Lord gathered him to Himself from the face of evil.
And his son Methuselah came and lived nearly a thousand years.
His life was very long, but his life ended in death.
The years of his life passed like a moment of time, so it no longer concerns us how many years we dwell in exile.
v His son Lamech opened a dangerous door in the life of mankind.
He was not committed, like the first man, to one Eve.
Lamech was the first to marry two women, and so he corrupted the concept of marital love and the unity of the family.
We say with St. Mar Ephrem that by his marriage his life was filled with toil.
So he looked forward to the Messiah born of a virgin to give him rest and righteousness.
v I pass quickly to righteous Noah in the midst of a dark and crooked generation.
The Lord commanded him to make an ark, in order to flood the whole world.

And the nations and peoples believed in You, and became members of Your holy body.

These are the sons of Israel;
Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun, [1]
Dan, Joseph, and Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher. [2]
He begins with the names of the sons of Jacob, whom God called Israel, but they are not in the order of the date of birth.

The sons of Jacob and the twelve tribes occur more than 20 times in the Holy Bible, each time in a different order according to the purpose of mentioning the tribes. They occur in the First Book of Chronicles three times (1 Chr 2:1-2; 2:3-8:34; 12:23-27). I would like to write a special appendix on the order of the names of these tribes in the most important places in the Holy Bible.

The book does not refer here to any event in the life of Jacob; what concerns it is to record his name as God gave it to him, "Israel," since this name points to the attachment of the twelve tribes to him.

In the midst of distress Jacob laid his head on a stone, and lay down on the way, to see the heavens open, and a heavenly ladder set up on the earth with its top touching heaven (Gen 28:12-15). In this place Jacob received a divine promise for himself and his offspring: "In thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed... for I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken to thee of" (Gen 28:14-15). What is the secret of the blessing that is in him and in his offspring, except that in his loins was Judah, who begets David, and from his offspring the Word of God becomes incarnate, who blesses all the families of the earth by His Cross and the power of His resurrection?!

v The stone under his head is Christ, for he had had no stone under his head before, but he had one at that time when he fled from his persecutor. When he was in his father's house, at rest according to the flesh, he did not enjoy a stone under his head. He left his house like a poor man and became like one alone, having nothing but a staff, and in the same night he found a stone to put under his head. And when he had a pillow of this kind, his head rested through the vision he saw[1].

St. Jerome He spoke afterward about the line of the twelve tribes in the following chapters, and it seems that the writer hastens as fast as possible to the emergence of the kingdom of David, which occupies the two books, where he wishes to speak of the house of David seated on the throne, in order to carry our thought across to the Son of David, the King of kings.

It is observed in the mention of the sons of Jacob (Israel) that they are not mentioned in order, but he began with the sons of Leah, then the two sons of Rachel (Joseph and Benjamin) between Dan and Naphtali the sons of Bilhah, and at the end the sons of Zilpah, Leah's maidservant, Gad and Asher.

We observe in the genealogies that he paid attention to the genealogies of the two tribes of Judah and Levi, the royal tribe and the priestly tribe. The genealogies of Judah occupy 102 verses, Levi 81 verses, while the genealogies of all the rest of the tribes together occupy 126 verses.

He wanted to affirm the obligation of cooperation among the tribes in spite of the differences between them, each tribe completing the rest of the tribes and needing them, and they needing it and not able to do without it, especially between the royal tribe and the priestly tribe.

We will see this in a practical and clear way when all the tribes meet together in Hebron around David to make him king over them all. Each tribe offers what it has of abilities and gifts, not in a spirit of competition or jealousy or boasting or superiority, but as it is said: "All these men of war, that could keep rank, came with a perfect heart to Hebron, to make David king over all Israel... of one heart... for there was joy in Israel" (1 Chr 12:38-40).
I mention, by way of example, what some of the tribes were distinguished by:
a. The tribe of Judah, the foremost and royal.
b. The tribe of Levi, indispensable, from which came the priests the sons of Kohath, and the Levites with their varied roles in service, guarding and praise.
c. The tribe of Benjamin, who accompanied Judah wherever they were found, and who were ahead of others in choosing David as king, although they were brothers of Saul, who resisted and envied David.
d. Joseph, the one with two portions, the only one who became two tribes: Ephraim and Manasseh.

We will return, God willing, to speak about all the tribes, especially Judah and Levi. But here we wish to affirm that the sons of Jacob or Israel... found in David the king a leader who gathers all together to work for the glory of God!

The sons of Jacob or Israel bear types, especially Joseph, who was greatly beloved of his father. I content myself here with quoting a little of what the Fathers said about him as a type of the Lord Christ:
v Jacob loved his son, because the Father loves His only-begotten Son, for He says: "This is my beloved Son" (Mt 3:17)[2].

Father Caesarius, bishop of Arles v Joseph was persecuted, and his brothers were the persecutors. Joseph was glorified, and his persecutors bowed down to him, and his dreams and visions were fulfilled.
The persecuted Joseph was a type of the persecuted Jesus.
His father clothed Joseph with a coat of many colors, and Jesus His Father clothed with a body from the Virgin.
His father loved Joseph more than his brothers, and Jesus is the dear beloved of His Father.
Joseph saw visions and dreamed dreams, and the visions and the prophets were fulfilled in Jesus.
Joseph was a shepherd with his brothers, and Jesus is the Chief Shepherd.

When his father sent him to visit his brothers, they saw Joseph coming and planned to kill him, and when the Father sent Jesus to visit His brothers, they said: "This is the heir; come, let us kill him" (Mt 21:38).
The brothers of Joseph cast their brother into the pit, and Jesus was brought down by His brothers to dwell among the dead.
Joseph came up from the pit, and Jesus rose from the dead.

Joseph, after he rose from the pit, had authority over his brothers, and Jesus, after He dwelt among the dead, His Father gave Him a great and glorified name (Phil 2:9) that His brothers might serve Him and His enemies be subdued under His feet.

After Joseph's brothers knew him, they were ashamed and afraid and astonished before his greatness, and when Jesus comes at the end of time and declares His greatness, His brothers will be ashamed and afraid and tremble before Him because they crucified Him.
Moreover, Joseph was sold into Egypt on the counsel of Judah, and Jesus was delivered to the Jews by the hands of Judas Iscariot.
When they sold Joseph, his brothers did not answer a word, and Jesus also did not speak nor answer the judges who tried Him.
Joseph was delivered to prison unjustly by his master, and Jesus was condemned unjustly by the sons of His people.
Joseph surrendered his two garments, one in the hands of his brothers and the other in the hand of his master's wife, and Jesus surrendered His garments, and they were divided among the soldiers.

Joseph, when he was thirty years old, stood before Pharaoh and became lord of Egypt, and Jesus, when He reached thirty, came to the Jordan to be baptized, and received the Spirit and went out preaching.
Joseph sustained Egypt with bread, and Jesus sustained the whole world with the bread of life.
Joseph took the daughter of the wicked, unclean priest as his wife, and Jesus betrothed to Himself the Church from the unclean Gentiles.
Joseph died and was buried in Egypt, and Jesus died and was buried in Jerusalem.

The bones of Joseph were brought up by his brothers from Egypt, and Jesus His Father raised from the dwelling of death and He put on His body, and was lifted up with it to heaven without corruption[3].
St. Aphrahat the Persian Sage

The sons of Judah; Er, and Onan, and Shelah:
which three were born unto him of the daughter of Shua the Canaanitess.
And Er, the firstborn of Judah, was evil in the sight of the LORD; and he slew him. [3]

The First Book of Chronicles centers on the tribe of Judah, although Judah is the fourth son of Jacob, to hasten the believer to the meeting with David the prophet, and to become acquainted in Second Chronicles with the house of David, especially the kings, whether Solomon before the division or his son Rehoboam and all the kings of Judah after the division until the fall under the Babylonian captivity and the return to Jerusalem. The purpose of these two books is the entry of every soul into the enjoyment of the Son of David, the Word incarnate, who establishes His kingdom in the heart of the true believer.

Judah was the foremost of his brothers, because from him the Messiah comes, for his father blessed him, saying: "The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be" (Gen 49:10).

With all this the writer reveals Judah, who held the position of the birthright, so that his tribe became the royal tribe leading Israel; the Holy Bible mentioned the weaknesses of Judah, among them the following:

a. He married a Canaanite girl, "the daughter of Shua" (Gen 38:1-3). The Holy Bible did not hide this fact, but repeated it in (1 Chr 2:3), to affirm that the choice of Judah as the royal tribe from whose offspring the Word of God becomes incarnate does not rest on human righteousness or personal merit, but on the wondrous grace of God, who turned this wrong conduct to good. For by his marriage to the Canaanite woman he opened the door of hope before the Gentiles, declaring that salvation is offered to all, to the Jew as to the Gentile.

The daughter of Shua: the word "Shua" is a Semitic name meaning "wealth," and he was a Canaanite man. Perhaps Judah married her for the wealth of her father or for her beauty. But God by His grace granted that there should become incarnate from his offspring the Creator of heaven and earth, the source of true wealth and beauty.

b. The daughter of Shua bore Judah his three sons: Er, Onan and Shelah. It is said of his firstborn son: "And Er, the firstborn of Judah, was evil in the sight of the LORD; and he slew him." Er is a Hebrew name meaning "watchful." Neither the Book of Genesis nor the First Book of Chronicles says what Er's sin was, but is content to say that God allowed his early death, because he was wicked in the sight of the Lord. Most likely God allowed him to be killed in Canaan at an early age because of the multitude of his evils. This is the firstborn of Judah by the Canaanite woman!

History has covered over the evil of Er, but since Er persisted in it and offered no repentance for it, it remained engraved, to be declared on the great day of the Lord. So it befits us not to be concerned to cover up our evils, but to wash them in the blood of the Lamb through sincere repentance, and the return to the bosom of God, open to every person however great his evil.

c. When Er died without having a son, his brother Onan married Tamar, his brother's widow, to beget a son who would be attributed to his dead brother, and Onan died without begetting. Judah feared for his third son Shelah, lest he marry her and die (Gen 38:6-11). Tamar resorted to a ruse to bear a son: she took off her widow's garments, and covered herself with a veil and disguised herself, and Judah thought her a harlot, and asked to come in to her. And when she conceived he ordered her to be burned, but she disclosed to him that the one in her womb was from him. Judah went in to her, supposing her a harlot, and was not ashamed to ask about the harlot among many, and when he discovered that Tamar was with child he asked for her to be burned! This Judah confessed that Tamar, the wife of his wicked son Er, was more righteous than he.

This is Judah, whose tribe later became the royal tribe. The Lord's choice to become man from this tribe, with Judah at its head, and to have in His lineage Tamar, the widow of wicked Er, confirms to us that He came for the sake of sinners and all the nations, opening the gates of heaven before every person who clings to Him, whatever his past or lineage or nationality. He is a lover of all mankind.

Although Reuben is the firstborn son of Jacob, the line of genealogies here began with Judah, though he is the fourth of the sons of Jacob, because the tribe of Judah was distinguished as the royal tribe, and the Lord Christ, the Word incarnate, came from his offspring (Gen 38:2-10, 13-30). From it came David the king, and from it St. Mary, in whose womb the King of kings became incarnate.
Although the tribe of Judah took the place of precedence, yet the Lord put to death Judah's firstborn "Er," because he was wicked in the sight of the Lord.

The hideous sin of Reuben, for which the Scripture does not say he offered repentance, cost him much: 1. The loss of his privileges as firstborn. 2. The loss of the possibility that the Messiah would come from his offspring. 3. The loss of his life.
His name became a stigma of shame in the record of his clan. The psalmist says: "For evildoers shall be cut off: but those that wait upon the LORD, they shall inherit the earth" (Ps 37:9).

v These (the wicked), according to the testimony of the psalmist, have tongues like a sharp sword, and teeth that are spears and arrows (Ps 57:4). But the wonderful thing is that while they attack others they do not harm them, but they themselves are torn by their own tongues, because they carry within them anger, resentment, envy, deceit, hatred and bitterness...

And although they are unable to harm others, it turns back upon themselves first and against them, as the psalmist prays, saying: "Their sword shall enter into their own heart" (Ps 37:15). And there is also said of such a one, "His own iniquities shall take the wicked himself, and he shall be holden with the cords of his sins" (Prov 5:22)[4].
Pope Athanasius the Apostolic A question remains for us: why did God choose the tribe of Judah to be the royal tribe in spite of the faults mentioned before?

It seems to me that David, who was of the offspring of Judah, was chosen so that the incarnate Word of God might come from his offspring, for the following reasons: 1. Because of the purity of his heart, for God Himself testified of him that he was a man after God's own heart (Acts 13:22). 2. Because he rose to the commandment of the New Testament while still under the shadow of the Law, for he loved Saul, who bore bitter enmity toward him and tried with all his powers and means to kill him. 3. He was not concerned to take the throne in spite of God's promise of it to him when he was still a little boy, but what concerned him was the heavenly Kingdom. 4. He was the first man of praise even in the midst of his afflictions. 5. Because in many situations he was a type of the Lord Christ, as we shall see in the appendix to chapter ten. 6. With every fall into sin he would flood his bed every night with his tears. 7. He devoted his zeal and energies to preparing materials and arrangements for building the house of the Lord, in spite of the Lord's refusal of his request to build it, and His granting that his son should undertake this task.

So for the sake of David, who was in the loins of his grandfather Judah, this tribe was chosen to have this privilege. If the tribe of Judah had its faults, and David himself also, this did not deprive David of God's own testimony about him. Therefore we should not wonder that the Lord Christ is called the Son of David, despite his faults, and this has become His title to this day, and the Lord did not bear the title Son of Judah or Son of Abraham.

How wonderful is the love of God, for the blessing of David's purity of heart and the tears of his sincere repentance had their effect upon his ancestors up to Judah the son of Jacob and his tribe, and extended to his descendants, as we shall see in our study of Second Chronicles!

v Some are astonished that Matthew saw fit to mention in the genealogy of the Lord Christ the name of "Tamar," who seems like a harlot, and of Ruth, and of her who had been Uriah's and whom David married after he killed her husband, and did not mention the names of the holy women such as Sarah, Rebekah and Rachel...

For since Matthew was proclaiming the Lord born in the flesh, who was made sin for all, and who was exposed to insults and crucifixion, he believed that it was not fitting to show Him defending Himself against insult by having sinners among His ancestors...
So also the Church is not ashamed to be chosen from among sinners!
St. Ambrose Onan: the second son of Judah (1 Chr 2:3).
Shelah: a Hebrew name meaning "petition," the third of the sons of Judah (1 Chr 2:3).
And Tamar his daughter in law bare him Pharez and Zerah.
All the sons of Judah were five. [4]

Tamar[5]: we spoke of her before in the commentary on the preceding verse, and we saw that, since she desired, like every Hebrew woman, to bear a son, even if from her father-in-law, because she desired that the Messiah the Savior should come from her offspring, God fulfilled her request.

She agreed to expose her life to danger, so she took off her widow's garments, and put a veil on her face, and was not ashamed to appear as a harlot, not for the lust of the flesh but for the sake of bearing a child. For she clung to her father-in-law, who was a man advanced in years... And her purity is shown in that, when she disclosed the matter, she did not ask after that to marry her husband's brother, but lived with her father-in-law, and it is said: "And he knew her again no more" (Gen 38:26).

For her faith's sake she desired to bear, while Judah in his old age committed adultery... Therefore he says: "She hath been more righteous than I" (Gen 38:26). And Tamar became a living example that prevents us from condemning, however clear and tangible the signs of sin appear. St. Ambrose commented much on this phrase "she hath been more righteous than I" in his discourse on repentance, asking every person, even the bishop, not to condemn anyone, but to show mercy and compassion to sinners; among his words:

v O Lord, grant me to have the falls of every person before me, that I may bear them with him, and not rebuke him in pride, but grieve and weep, for in my weeping for others I weep for myself, saying: "She hath been more righteous than I."

Suppose a girl has fallen, deceived and swept away by circumstances that provoke sin; well! We who are older may fall also! In us also the law of the flesh wars against the law of our minds, and makes us captives to sin, so that we do what we do not want (Rom 7:23). Her youth may be an excuse for her, but what is my excuse?! She must learn, but I must know that "she hath been more righteous than I"...

May we then not be ashamed to confess that our fault is more hideous than the fault of one whom we think deserving of rebuke, for this is what Judah did, who reproved Tamar, and when he remembered his sin said: "She hath been more righteous than I"... He accused himself before others accused him[6].

St. Ambrose By this deed of faith Tamar was made worthy to be a grandmother of the Lord Christ, her blood running in His veins, so that the Evangelist Matthew recorded her name in the genealogy of the Lord Christ (Mt 1:3), while he did not record the name of Sarah or Rebekah or other blessed mothers.

Tamar was a type of the company of the Gentiles which became a holy Church for the Lord, which was formerly fruitless like Tamar, like a forsaken widow with none to support her or help her. Her first kinsman Shelah did not marry her, but she clung to the second kinsman Judah... So the company of the Gentiles did not cling to the first kinsman, that is, the Mosaic Law, nor did it bind itself to circumcision and Judaizing, but clung to the second kinsman, that is, the true Judah, our Lord Jesus Christ, who came forth from the tribe of Judah.
And the wonder is that the conduct of Tamar, as recorded in Genesis chapter (Gen 38), bore many symbols that correspond to what the Church of the Gentiles enjoyed; we mention among them:

a. Tamar put off her widow's garments, in order to cling to Judah (Gen 38:14), and so the Gentiles put off the garments of the old man to put on the new man, who befits its union with the eternal Bridegroom, indeed the Lord Christ Himself became its new garment.

b. Tamar covered her face with a veil (Gen 38:15), and the Gentiles, having received the faith, live here as in a riddle, until they meet the Bridegroom face to face, and see Him in the fullness of His glory and the greatness of His splendor, and come to know the loftiness of His surpassing mysteries.

c. Tamar sat at the entrance of Enaim (Gen 38:14), that is, the entrance of two springs, as though she were the Church of the Gentiles, which did not enjoy the spring of the Old Testament alone but also the spring of the New Testament with it.
d. Tamar enjoyed the signet of Judah and his bracelets and his staff (Gen 38:18), that is, the seal of sonship to God and the heavenly crown together with the wood of the life-giving Cross.

e. The signs of pregnancy appeared after three months (Gen 38:24), as though she were the Church of the Gentiles which bore spiritual fruits, through its faith in the Holy Trinity (3 months) and its enjoyment of the risen life in Christ Jesus, who rose on the third day.

v (Tamar) longed to have children from her father-in-law when she saw that her mother-in-law had died... This was not for lack of purity, far from it! but to avoid remaining without a memorial. In fact, what happened was by a divine plan, and the result was that her plan was accomplished...
May whoever hears this not blame Tamar. As I said before, she was fulfilling the divine plan, so no blame is cast upon her, and Judah did not make any accusation against her.
I mean that you notice here that the genealogy of Christ bears her two sons.
For in particular the two children born to him signified the two peoples, representing the Jewish life and the spiritual life[7].

St. John Chrysostom v Tamar was afraid lest she be seized and killed in revenge for his two sons, since she was accused of being the cause of their death. She asked for a sign... She appears to him in another guise so that he would not kill her, and she offers him an invitation to lie with her from his own mouth...
While Tamar was asking this of God, Judah went out and saw her.
The prayer of Tamar made him incline, contrary to custom, and go to a harlot.

And when she saw him she put on a veil, because she was afraid. And after the word concerning a sign, as she had asked, she knew that God was pleased with what she had done. After that she uncovered her face without fear, and even asked a reward from the Lord of the reward[8].

St. Mar Ephrem the Syrian In St. Cyril the Great's comment on this matter he said: [The purpose of the Holy Bible is not to relate the lives of saints, for that is not so at all, but rather to give us knowledge of the mystery of Christ through these facts, which make our speaking of Him true and clear[9].]
God by His grace made Tamar an ancestress of David, and therefore of Jesus Christ (Mt 1:3).

Pharez and Zerah: the Lord Christ came from the offspring of Pharez whom Tamar bore, and Pharez broke through before his brother Zerah while still in his mother's womb to take the birthright from him (Gen 38:27-30). At their birth, Zerah put out his hand and the midwife bound his hand with a scarlet thread, but he drew back his hand and Pharez came out first and Zerah after him. Some Fathers see in Zerah a type of the Jewish people, who should have been the firstborn, and who stretched out his hand and received the Law which centered on sacrifice (the scarlet blood), but through unbelief Pharez came out, representing the Gentiles, who obtained the firstfruits of the Spirit instead of Zerah (the Jews).
The sons of Pharez; Hezron, and Hamul. [5]

Since the first and second sons of Judah died without begetting, and the genealogies of the third are mentioned in (1 Chr 4:21-23), he was content here with these two sons, as in (Gen 46:12; Num 26:21).
Hezron: a Hebrew name meaning "enclosure, fold." He was the firstborn son of Pharez, and the founder of a family in Judah (1 Chr 2:5).

From the list of the descendants of Judah [5-6], attention was given to Hezron, and his third son Caleb came, to whom special attention was given [18-20, 42-55]; and the second son of Hezron received the first place, because from his offspring came the family of David (1 Chr 2:10-17).
Hamul: a Hebrew name meaning "carried, pitied, spared," the youngest son of Pharez, and the founder of a family in Judah (1 Chr 2:5).
And the sons of Zerah; Zimri, and Ethan, and Heman, and Calcol, and Dara:
five of them in all. [6]

"And the sons of Zerah; Zimri...": in (Josh 7:1) "Zabdi." And it is said of Solomon: "For he was wiser than all men; than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, and Chalcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol" (1 Kgs 4:31). Some think that Zerah is their remote ancestor and not their father.

These five were called the sons of Mahol (1 Kgs 4:31), as they were referred to by their fame for wisdom, in which no one surpassed them except Solomon. And since the word מָחוֹל "mahol" is found among musical instruments (Ps 149:3; 150:4), and is also used for dancing, some think that these wise men are "the sons of music." Their wisdom is manifested in composing songs of praise[10].

Ethan and Heman: they became authors of inspired psalms (Ps 88-89). They are different from the musicians whom David appointed, "Heman and Asaph and Ethan" (1 Chr 15:19), who were of the tribe of Levi and not of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 6:33-44).
And the sons of Carmi; Achar, the troubler of Israel, who transgressed in the thing accursed. [7]
Carmi also was of the sons of Zerah.

It appears from (Josh 7:1) that Carmi is the son of Zabdi or Zimri, and Achar is Achan who troubled Israel. His name in Hebrew means "the troubler" or "disaster." The story of his transgression is told in (Josh 7). It is said: "But the children of Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing: for Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took of the accursed thing: and the anger of the LORD was kindled against the children of Israel" (Josh 7:1). He hid from the spoil what he desired and was forbidden: "When I saw among the spoils a goodly Babylonish garment, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight, then I coveted them, and took them; and, behold, they are hid in the earth in the midst of my tent, and the silver under it" (Josh 7:21).

It befits us to beware lest the enemy creep in upon us through small things. St. Mark the Ascetic says: [Satan presents to us small sins that seem trivial in our eyes, because without this he cannot lead us to the great sins[11].]

Achan sinned, and the wrath of the Lord fell upon all the people. Origen says, commenting on the wedge of stolen gold: [It befits us not to neglect this phrase, for when one person commits a sin, wrath is brought upon the whole people. How does this disaster happen? When the priests, the leaders of the people, wish to appear lenient with sinners, because they fear their tongue, lest it rise against them, forgetting the firmness that befits their priesthood. By this they refuse to carry out what is written: "Them that sin rebuke before all, that others also may fear" (1 Tim 5:20), and also: "Put away from among yourselves that wicked person" (1 Cor 5:13). These priests are not inflamed with zeal for the Lord, nor do they imitate the Apostle who commands: "to deliver such an one unto Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved" (1 Cor 5:5). They behave with indifference toward the counsels of the Gospel concerning sinners. When we see a sinner, let us go to him alone, then speak to him in the mouth of two or three witnesses, but if he is careless even after the Church's rebuke of him and does not repent, let him be separated from the Church and be counted as a heathen man and a publican (Mt 18:17)[12].]
v Great is the punishment that befell them (because of Achan), but a greater punishment will befall us if we do not come to our senses by looking at their fate[13].
St. John Chrysostom
And the sons of Ethan; Azariah. [8]

Azariah: a Hebrew name meaning "whom Jehovah has helped." More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. The son of Ethan, of the sons of Zerah of the sons of Judah (1 Chr 2:8). 2. The son of Jehu the son of Obed of the sons of Jerahmeel (1 Chr 2:38-39).
The sons also of Hezron, that were born unto him; Jerahmeel, and Ram, and Chelubai. [9]
What is mentioned in verses [8-10] here is quoted from (Ruth 4:19-22).
Jerahmeel: a Hebrew name meaning "God has mercy," the son of Hezron the son of Pharez the son of Judah (1 Chr 2:4-9, 25-26, 33, 42).

Ram: a Hebrew name meaning "exalted, lofty." More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. A man of the offspring of Judah and of the sons of Hezron (1 Chr 2:9-10). 2. A man of the offspring of Judah and of the sons of Jerahmeel (1 Chr 2:25, 27).
Chelubai: the son of Hezron, and he is Caleb (1 Chr 2:9, 18, 42).
And Ram begat Amminadab; and Amminadab begat Nahshon, prince of the children of Judah; [10]

This list is certainly incomplete, for between Ram the son of Hezron and Nahshon the son of Amminadab there are three generations. For Nahshon the son of Amminadab was head of the tribe of Judah in the wilderness in the days of the prophet Moses (Ex 6:23; Num 1:7; 2:3), and his son Salmon married Rahab the harlot after the fall of Jericho (Mt 1:5).
And Nahshon begat Salma, and Salma begat Boaz, [11]
Also three other generations are omitted before reaching Boaz, the husband of Ruth, the grandfather of Jesse the father of David.
Salma [11] is Salmon (Ruth 4:20).

Boaz: he was marked by simplicity with wisdom, when he discovered the truth about Ruth the Moabitess, the poor widow of a foreign race, and her clinging to the living God, and her faithfulness to her mother-in-law. He took positive practical steps. Since he embraced Ruth although she was a Moabitess, he was made worthy that there should come from their offspring David the king and Jesus (Christ) the Son of David, the Savior of the world (see the Book of Ruth).
And Boaz begat Obed, and Obed begat Jesse, [12]

Obed: a Hebrew name meaning "servant." More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. The son of Ruth and Boaz, who is the father of Jesse the father of David (1 Chr 2:12). In the genealogies of Judah special attention was given to the father of David, Jesse [10-12], and after that his sons [13-15]. 2. The son of Ephlal, of the offspring of Sheshan, of the sons of Judah (1 Chr 2:37).

Jesse: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "man," the son of Obed and father of David and grandson of Ruth and Boaz, and the father of seven sons who had offspring (1 Chr 2:15), and an eighth who died without having offspring, and he had two daughters by a wife other than David's mother (1 Chr 2:16).
And Jesse begat his firstborn Eliab, and Abinadab the second, and Shimma the third, [13]
Eliab: a Hebrew name meaning "God is Father."
Abinadab: a Hebrew name meaning "the Father is generous or willing."
Shimea: (with a fatha on the ayin) a Hebrew name meaning "God hears," and (with a kasra on the ayin) a Hebrew name meaning "Jehovah, let him hear."
Nethaneel the fourth, Raddai the fifth, [14]
Nethaneel: a Hebrew name meaning "God has given," the fourth son of Jesse, that is, the brother of David (1 Chr 2:12-14).
Raddai: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "Jehovah has subdued," a brother of David, the fifth of the sons of Jesse (1 Chr 2:14).
Ozem the sixth, David the seventh: [15]

Ozem: a Hebrew name, probably meaning "angry." More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. A son of Jesse and brother of David of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 2:15). 2. A son of Jerahmeel in the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 2:25).

David: although he was the youngest of the sons of Jesse, he was chosen by God to begin the royal line through the generations until it reached its peak with the coming of the Son of David. He is perhaps one of the most famous figures of the Old Testament; the men of faith were looking for the coming of the Messiah, the Son of David. David the king and prophet is a wonderful example of purity of heart and holy love, and humility with courage, and his love of praise, and reliance on God, and his zeal for the glory of God, and his love and devotion to the people of God, and his longing to build the Temple. He had his bitter falls, but with every fall he rose in a spirit of sincere repentance in complete submission to the Lord's disciplines of him. This raised him in the eyes of God, so Jesus (Christ) came from his offspring, and he became a great example of repentance (Acts 13:22; 1 Kgs 16 ff.; 1 Chr 19 ff.).

In First Samuel it is mentioned that Jesse had eight sons (1 Sam 16:6-11), but here only seven are mentioned, because the eighth died without marrying or married and did not beget a child, and therefore he is no longer counted in the genealogies, and his name is not known.
Whose sisters were Zeruiah, and Abigail.
And the sons of Zeruiah; Abishai, and Joab, and Asahel, three. [16]
Zeruiah and Abigail: the line of genealogies cared not only for David the king but even for his two sisters.

Zeruiah is a Hebrew name, most probably meaning "perfumed with balm"; and Abigail is a Hebrew name meaning "my father is joy." They are two sisters, the daughters of Nahash (2 Sam 17:25), which is another name of Jesse, or the name of the wife of Jesse, or after the death of Nahash Jesse took his widow and she bore him David and his brothers, so Zeruiah and Abigail were their sisters by their mother and not by their father.

Abishai or Abshai: he and his two brothers Joab and Asahel were among the prominent heroes of their uncle David. He was brave, very impetuous. He saved David's life, and killed three hundred men at one time with his spear (see 2 Sam 23:18-23). He advised his uncle to kill King Saul while he slept at night, but he said to him: "Destroy him not: for who can stretch forth his hand against the LORD'S anointed, and be guiltless?" (1 Sam 26:9). He was marked by his faithfulness and devotion to David. He accompanied him in his wars from the face of Absalom.
When Shimei the son of Gera of the house of Saul cursed, Abishai wanted to kill him immediately, but David forbade him (2 Sam 16:5-14).

Joab: a Hebrew name meaning "Jehovah is Father," the firstborn of the sons of Zeruiah, David's sister, and the commander of his army. He was a skilled strategist and a brave warrior, who helped in reconciling David with his son Absalom. But he was a stubborn avenger, who carried out David's plan to kill Uriah the Hittite, and also killed Absalom in spite of David's orders not to kill him, and conspired with Adonijah against David and Solomon. He avenged the killing of his brother, and killed Abner.

Asahel: a Hebrew name meaning "God has made," the son of Zeruiah (David's sister) and brother of Joab and Abishai. He was famous for speed, for he was light of foot like a wild gazelle. He was one of the heroes in David's army. He took part in the battle of Gibeon, where he pursued his enemy Abner and wanted to kill him, but it was Abner who killed him, and that was before David took the kingship (1 Chr 2:16).
And Abigail bare Amasa: and the father of Amasa was Jether the Ishmeelite. [17]
Amasa: a Hebrew name, a shortening of the name Amasai, the son of Jether the Ishmaelite and Abigail the sister of David and the cousin of Joab (1 Chr 2:17).

Jether the Ishmaelite[14]: Jether is a Hebrew name meaning "excellence." In (2 Sam 17:25) he is "Ithra an Israelite," and in the Septuagint "Ithra the Jezreelite." Was he an Israelite or an Ishmaelite? The Talmud presents two opinions to us:
The first: R. Samuel bar-Nachmani proclaimed that Jether was an Ishmaelite by birth, and entered the Jewish faith, so he became an Israelite as a proselyte.

The second: that Jether the father of Amasa was an Israelite, and was called Jether the Ishmaelite because he lived in the land of Ishmael. This is like Obed-edom, who was called the Gittite (2 Sam 6:11).

David Kimchi offers the suggestion that the Israelites in the land of Ishmael used to call Jether the Israelite because of his nationality, while in Israel they used to call him the Ishmaelite because of his residence in the land of Ishmael.

18 And Caleb the son of Hezron begat children of Azubah his wife, and of Jerioth: her sons are these; Jesher, and Shobab, and Ardon. 19 And when Azubah was dead, Caleb took unto him Ephrath, which bare him Hur. 20 And Hur begat Uri, and Uri begat Bezaleel. 21 And afterward Hezron went in to the daughter of Machir the father of Gilead, whom he married when he was threescore years old; and she bare him Segub. 22 And Segub begat Jair, who had three and twenty cities in the land of Gilead. 23 And he took Geshur, and Aram, with the towns of Jair, from them, with Kenath, and the towns thereof, even threescore cities. All these belonged to the sons of Machir the father of Gilead. 24 And after that Hezron was dead in Caleb-ephratah, then Abiah Hezron's wife bare him Ashur the father of Tekoa.
And Caleb the son of Hezron begat children of Azubah his wife, and of Jerioth:
her sons are these; Jesher, and Shobab, and Ardon. [18]

Caleb the son of Hezron [18], who is Chelubai in [9], is different from Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenezite, the famous companion of Joshua the son of Nun, one of the twelve spies whom Moses sent to spy out the land of Canaan (Num 13:6; Josh 14:6-7). He was among those close to Hur, the companion of Aaron, and Bezaleel his grandson is one of the skilled craftsmen. Some think that each of them had a daughter named Achsah.

Azubah: a Hebrew name meaning "forsaken, abandoned," and she was the wife of Caleb the son of Hezron (1 Chr 2:18-19). Caleb had other women besides her. The sons mentioned here are by her, and not by Jerioth (a Hebrew name meaning "upright"), his concubine.
Ardon: a Hebrew name meaning "humpbacked," the name of a son of Caleb the son of Hezron of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 2:18).
And when Azubah was dead, Caleb took unto him Ephrath, which bare him Hur. [19]
Hur: different from Hur who was also his contemporary, who accompanied Aaron, and the two supported the hands of Moses (Ex 17:10, 12; 24:14).
And Hur begat Uri, and Uri begat Bezaleel. [20]

Uri: a Hebrew name, a shortening of Uriah, a man of the tribe of Judah, and he is the father of Bezaleel, who was among those who worked in building the tabernacle of the congregation and in inlaying it.

Bezaleel: a Hebrew name meaning "in the shadow of God," famous for his skill, and he did the work of the tabernacle of the congregation. The Lord said to Moses: "See, I have called by name Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah: and I have filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship" (Ex 31:2-3).
And afterward Hezron went in to the daughter of Machir the father of Gilead, whom he married when he was threescore years old; and she bare him Segub. [21]

The daughter of Machir the father of Gilead [21] is Abiah [24]. The Gileadites were the greatest clan of the tribe of Manasseh, and in (Num 32:41) Jair is called the son of Manasseh, that is, he descended from Manasseh through his mother, and from Judah through his father.
Segub: a Hebrew name meaning "exalted." Of the offspring of Judah, he is a son of Hezron, whom the daughter of Machir bore, and Segub begat Jair, who had twenty-three cities in the land of Gilead.
And Segub begat Jair, who had three and twenty cities in the land of Gilead. [22]
Jair: a Hebrew name meaning "he enlightens." He was one of the victors after crossing the Jordan.

The twenty-three cities here are in Lejah (Argob), which is in the region east of the Jordan; some think they are a part of the sixty cities mentioned in [23], and others think they are different from the sixty cities.
And he took Geshur, and Aram, with the towns of Jair, from them, with Kenath, and the towns thereof, even threescore cities.
All these belonged to the sons of Machir the father of Gilead. [23]
The sixty cities here perhaps include the twenty-three cities [22], with 27 cities added to them in Kenath (Num 32:42).
Geshur: a Hebrew name meaning "bridge." It is a district lying between Hermon and Bashan, bordering on Argob (1 Chr 2:23), and it lies east of Maachah within the portion of Manasseh.
He took Geshur and Aram: that is, Jair took the cities of the Geshurites and the Arameans, which became Havoth-jair, that is, the cities of Jair (Deut 3:14).
Aram Havoth: "Aram," which is pronounced "Aramu" in Akkadian, perhaps meant "the high land."
Kenath: it is present-day Qanawat in Hauran.
Machir the father of Gilead: a Hebrew name meaning "purchased." He is the father of Gilead, and his son's name was Abiah (1 Chr 2:21, 24).
And after that Hezron was dead in Caleb-ephratah, then Abiah Hezron's wife bare him Ashur the father of Tekoa. [24]

Ashur the father of Tekoa: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "blackness." He was the son of Hezron of the tribe of Judah, and his mother's name was Abiah (1 Chr 2:24). He is called "the father of Tekoa," and perhaps the inhabitants of his town Tekoa were of his descendants.
The expression [father of Tekoa] means the builder of Tekoa, which lies in the south of Judah (2 Sam 14:2, 4, 9).

25 And the sons of Jerahmeel the firstborn of Hezron were, Ram the firstborn, and Bunah, and Oren, and Ozem, and Ahijah. 26 Jerahmeel had also another wife, whose name was Atarah; she was the mother of Onam. 27 And the sons of Ram the firstborn of Jerahmeel were, Maaz, and Jamin, and Eker. 28 And the sons of Onam were, Shammai, and Jada. And the sons of Shammai; Nadab, and Abishur. 29 And the name of the wife of Abishur was Abihail, and she bare him Ahban, and Molid. 30 And the sons of Nadab; Seled, and Appaim: but Seled died without children. 31 And the sons of Appaim; Ishi. And the sons of Ishi; Sheshan. And the children of Sheshan; Ahlai. 32 And the sons of Jada the brother of Shammai; Jether, and Jonathan: and Jether died without children. 33 And the sons of Jonathan; Peleth, and Zaza. These were the sons of Jerahmeel. 34 Now Sheshan had no sons, but daughters. And Sheshan had a servant, an Egyptian, whose name was Jarha. 35 And Sheshan gave his daughter to Jarha his servant to wife; and she bare him Attai. 36 And Attai begat Nathan, and Nathan begat Zabad, 37 And Zabad begat Ephlal, and Ephlal begat Obed, 38 And Obed begat Jehu, and Jehu begat Azariah, 39 And Azariah begat Helez, and Helez begat Eleasah, 40 And Eleasah begat Sisamai, and Sisamai begat Shallum, 41 And Shallum begat Jekamiah, and Jekamiah begat Elishama.
And the sons of Jerahmeel the firstborn of Hezron were,
Ram the firstborn, and Bunah, and Oren, and Ozem, and Ahijah. [25]
The sons of Jerahmeel occupied the region of the Negev, which is a desert region south of Judah.
Bunah: a Hebrew name meaning "intelligence." He was a man of the descendants of Judah (1 Chr 2:25).
Orna or Oren: a Hebrew name meaning "laurel tree," or perhaps "camphor tree." This tree is known in Latin as Laurus nobilis, and it was the name of the sons of Jerahmeel of the tribe of Judah.

Ozem: a Hebrew name whose meaning may be "angry." More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. The name of a son of Jesse and brother of David, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 2:15). 2. The name of a son of Jerahmeel, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 2:25).
Ahijah: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "my brother."
Jerahmeel had also another wife, whose name was Atarah; she was the mother of Onam. [26]
Atarah: a Hebrew name meaning "crown."
And the sons of Ram the firstborn of Jerahmeel were, Maaz, and Jamin, and Eker. [27]
Maaz: a Hebrew name meaning "wrath." He was the son of Ram, of the descendants of Judah (1 Chr 2:27).
Jamin: a Hebrew name meaning "right hand of success." He was a man of Judah, of the house of Jerahmeel.
Eker: a Hebrew name meaning "uprooting." He was the son of Ram the son of Jerahmeel (1 Chr 2:27).
And the sons of Onam were, Shammai, and Jada.
And the sons of Shammai; Nadab, and Abishur. [28]
Shammai or Shumathi: one of the clans of the village of Kirjath-jearim (1 Chr 2:53).
Jada: a Hebrew name meaning "one who knows." He was the son of Onam, of the descendants of Judah, and his family was Hezron, of the house of Jerahmeel (1 Chr 2:28, 32).
Nadab: a Hebrew name meaning "generous." It is the name of a son of Shammai of Judah, of the sons of Jerahmeel the son of Hezron.
Abishur: a Hebrew name meaning "father of a wall or fortress." He was a man of Judah, of the clan of Hezron, of the house of Jerahmeel (1 Chr 2:28-29).
And the name of the wife of Abishur was Abihail, and she bare him Ahban, and Molid. [29]
Abihail: a Hebrew name meaning "father of joy." She was the mother of Amasa (1 Chr 2:17).
Ahban: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "the brother is wise or intelligent." He was the son of Abishur of the tribe of Judah.
Molid: a Hebrew name meaning "begotten." He was of the descendants of Judah (1 Chr 2:29).
And the sons of Nadab; Seled, and Appaim:
but Seled died without children. [30]
Seled: a Hebrew name meaning "exultation." He was one of the sons of Judah, the son of Nadab, and he died without leaving offspring (1 Chr 2:30).
And the sons of Appaim; Ishi. And the sons of Ishi; Sheshan. And the children of Sheshan; Ahlai. [31]

Sheshan: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "one who whitens." He was one of the descendants of Judah, of the clan of Hezron, of the house of Jerahmeel (1 Chr 2:31, 34, 35). He had no sons but daughters, and he gave his daughter in marriage to his Egyptian servant Jarha.
Ahlai: a Hebrew name that meant "Oh, if only!" The name of a person of the descendants of Sheshan appears (see 1 Chr 2:31, 34).
And the sons of Jada the brother of Shammai; Jether, and Jonathan:
and Jether died without children. [32]
Jonathan: the son of Jada, of the descendants of Jerahmeel, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 2:32-33). It is a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh gave."
Jether: a Hebrew name meaning "excellence." He was a man of the descendants of Judah, from Jerahmeel. He died without an heir (1 Chr 2:32).
And the sons of Jonathan; Peleth, and Zaza. These were the sons of Jerahmeel. [33]
Peleth or Pelet: a Hebrew name meaning "swift." It is the name of a man of Judah, of the descendants of Jerahmeel the firstborn of Hezron (1 Chr 2:33).
Zaza: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "movement." He was the son of Jonathan, and he was of the descendants of Judah (1 Chr 2:33).
Now Sheshan had no sons, but daughters.
And Sheshan had a servant, an Egyptian, whose name was Jarha, [34]
"Sheshan had no sons," whereas it is mentioned in [31] that the son of Sheshan was Ahlai. Perhaps Ahlai died without offspring before his father gave his daughter to Jarha his servant.

Some see that the reference to his giving his only daughter in marriage to an Egyptian servant, as a commendation of him, only reveals that this servant had accepted faith in the living God, and that he was marked by wisdom and virtue. It is as though his Egyptian (pagan) origin and his servitude did not make him lose his dignity, and were no obstacle to his eminence.
And Sheshan gave his daughter to Jarha his servant to wife; and she bare him Attai. [35]

According to the Mosaic Law, Hebrew women were not permitted to marry from outside the tribe to which they belonged, so that the inheritance might be kept within the tribe. Thus what Sheshan did appears to be contrary to the Law [36].

Harmer mentions that although this conduct appears contrary to the Law, it was the custom of the East that a person might be compelled to give one of his daughters in marriage to one of his servants, so that he might receive the inheritance, indeed even if he held a great position[15].
Attai: a Hebrew name meaning "suitable." He was the son of the daughter of Sheshan (of the sons of Judah), whom her father gave in marriage to his servant of Egyptian origin (1 Chr 2:34-36).
And Attai begat Nathan, and Nathan begat Zabad [36]

Nathan: a Hebrew name meaning "God has given." It is the name of the son of Attai and father of Zabad, of the family of Jerahmeel the son of Hezron, of the sons of Judah (1 Chr 2:36), and he was of the descendants of Caleb.
Zabad: a Hebrew name meaning "God has bestowed," or "gift." He was a son of Nathan the son of Attai.
And Zabad begat Ephlal, and Ephlal begat Obed [37]
Ephlal: a Hebrew word meaning "discerning." It is the name of the son of Zabad of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 2:37).

Obed: a Hebrew name meaning "servant." More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. The son of Ruth and Boaz, who was the father of Jesse the father of David (1 Chr 2:12). 2. The son of Ephlal, of the descendants of Sheshan, of the sons of Judah (1 Chr 2:37).
And Obed begat Jehu, and Jehu begat Azariah [38]
Jehu: a Hebrew name meaning "He is Yahweh." He was a man of the lineage of Judah, of the family of Jerahmeel (1 Chr 2:38).

Azariah: a Hebrew name meaning "whom Yahweh helped." More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. The son of Ethan, of the sons of Zerah, of the sons of Judah (1 Chr 2:8). 2. The son of Jehu the son of Obed, of the sons of Jerahmeel (1 Chr 2:38-39).
And Azariah begat Helez, and Helez begat Eleasah [39]
Helez: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "strength," or "(God) has saved; saved." He was a man of the sons of Judah, of the descendants of Hezron (1 Chr 2:39).
Eleasah: a Hebrew name meaning "God has made." It is the name of a man of the descendants of Judah and of the descendants of Jerahmeel (1 Chr 2:39).
And Eleasah begat Sisamai, and Sisamai begat Shallum [40]
Sisamai: a man of the tribe of Judah, of the family of Hezron, of the house of Jerahmeel (1 Chr 2:40).
Shallum: a Hebrew name meaning "recompense." He was a man of Judah (1 Chr 2:40-41).
And Shallum begat Jekamiah, and Jekamiah begat Elishama. [41]
Jekamiah: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh rises up." He was a man of Judah, of the royal line.
Elishama: a Hebrew name meaning "God has heard." He was the son of Jekamiah, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 2:41).

42 Now the sons of Caleb the brother of Jerahmeel were, Mesha his firstborn, which was the father of Ziph; and the sons of Mareshah the father of Hebron. 43 And the sons of Hebron; Korah, and Tappuah, and Rekem, and Shema. 44 And Shema begat Raham, the father of Jorkoam: and Rekem begat Shammai. 45 And the son of Shammai was Maon: and Maon was the father of Bethzur. 46 And Ephah, Caleb's concubine, bare Haran, and Moza, and Gazez: and Haran begat Gazez. 47 And the sons of Jahdai; Regem, and Jotham, and Gesham, and Pelet, and Ephah, and Shaaph. 48 Maachah, Caleb's concubine, bare Sheber, and Tirhanah. 49 She bare also Shaaph the father of Madmannah, Sheva the father of Machbenah, and the father of Gibea: and the daughter of Caleb was Achsa. 50 These were the sons of Caleb the son of Hur, the firstborn of Ephratah; Shobal the father of Kirjath-jearim, 51 Salma the father of Bethlehem, Hareph the father of Bethgader. 52 And Shobal the father of Kirjath-jearim had sons; Haroeh, and Hazi-hammenuchoth. 53 And the families of Kirjath-jearim; the Ithrites, and the Puhites, and the Shumathites, and the Mishraites; of them came the Zareathites, and the Eshtaulites. 54 The sons of Salma; Bethlehem, and the Netophathites, Ataroth, the house of Joab, and half of the Manahethites, the Zorites. 55 And the families of the scribes which dwelt at Jabez; the Tirathites, the Shimeathites, and Suchathites. These are the Kenites that came of Hemath, the father of the house of Rechab.
Now the sons of Caleb the brother of Jerahmeel were, Mesha his firstborn, which was the father of Ziph;
and the sons of Mareshah the father of Hebron. [42]

The sons of Caleb [42]: he is the same Caleb mentioned in vv. 18-19. Here his descendants are given in more detail; perhaps they are his children by Jerioth his concubine, whom he had not mentioned previously.
Mesha: a Hebrew name meaning "salvation." He was a son of Caleb (1 Chr 2:42).
Mareshah: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "place of the head and the summit." It is the name of the father of Hebron (1 Chr 2:42), and he was of the offspring of Caleb.
And the sons of Hebron; Korah, and Tappuah, and Rekem, and Shema. [43]
Korah: a Hebrew name meaning "baldness." It is the name of a son of Hebron, of the descendants of Judah (1 Chr 2:43).
Tappuah: a Hebrew name meaning "apple." It is the name of a son of Hebron (1 Chr 2:43), of the descendants of Judah.
Rekem: a Hebrew name meaning "variegation, forming, coloring." A man of the descendants of Judah, from among the sons of Hebron.
Shema: a Hebrew name meaning "report." He is a son of Hebron of the tribe of Judah.
And Shema begat Raham, the father of Jorkoam: and Rekem begat Shammai. [44]

Jorkoam: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "he enlarges the people." It is a village in the portion of Judah (1 Chr 2:44). Perhaps it was the village of Raka near Ziph, and some thought it the same as Jokdeam.

Shammai: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh Jesus." More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. The son of Onam, of the family of Jerahmeel, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 2:28). 2. The son of Rekem, of the house of Caleb, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 2:44).
And the son of Shammai was Maon: and Maon was the father of Bethzur. [45]
Maon: a Semitic name meaning "dwelling." It is the name of a son of Shammai of the tribe of Judah, and the founder of Bethzur.
And Ephah, Caleb's concubine, bare Haran, and Moza, and Gazez:
and Haran begat Gazez. [46]

Ephah: a Hebrew name meaning "darkness." More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. The concubine of Caleb, who bore Haran, Moza and Gazez (1 Chr 2:46). 2. The son of Jahdai, of the family of Caleb, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 2:46).
Haran: a name perhaps of Akkadian origin, meaning "road, caravan." It is the name of a son of Caleb and Ephah, of the family of Hezron (1 Chr 2:46).
Moza: a Hebrew name meaning "going out." It is the name of the second son of Caleb by his concubine Ephah (1 Chr 2:46).
Gazez: a Hebrew name meaning "shearing."
And the sons of Jahdai; Regem, and Jotham, and Gesham, and Pelet, and Ephah, and Shaaph. [47]
Jahdai: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh guides." He was a head of a people from the descendants of Judah, mentioned with the descendants of Caleb (1 Chr 2:47).
Regem: a Hebrew name meaning "friend." He was a son of Jahdai, of the descendants of Judah (1 Chr 2:47).
Jotham: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh is perfect," or "Yahweh is complete." It is the name of a man of the descendants of Judah (1 Chr 2:47).
Gesham: a Hebrew name meaning "filthy." A man of Judah, a son of Jahdai (1 Chr 2:47).
Pelet: a Hebrew name meaning "God has set free." He was one of the sons of Jahdai the Calebite, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 2:47).
Shaaph: an Aramaic word meaning "balsam." More than one person bears this name, among them:
One of the sons of Jahdai, of the sons of Caleb, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 2:47).
A son of Caleb by his maidservant Maachah, from whom came the inhabitants of Madmannah (1 Chr 2:49-50).
Maachah, Caleb's concubine, bare Sheber, and Tirhanah. [48]
Sheber: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "lion." He was a son of Caleb by Maachah his concubine (1 Chr 2:48).
Tirhanah: a Hebrew name meaning "favors." He was a son of Caleb the son of Hezron, and he is the brother of Berahiel by Maachah his concubine.
She bare also Shaaph the father of Madmannah, Sheva the father of Machbenah, and the father of Gibea:
and the daughter of Caleb was Achsa. [49]
Madmannah: a Hebrew name meaning "dunghill."

Sheva: a Hebrew name meaning "hero," or perhaps it is close to the Arabic word "sawa'" ("equal"), in which case its meaning would be "like." He was the son of Hezron, of the house of Caleb, of the tribe of Judah. From his descendants came the Machbenites and the Gibeites (1 Chr 2:49).
Machbenah: the name of a city that is not known, whose location is in the portion of Judah; it was founded by Sheva (1 Chr 2:49).
Gibea: a Hebrew name meaning "hill." He was one of the descendants of Caleb (1 Chr 2:49).
Achsa: a Hebrew name meaning "anklet." She was the daughter of Caleb the son of Hezron (see 1 Chr 2:18).
These were the sons of Caleb the son of Hur, the firstborn of Ephratah;
Shobal the father of Kirjath-jearim, [50]
Caleb the son of Hur: some see that this Caleb is a third Caleb. The first is the son of Hezron [18], and the second is the son of Jephunneh.
Ephratah: a different form of the name of Caleb's wife Ephrath [19].
And Salma the father of Bethlehem, and Hareph the father of Bethgader. [51]

The writer was concerned with the descendants of Caleb because of the importance of Bethlehem, the place of the birth of the Lord Christ. Salma, one of the line of Caleb, is the founder, or father, of Bethlehem.
Salma: a Hebrew name meaning "clothed." He was the son of Hur, of the descendants of Caleb, and the father of Bethlehem, and some think that he is Salmon (1 Chr 2:51).
Hareph: a Hebrew name meaning "autumn, autumnal, harvest." A man of the sons of Caleb.
And Shobal the father of Kirjath-jearim had sons;
Haroeh, and Hazi-hammenuchoth. [52]
Shobal: the son of Hur, of the house of Caleb, of the tribe of Judah, of the family of Hezron. From his descendants came the inhabitants of Kirjath-jearim (1 Chr 2:50, 52).
Haroeh: a Hebrew name meaning "the seer." He was one of the sons of Shobal the son of Caleb, the father of Kirjath-jearim.
Hazi-hammenuchoth: a Hebrew name meaning "place of rest." It was a village inhabited by a son of Shobal, one of the descendants of Caleb (1 Chr 2:52).
And the families of Kirjath-jearim;
the Ithrites, and the Puhites, and the Shumathites, and the Mishraites;
of them came the Zareathites, and the Eshtaulites. [53]
The Ithrites were a family that dwelt in Kirjath-jearim, while the Puhites, the Shumathites and the Mishraites were clans in the village.
The Zareathites: from the Zareathites (1 Chr 2:53-54; 4:2), the people of Zorah.
The Eshtaulites: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "the question."
The Zareathites and the Eshtaulites were in the south of Judah, on the border of the Philistines, and they are mentioned in the account of Samson (Judg 13:25).
The sons of Salma; Bethlehem, and the Netophathites, Ataroth, the house of Joab, and half of the Manahethites, the Zorites. [54]
The Netophathites: Netophah is a Hebrew name meaning "blistered," and it is a town in Judah near Bethlehem.
Ataroth: a town in Judea (1 Chr 2:54), near Bethlehem.
And the families of the scribes which dwelt at Jabez; the Tirathites, the Shimeathites, and Suchathites.
These are the Kenites that came of Hemath, the father of the house of Rechab. [55]

Some see that the author of the book was one of the scribes, and therefore he was concerned with the clans and genealogies of the scribes, such as those who dwelt at Jabez, since they are linked with the place of their dwelling because they are not known. They are Kenites who joined Israel through the marriage of Moses to a Kenite woman. They are sometimes referred to as Midianites (Judg 4:11).
The clans of the scribes: these are distinct from the company of the scribes who were of the Levites. It appears that writing was the craft of some clans, which the fathers handed down to the sons.
The Tirathites: one of the three clans of the Levite scribes, of the Kenites who dwelt at Jabez.
The Shimeathites: a family of scribes (1 Chr 2:55).
The Suchathites: a family of scribes, who dwelt in a place unknown to us today, named Jabez.
Hemath: a Hebrew name meaning "hot spring." He was the founder of the house of Rechab, a family of the Kenites.

The Kenites: they were not originally of Judah, but were among those whose land was given to the children of Israel (Gen 15:19), yet they united with Judah through friendship and marriage. The account of the Kenite scribes came within the genealogy of Judah. They are also linked with Rechab, the founder of the line of Israelites who were concerned with obedience to their fathers (Jer 35:1-9).
Hobab, the father-in-law of Moses or his relative by marriage, was with the children of Israel in their journey, and he settled in the south of Judah.
Also Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite killed Sisera, the commander of the army of Jabin king of Canaan, when he fought against Israel in the days of the Judges (Judg 4:7).
The house of Rechab: they are mentioned in (2 Kgs 10:15; Jer 35).
A pleasant journey with Judah and his brothers
v Grant me, with my father Jacob, to set out in flight!
Where shall I go, for my father and my mother cannot protect me.
Let Esau spew out all his venom; it will not harm me as long as I am in Your embrace.
I set out with Jacob on the road, as one who has been stripped of everything!
But You are the Way; I walk in You, and the gates of heaven are opened to me.
I do not need a pillow on which my head may rest.
I place a stone under my head with Jacob.
You are the Rock, who supports my head and sanctifies my thoughts.
I do not need a ladder by which to reach heaven, for Your cross carries me to the bosom of Your Father.
v You opened the gates of heaven to my father Jacob.
So he saw the angels ascending and descending.
By Your Holy Spirit You have established Your Kingdom within me, and so heaven has become in my depths.
The angels rejoice in Your Kingdom which You establish in me.
And I rejoice in the heavenly orders who rejoice in my salvation!
v How the soul of my father Jacob rejoiced, as he heard Your voice saying:
In thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed.
For I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken to thee of (Gen 28:14-15).
And I also, my depths rejoice in Your true promises to me.
"Behold, the kingdom of God is within you" (Lk 17:21).
Let me rejoice in Your Kingdom, which embraces the Gentiles and the peoples.
In You my heart is greatly enlarged, if it be possible, for all humanity.
I see You within me, embracing with love all the sons of men.
v You gave my father Jacob twelve sons, who establish tribes with one rejoicing heart (1 Chr 12:38-40).
Allow me to cleave to those who cleaved to You!
No tribe is without weaknesses, but Your grace has lifted all to You.
v The tribe of Reuben the firstborn: on its list is Reuben himself.
He fell into fornication with his father's concubine; he declined, for he defiled his father's bed.
He lost the birthright and the blessing, and destroyed himself by himself!
Your grace allowed him to be disciplined, yet from his sons there were found mighty men of valor, who cleaved to David the king and worked with him!
v Benjamin declined until he almost perished.
There were found among them wicked men who were called the sons of Belial (Judg 19:22).
They wrought an abomination such as had not been seen since the children of Israel came up out of Egypt (Judg 19:30).
Benjamin almost perished at the hands of all the tribes (Judg 20:21).
From Benjamin also appeared Saul, the first king of Israel.
He betrayed the Lord his God, and sought spirits instead of the Lord.
You were merciful, O Lord, to the tribe, and mighty men of valor were found among them.
They left their brother Saul the wicked, and cleaved to David wherever he was found.
And the tribe remained faithful to the tribe of Judah to the end.
There were found in the tribe of Benjamin those more faithful than Absalom the son of David!
Your grace raises up the fallen, and lifts up the contrite in heart.
Join me to Yourself, O Son of David, that I may cleave to You and never part from You!

Grant me to be faithful with You and to You, who are faithful forever, so that it does not concern me to belong to some tribe, for in the waters of Baptism You gave me the Spirit of adoption to the Father!
v If You count me a son of righteous Joseph the son of Jacob, grant me a portion with Ephraim or Manasseh!
Many faithful ones from the two tribes cleaved to David.
Do not deprive me of being among the heirs of God, heirs with You, through You and for You, for You are our eternal inheritance and our portion that does not pass away!
v I do not presume to count myself of the tribe of Judah or the tribe of Levi!
You have made me a king with authority, treading on serpents and scorpions and all the power of the enemy.
I defy the devil, sin and death!
For You are the Holy One and the Resurrection, the Giver of victory!
You have made me a priest to God Your Father in the waters of Baptism, accepting every word of thanksgiving or praise as an acceptable sacrifice before You.
v I do not enumerate all the tribes in order to belong to one of them, for You have made me a member of Your body, O Holy One.
You have become to me righteousness and sanctification and redemption! (1 Cor 1:30)
v You are wonderful, O Lord, in Your kindness and tenderness!
Many Hebrew women desired to bear children, that they might have the blessing of Your Incarnation from their seed.
Tamar the Canaanite was bitter of soul because she was childless.
Her husband Er the son of Judah died, and she bore no son.
She married his brother Onan, that she might bear a son for the dead.
She heard of Your Incarnation through the shadow, and longed that the blessing of Your Incarnation might come from her seed.
Her father-in-law Judah kept her from marrying the third son Shelah, for he thought that Tamar was the cause of the death of his two sons Er and Onan.
By a ruse she took on the likeness of shame, and assumed the position of a harlot.
She lay with her father-in-law, and he did not know who she was.
She conceived and bore, and obtained the desire of her heart.
The Canaanite woman surpassed many of the believing Hebrew women.
She bore two children who represent the Gentiles who were able to believe in the Messiah.
She bore Zerah, who lost the birthright, representing the Jews who refuse to believe in the Savior.
And she bore Perez, who seized the birthright while in his mother's womb, and became a representative of the Gentiles who accepted faith in the Savior of the world.
Kindle my heart with longing and fill it with hope, that I may be at Your right hand.
Your voice resounds in my depths: Come to Me, you blessed of My Father!
v Do I have the heart of Boaz, the simple one and servant of the needy?
He did not despise Ruth because she was a Moabitess, nor because she was poor.
He cared for her and for her mother-in-law, and received exceeding honor.
He became the grandfather of David, great among the prophets and kings.
Grant me a heart that loves every needy one.
Then You will satisfy my need, and bestow on me fellowship in Your glories!

entries.section: 1. The descendants of David in Hebron

paragraphs.text: 1 Now these were the sons of David, which were born unto him in Hebron; the firstborn Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess; the second Daniel, of Abigail the Carmelitess: 2 The third, Absalom the son of Maachah the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur: the fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith: 3 The fifth, Shephatiah of Abital: the sixth, Ithream by Eglah his wife. 4 These six were born unto him in Hebron; and there he reigned seven years and six months: and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty and three years.
Now these were the sons of David, which were born unto him in Hebron;
the firstborn Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess;
the second Daniel, of Abigail the Carmelitess: [1]

In speaking of the descendants of David, he began with the firstborn Amnon [1] and ended with Tamar [9]. Amnon was the firstborn according to the flesh, and he was the shame of his father's house, so it was necessary to set him aside.

All the sons of David who were born before the full establishment of the monarchy are under a general judgment, such as Amnon and Absalom, because of corruption, rebellion and pride. These fell under judgment. The monarchy had to reach Jerusalem specifically, and the choice was according to grace (Ps 132:13).

entries.section: 1. The descendants of David in Hebron

paragraphs.text: Shimea, Shobab and Nathan are mentioned as the sons of Bathsheba, but they disappear so that Solomon, the youngest son, may come. Moreover, all the other sons who came after him had no right to the kingship[2].
In the Septuagint the list of the royal tribe was extended to about the year 250 B.C., which is the time of the translation itself.

The text points to the names of the mothers of six sons of David, who were born in Hebron before the transfer of his capital to Jerusalem (993 B.C.). Here the descendants of David begin with his sons in Hebron.
Hebron: an important city, and the name Hebron was also given to many people. A small city was also found with this name, though in a changed form in Hebrew.
This city is 18 miles south of Jerusalem, and the same distance north of Beersheba, and it still exists today.
Why do the descendants of David begin here with his sons in Hebron?

a. Since the two books of Chronicles focus on the joyful Kingdom of God, which is realized by the salvation that the Son of David offers, the First Book of Chronicles presented the person of David and his holy sons as types of the Lord Christ. So we are not surprised that the book does not refer to the glorious events in the life of David from his youth, when the Lord chose him to be king while he was still tending his father's sheep, and that was in secret, in the house of his father Jesse. The book also ignored the troubles that pursued David, especially from King Saul; what concerned it was the setting up of David as king over all the tribes in Hebron, to make him king over Israel.

"Hebron" is a Hebrew name meaning company, fellowship, bond, union, conjunction or marriage. What the book wishes to present as the starting point of the kingdom of Israel under the leadership of King David is that, as a representative of the Lord Christ, the King of kings, all the believers should be one holy company, bound by love and holiness, in constant fellowship together in Christ Jesus. We shall see later, especially in chapter 12, that "there was joy in Israel" (1 Chr 12:40), the secret of which was the cleaving of all the tribes, even the tribe of Benjamin, from which came King Saul, the opponent of David; it cleaved to him and to Judah even after the division of the kingdom, for Benjamin did not depart from Judah.
The kingdom of the Lord Christ rests on love, unity and fellowship; therefore it is fitting for the believer, in order to enjoy the divine Kingdom, that his heart open in love to all humanity.
The name "Hebron," then, offers us a practical indication of the true way to the heavenly royal wedding.

entries.section: 1. The descendants of David in Hebron

paragraphs.text: v The souls of all men and women are known to be brides of Christ, if they wish to keep bodily chastity and virginity of heart. Let them understand that Christ is the Bridegroom of their souls, not of their bodies[3].

Father Caesarius, Bishop of Arles b. Hebron took its fame because of famous events that took place in the days of the patriarchs. For example, when Sarah died in Hebron her husband Abraham bought the field of Ephron the Hittite which is in Machpelah, and buried her in a cave in the field, and it became a tomb for the family (Gen 23:19-20), and the cave still exists. A city was established in the valley, and Abraham, Isaac and Jacob each spent long periods in the region, and the three were buried in Hebron. If Hebron is the place of death and tombs, then there is need of a king who raises from the dead and challenges death.

It is as though the Son of David proclaims His glory by raising those who sleep in the graves of sins, that they may experience the pledge of eternity and accept the Son of David as the Door and the Way and the Life and the Resurrection and the Crown and the Treasure and the source of heavenly joy.

entries.section: 1. The descendants of David in Hebron

paragraphs.text: v He tasted death for all. And though by nature He Himself is Life, and is the Resurrection, He surrounded His body with death. And by His mighty power He trod down death in His body, to become the firstborn from the dead, and the firstborn of those who have fallen asleep... If the resurrection from the dead is said to come about through a man, and the man whom we know through it is the Word begotten of God, through Him the power of death was broken[4].
