St. Cyril the Great c. From Hebron Joseph, rejected by his brothers, set out to seek his brothers (Gen 37:14); thus he was a type of the Lord Christ, who, being the Lord of all, did not disdain to become a firstborn brother to humanity, taking what is theirs (their humanity) and giving them what is His, partakers of the divine nature (2 Pet 1:4).

entries.section: 1. The descendants of David in Hebron

paragraphs.text: v When Paul calls the Corinthian Christians his brothers, he lays down a foundation of greater assurance. For we became brothers through the work of Christ in His earthly life and death. Above all this, what is the Gospel but the message that God became man, was crucified and rose? This the angel Gabriel proclaimed to the Virgin Mary (Lk 1:26-38), and it is what the prophets preached to the world, and what the Apostles proclaimed in truth[5].

St. John Chrysostom d. Hebron became a city of refuge (Josh 20:7), protecting the one who killed by mistake from the avenger of blood, so that he does not lay a hand on him until the high priest dies, and he lives in complete freedom, no one taking vengeance on him. It is as though Hebron points to the cross of the Lord Christ.

It is stated in the law of the cities of refuge that one who has killed unintentionally must flee quickly to the nearest city of refuge. Then he presents his case before the elders of the city, and they receive him among them if they see that he has confessed that he killed and have verified that the killing was done unintentionally, and not deliberately or with the intent to harm him. Then he returns to the city of refuge and stays within its walls, and the avenger, that is, the nearest kinsman of the slain, has no right to take vengeance for the blood of the slain. He remains so until the high priest dies, and then he has the right to leave the city, and the avenger has no right to approach him.

The death of the high priest points to the death of the Lord Christ, by whom we were released from the wages of sin, and who granted us complete freedom in Him. Since the city of refuge pointed to the Lord Christ, the repentant person remained safe as long as he was inside the Lord, but if he fled from Him he would be exposed to death.
v Tell me, let us see: when the high priest died, why did all the prisoners return to their borders?

entries.section: 1. The descendants of David in Hebron

paragraphs.text: This is the mystery of the High Priest who died on Golgotha, and by Him the two who went out of Eden returned, for they had been banished[6].

St. Mar Jacob of Sarug e. Hebron is the dwelling place of the priests, the sons of Aaron, until our Lord Jesus Christ, the heavenly High Priest after the order of Melchizedek (Ps 110:4), comes, who offered no animals, but offered His heart and conscience, as He offered bread and wine as a type of what the Lord of glory Jesus offers, turning the bread and wine into His Body and Blood which are given for us.
v When David clearly knew these (priests) in his prophecy, he did not liken any one of them to the Son.
He saw that all of them bring sacrifices that are not their own and are external to them, to offer them to God.
And he looked forward to the fact that Christ, when He willed and set out to become a priest, offered to His Father nothing external to Himself.
For King David looked at all the priests, who resembles the Son of God and who does not resemble Him.
He found that Melchizedek was made a priest without sacrifices, and did not pour out the blood of animals before God.
He did not bring the firstborn to the house of offering like Abel, nor offer a burnt offering of clean animals like Noah.
He did not slay (animals of) three years old before the Lord like Abraham (Gen 15:9), nor offer bulls and rams like the Levites.
He did not pour out the blood of turtledoves and young pigeons, nor make bulls and calves an offering (Ex 24; Lev 21:8; Lk 2:24).
But he stood before God with a pure heart and clean thoughts that rise above sacrifices.
He thought within himself to be pure like the offering, and to slay his mind, not animals, before God.
And to make no burnt offering to the Lord but himself, and for the pure conscience to be a sacrifice without stench.
(He said): I do not bring flesh to offer to the Lord, for He does not eat as food the sacrifice that is offered to Him.
It is an insult for animal sacrifices to be made to the Lord; I purify myself, and I slay my thought to God.
By these pure and lofty spiritual movements, the famous Melchizedek became a priest.

entries.section: 1. The descendants of David in Hebron

paragraphs.text: He was made a priest by the sufferings of his soul without sacrifices, and for this he was made like the Son of God[7].

St. Mar Jacob of Sarug f. The city of Hebron was known before Damascus, and its name was Kiriath-arba (Josh 14:15; 15:3; 21:11; Judg 1:10). It is stated in Joshua chapter 14 that Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenezite demanded his right, which the Lord had promised him by the tongue of Moses, which was to possess the mountain where the fortified cities were, and Hebron, which means "union" or "joining" or "company." Now when Caleb received "Hebron," which is also called "Kiriath-arba," "he drove thence the three sons of Anak, Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai, the children of Anak" (Josh 15:14). If Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenezite, who points to the heart that turned away from contempt and entered into glory, received Hebron as a reward, and thus entered into a holy and spiritual marriage or union, in which the soul is united with its Bridegroom forever, then Hebron on the other hand is called Kiriath-arba. The number 4 points to the world with its four directions: east and west, north and south, and it also points to the body taken from this earth or this world. So the one with a sanctified heart, who has turned to his eternal Bridegroom, reigns over his body, driving out from it the three sons of Anak, that the Lord may reign in it also. It is not enough that our hearts or inner lives be holy, but we must look upon our bodies with a holy look, for as we offer to the Bridegroom our inner hearts, so we offer Him our bodies, and the person works in his entirety in harmonious tone. St. Gregory of Nyssa likens the whole person to a lyre that bears different strings, yet which, by the Holy Spirit, presents a harmonious musical piece that rejoices the heart of God.
It is as though Hebron here, linked with its old name "Kiriath-arba," calls us to be sanctified in all our inner being as in our bodies, for the sake of the Son of David, the King of kings.
In brief we can say that if the two books urge us to come to know Christ the Redeemer and Savior, the bearer of the sins of the world, it emphasizes in particular His kingship.

g. Since Hebron points to union with the Lord Christ, the soul becomes a bride clinging to her Bridegroom, and forgets, with David, all her life with its dangerous deeds, such as the victory over Goliath the giant, and the women welcoming him with songs because he had rescued his country, and the rescuing of Saul from the evil spirit by playing the lyre with praises to the Lord, and Saul's battles against him, and Saul's continual plans to be rid of him. Nothing occupies the believer any longer except his clinging to the King of kings, and so he sees all the tribes coming to him to make him king over Israel. In a spirit of humility the believer looks with David in Hebron, in amazement, at how the Lord draws all mighty energies to work with Him for the sake of the Kingdom of God.

In Hebron David grows in humility, as he realizes that his installation as king is nothing but free divine grace, in which he has no merit, but it is the work of the Lord of Hosts for the glory of His holy name, for the sake of humanity, the object of His surpassing love.
Daniel: meaning "God judges," one of the sons of David by Abigail, who was born in Hebron (1 Chr 3:1). His name came as Chileab in (2 Sam 3:3), and some see that he had two names.

Abigail: her story is recorded in (1 Sam 25-30). A beautiful and virtuous wife, marked beside her beauty by her wisdom, who managed the wealth of her husband Nabal with wisdom. She was a successful counselor to her foolish husband, as also to David, for she prevented him from taking vengeance on Nabal.

She was not preoccupied with her husband's great wealth, nor with what she inherited from him, but gave herself and what she possessed to David, for she realized that he was a man of God. David the psalmist said to her: "Blessed be the LORD God of Israel, which sent thee this day to meet me: And blessed be thy advice, and blessed be thou, which hast kept me this day from coming to shed blood, and from avenging myself with mine own hand" (1 Sam 25:32-33).

entries.section: 1. The descendants of David in Hebron

paragraphs.text: The third, Absalom the son of Maachah the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur:
the fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith: [2]

entries.section: 1. The descendants of David in Hebron

paragraphs.text: The fifth, Shephatiah of Abital:
the sixth, Ithream by Eglah his wife. [3]

Absalom the son of Maachah: nothing is mentioned about him in Chronicles. He was handsome in appearance, with long hair, loved by his father and by the people. When his brother Amnon – from his father, not from his mother – assaulted Tamar his sister, and his father did not punish him, Absalom was greatly enraged, and had Amnon murdered by means of his servants. Absalom fled from the face of his father to King Geshur, the father of his mother (2 Sam 3:3; 13:37), and stayed there for three years, and when he returned to Jerusalem David refused to meet with him.

He used every means to draw the people to himself, and was able to proclaim his rebellion against his father and take over the throne. A battle took place between Absalom with his army and his father's army. As Absalom was riding on a mule, he went under the branches of a terebinth tree, and his head caught in a branch, so that he was hanging between heaven and earth (2 Sam 18:6-9). Joab aimed three darts at the heart of Absalom, although David had commanded the army commanders not to touch him. Ten young men of Moab struck him and killed him, and buried him in a great pit, and raised over him a great heap of stones, as a kind of public disgrace of rebels and criminals.
David grieved greatly for him and lamented him, but he was compelled to meet the army returning victorious, so that the people would not rise up against him.
David had been anointed king over all Israel in Hebron (1 Sam 2:1-4, 11), and made it his royal center; sadly his son Absalom, who was of his own loins, rebelled against David in Hebron!
Talmai king of Geshur: a Semitic name meaning "belonging to furrows or the plowman." It is likely derived from the Hurrian word "talma'" meaning "great."
Shephatiah of Abital: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh has executed judgment," and he is the fifth son of David (1 Chr 3:3), who was born in Hebron of Abital.
Adonijah the son of Haggith, or Adonijah: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh is Lord" or "the Lord is Master."
Ithream: a Hebrew name meaning "the uncle is generous," a son of David born in Hebron (1 Chr 3:3).

entries.section: 1. The descendants of David in Hebron

paragraphs.text: These six were born unto him in Hebron;
and there he reigned seven years and six months: and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty and three years. [4]

entries.section: 2. The descendants of David in Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: 5 And these were born unto him in Jerusalem; Shimea, and Shobab, and Nathan, and Solomon, four, of Bathshua the daughter of Ammiel: 6 Ibhar also, and Elishama, and Eliphelet, 7 And Nogah, and Nepheg, and Japhia, 8 And Elishama, and Eliada, and Eliphelet, nine. 9 These were all the sons of David, beside the sons of the concubines, and Tamar their sister.

The book moves us from the city of Hebron, as the beginning of the kingdom of David over all Israel, to the city of Jerusalem as the city of God or the holy city (Neh 11:1, 16; Mt 4:5). The contemporary Arabs call it al-Quds. As for the origin of the Hebrew word, it is disputed; some see that it means possession of peace or foundation of peace. Heaven itself has been called "Jerusalem which is above" (Gal 4:26).

If the beginning of the way to enjoy the Kingdom of Christ is union and fellowship with God and people (Hebron), then the end of the way is the enjoyment of eternal, heavenly peace. This is the way to which the two books of Chronicles point.
Perhaps the most important matters that concern us in Jerusalem are the following:

a. It was anciently called Salem, and its king was Melchizedek, after whose order appeared the Lord Christ, the heavenly High Priest, who by His blood carries us to the bosom of the Father, justified.

b. Jerusalem was linked with Mount Moriah, which Abraham reached on the third day after setting out from Beersheba with his son Isaac to offer him as a sacrifice (Gen 22), and he returned with him alive, for the number three points to the resurrection of the Lord Christ.

c. In Jerusalem Solomon built the Temple as a sign of the constant divine presence in the midst of His people. It is as though Jerusalem urges us to enjoy the Lord Christ as the Priest-King (after the order of Melchizedek), and as the sacrifice that bestows righteousness and resurrection, and to enjoy fellowship with God.
And these were born unto him in Jerusalem;
Shimea, and Shobab, and Nathan, and Solomon,
four, of Bathshua the daughter of Ammiel. [5]
These were born in Jerusalem, and they are mentioned in (2 Sam 5:14-16; 1 Chr 14:4-7), but we find a difference in the names.
Shimea appears in Samuel and in (1 Chr 14) as Shammua.

entries.section: 2. The descendants of David in Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: Elishama [6]: appears in Samuel and in (1 Chr 14) as Elishua.

entries.section: 2. The descendants of David in Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: Eliada [8]: appears in (1 Chr 14) as Beeliada, and the two names carry the same meaning, "the Lord knows."
The Book of Samuel did not mention Eliphelet [6] and Nogah [7], and perhaps they died young.
Shobab: a Hebrew name meaning "backsliding." He is the son of Bathshua by David, born in Jerusalem.
Nathan: a Hebrew name meaning "God has given."

Bath-shua: a corruption of Bathsheba, a Hebrew name meaning "daughter of the oath" or "daughter of the seventh day." Her story is recorded in (2 Sam 11-12; 1 Kgs 1). David fell into sin with her, and summoned her husband Uriah the Hittite, who was a commander in the army, loyal and faithful to David and to the children of Israel, and asked him to spend the night in his house, but he refused to sleep with his wife while the army was in battle. David arranged his killing in the army so that his error would not be exposed. God sent to David Nathan the prophet, who rebuked him and declared to him the chastisements of the Lord for him. Her son Solomon the Wise took the throne after his father David, and built the Temple (1 Kgs 1-11; 2 Chr 2-9).
Ammiel: he was also called Eliam (2 Sam 11:3).

entries.section: 2. The descendants of David in Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: And Ibhar, and Elishama, and Eliphelet [6]
Ibhar: a Hebrew name meaning "he chooses," one of the sons of David, born in Jerusalem.

Elishama: a Hebrew name meaning "God has heard," which appears in (2 Sam 5:16; 1 Chr 14) as "Elishama." More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. A son of David, who was born in Jerusalem (1 Chr 3:1, 5-6). 2. Another son of David (1 Chr 3:8).

Eliphelet: a Hebrew name meaning "God has delivered him," which appears in (2 Sam 5:16; 1 Chr 14) as "Eliphalet." More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. A son of David, born in Jerusalem (1 Chr 3:5-6, 14; 14:5). 2. Another son of David, also born in Jerusalem, and perhaps after the death of the previous son.

entries.section: 2. The descendants of David in Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: And Nogah, and Nepheg, and Japhia, [7]
Nogah: a Hebrew name meaning "brightness," and he is one of the sons of David.

entries.section: 2. The descendants of David in Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: And Elishama, and Eliada, and Eliphelet, nine. [8]
Eliada: a Hebrew name meaning "one who knows God", a son of David born in Jerusalem.
Eliphelet: a son of David other than Eliphalet, and perhaps after Eliphalet died his brother was born and was called by his name, with a change in his name.
Japhia: a Semitic name meaning "he shines."

entries.section: 2. The descendants of David in Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: These were all the sons of David, beside the sons of the concubines,
and Tamar their sister. [9]
David had concubines, the names of whose sons are not mentioned, and perhaps the reason for this is that the concubines committed a kind of betrayal of David in the matter of Absalom.

Tamar: David had other daughters besides Tamar; Tamar is mentioned because of the incident concerning her brother Amnon. She was marked by beauty; Amnon her brother by her father assaulted her, and as much as he loved her exceedingly, so that he became sick because of his love for her, he hated her after assaulting her, and drove her from his presence, and so shame fell upon her (2 Sam 13-14).

10 And Solomon's son was Rehoboam, Abia his son, Asa his son, Jehoshaphat his son, 11 Joram his son, Ahaziah his son, Joash his son, 12 Amaziah his son, Azariah his son, Jotham his son, 13 Ahaz his son, Hezekiah his son, Manasseh his son, 14 Amon his son, Josiah his son. 15 And the sons of Josiah were, the firstborn Johanan, the second Jehoiakim, the third Zedekiah, the fourth Shallum. 16 And the sons of Jehoiakim: Jeconiah his son, Zedekiah his son. 17 And the sons of Jeconiah; Assir, Salathiel his son, 18 Malchiram also, and Pedaiah, and Shenazar, Jecamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah. 19 And the sons of Pedaiah were, Zerubbabel, and Shimei: and the sons of Zerubbabel; Meshullam, and Hananiah, and Shelomith their sister: 20 And Hashubah, and Ohel, and Berechiah, and Hasadiah, Jushabhesed, five. 21 And the sons of Hananiah; Pelatiah, and Jesaiah: the sons of Rephaiah, the sons of Arnan, the sons of Obadiah, the sons of Shechaniah. 22 And the sons of Shechaniah; Shemaiah: and the sons of Shemaiah; Hattush, and Igeal, and Bariah, and Neariah, and Shaphat, six. 23 And the sons of Neariah; Elioenai, and Hezekiah, and Azrikam, three. 24 And the sons of Elioenai were, Hodaiah, and Eliashib, and Pelaiah, and Akkub, and Johanan, and Dalaiah, and Anani, seven.

Sadly, among the sons of David there were those who caused him great bitterness, such as Amnon, Absalom and Adonijah. And we have not heard of any of his sons who imitated his godliness except Solomon, though Solomon himself went astray because of his marriage to pagan women.

Solomon, who was the fourth son of Bathsheba among those born in Jerusalem, sat on the throne, and the descendants of Solomon came in harmony with what is stated in the First and Second Books of Kings and what is stated during the exile and the return from it.
And Solomon's son was Rehoboam, Abia his son, Asa his son, Jehoshaphat his son, [10]

Rehoboam: he took the kingdom after the death of his father. He was narrow in thinking, and so he caused the division of the kingdom, for he answered harshly those who asked him to lighten the yoke with which his father had burdened them. This was done on the counsel of the young men who had grown up with him, and he rejected the counsel of the elders, the counselors of his father. Jeroboam exploited the matter, and gathered around him ten tribes under the name of the kingdom of Israel, and Judah and Benjamin remained with Rehoboam under the name of the kingdom of Judah.

The war continued between the two kingdoms for a long time, and often one of the two kingdoms allied itself with a foreign kingdom such as Aram or Assyria against its sister. Many of the descendants of Solomon took the rule in the kingdom of Judah, and we have previously spoken about these kings in Second Kings and Second Chronicles.
Abia, who is Abijam (1 Kgs 14:31).

Jehoshaphat (2 Chr 17-20): It seems that he learned from his father Asa, and imitated his good works, but on many occasions we see him imitating his father in his evil. He often returned to the Lord seeking His counsel and succeeded, but he allowed his son to marry Athaliah the daughter of Ahab the wicked king of Israel, who was an image of her mother, the wicked Jezebel.
Joram his son, Ahaziah his son, Joash his son, [11]
Amaziah his son, Azariah his son, Jotham his son, [12]

Azariah (Uzziah) (2 Chr 26): he was a successful king, who made many accomplishments, succeeded in wars and in time of peace, and was marked by building up and sound planning. Sadly his desire drove him not to give thanks to God but to fall into pride. He tried to seize the priestly work, and was struck with leprosy. He also failed to remove many symbols of idolatry from the country.
Ahaz his son, Hezekiah his son, Manasseh his son, [13]
King Hezekiah: we have previously spoken about him in (2 Kgs 18-20).
Amon his son, Josiah his son. [14]
King Josiah: we have previously spoken about him in (2 Kgs 22-23).
And the sons of Josiah were, the firstborn Johanan, the second Jehoiakim, the third Zedekiah, the fourth Shallum. [15]
From verse 15 onward, after the reign of the devoted and faithful Josiah, we find the kings at the time of the final ruin of Judah. This group brought the kingdom to the exile.

In the genealogies of Jesus Christ (Mt 1) Hananiah, Shechaniah, Neariah, Elioenai and Hodaiah are not mentioned. Some see that the rulers of Babylon changed these names in order to blot out every trace of monarchy from the spirit of the Jewish exiles (Dan 1:6-7)[8].

Johanan: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh is gracious." More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. The firstborn of Josiah, though he did not take the throne. Johanan is mentioned only here, and perhaps he died in his youth. 2. A son of Elioenai, of the descendants of David (1 Chr 3:24).
Jehoiakim: he is Eliakim (2 Kgs 23:34). (See Jer 22-28; 35-36).
Zedekiah: he is the fourth, and his first name was Mattaniah (2 Kgs 24:17). See (Jer 21-39).
Shallum: he is Jehoahaz (2 Kgs 23:30), and he is the third of the brothers, though he is mentioned last.
And the sons of Jehoiakim: Jeconiah his son, Zedekiah his son. [16]
Jeconiah: he is Coniah in (Jer 22:24, 28; 37:1); it means "He establishes" or "the Lord establishes."

Zedekiah: some see that the word "his son" here means "his successor." Zedekiah here is Zedekiah the son of Josiah, the king who succeeded Jehoiachin, and he is mentioned here because he did not go into exile.
And the sons of Jeconiah; Assir, Salathiel his son, [17]

Assir: a Hebrew word meaning "captive," and some thought that this name means a description of Jeconiah as "the captive," but it is clear from the Hebrew text and from the ancient versions that it does not indicate a description but a proper name.
Salathiel or Shealtiel: a Hebrew name meaning "I asked of God," and he is the son of Neri (Lk 3:27), adopted by Jeconiah after his late exile in March 597 B.C.
Malchiram also, and Pedaiah, and Shenazar, Jecamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah. [18]
Malchiram: a Hebrew name meaning "the king is exalted," and he is the son of Jehoiachin (Jeconiah) king of Judah.
Pedaiah: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh has redeemed," and it is the name of the brother of Salathiel and the father of Zerubbabel.

Shenazar[9]: of the descendants of Jeconiah. He is equivalent to "Sheshbazzar the prince of Judah at the return from Babylon in (538/537 B.C.) (Ezra 1:8). Both are an abbreviation of the Akkadian word Sin-aba-usur, which means: "Protect me, O moon god (Bassar)." He succeeded his nephew Zerubbabel, the natural son of the next older brother Pedaiah, but who was legally ascribed to the eldest son Salathiel (Ezra 3:2; Hag 1:1, 12; Mt 1:12; Lk 3:27). For Salathiel probably died without having offspring, therefore his brother raised up offspring for him to be ascribed to him according to the Law (Deut 25:5-10).
Jecamiah or Jekamiah: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh rises up," a man of Judah of the royal line.
Hoshama: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh has heard," and he is one of the descendants of King Jeconiah.
Nedabiah: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh is generous," and he is a son of King Jeconiah.
And the sons of Pedaiah were, Zerubbabel, and Shimei:
and the sons of Zerubbabel; Meshullam, and Hananiah, and Shelomith their sister: [19]

Zerubbabel: an Akkadian name meaning "sown in Babylon" or "born in Babylon," the son of Salathiel. Salathiel died without offspring, and perhaps Pedaiah his brother took his wife and raised up offspring for his brother according to the Law, so Zerubbabel became a son to him.

The leader of the first group of those returning from the captivity of Babylon to Jerusalem by the decree of Cyrus. Cyrus sent him in the sixth century B.C., and financed his project, and brought back with him the gold and silver vessels that Nebuchadnezzar had seized from the Temple. He began by building the altar for the worship of God, and laid foundations of the Temple. Two problems arose. The first was that some of the elders grieved when they compared the Temple that Solomon had previously built with the Temple that Zerubbabel rebuilt. And the second problem was that some enemies infiltrated and stopped the work by political pressure. So some were occupied with building their own houses, saying that the time had not come to build the house of the Lord. So God sent the prophets Haggai and Zechariah to encourage Zerubbabel, and the work began again after 16 years and the Temple was completed in four years. He was not like Nehemiah, for the latter did not allow problems and opposition to stop him from building.

The message of the Lord to him: "Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the LORD of hosts. Who art thou, O great mountain? before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain: and he shall bring forth the headstone thereof with shoutings, crying, Grace, grace unto it" (Zech 4:6-7).
In [19] two sons and their sister are mentioned, and in [21] five. Perhaps these five were from another mother, or were born after the return from the exile.
Shimei: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh hears," and he is the brother of Zerubbabel (1 Chr 3:19).
Meshullam: a Hebrew name meaning "one who has received his recompense," and it is the name of one of the sons of Zerubbabel (1 Chr 3:19).
Hananiah: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh has shown favor, has been gracious." He is the son of Zerubbabel, and the father of Pelatiah and Jesaiah.
Shelomith or Shelomoth: the feminine of "Shelomi" or "Solomon," and she is the daughter of Zerubbabel (1 Chr 3:19).
And Hashubah, and Ohel, and Berechiah, and Hasadiah, Jushabhesed, five. [20]
Hashubah: a Hebrew name meaning "reckoned or measure," and he is a son of Zerubbabel (1 Chr 3:20).
Ohel: a Hebrew name meaning "tent," and he is one of the sons of Zerubbabel (1 Chr 3:20).
Berechiah: a Hebrew name meaning "blessed of God." A son of Zerubbabel, of the descendants of David (1 Chr 3:20).
Hasadiah: a Hebrew name meaning "the Lord has been gracious," and he is a son of Zerubbabel, of the royal line of David.
Jushab or Jushabhesed: a Hebrew name meaning "mercy is repaid," and he is a son of Zerubbabel, of the descendants of David.
And the sons of Hananiah; Pelatiah, and Jesaiah: the sons of Rephaiah, the sons of Arnan, the sons of Obadiah, the sons of Shechaniah. [21]
Pelatiah: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh has set free," one of the sons of Hananiah, and a grandson of Zerubbabel.
Jesaiah: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh has saved." A son of Hananiah, of the descendants of David (1 Chr 3:21).
Rephaiah: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh has healed." A man of the descendants of David (1 Chr 3:21).
Arnan or Araunah: the meaning of the Hebrew word is not known with certainty.
Obadiah: a Hebrew name meaning "servant of Yahweh," and he is a head of a house of the descendants of David (1 Chr 3:21).
Shechaniah: an Aramaic word meaning "Yahweh dwells." Of the descendants of David, and the founder of a family.
And the sons of Shechaniah; Shemaiah: and the sons of Shemaiah; Hattush, and Igeal, and Bariah, and Neariah, and Shaphat, six. [22]
Shemaiah: a Hebrew name meaning "God hears." He is a son of David by Bathshua.
Hattush: a Hebrew name meaning "gathered." A man of Judah, the son of Shemaiah, and of the family of Shechaniah.
Igeal: a Hebrew name meaning "he redeems." He is the son of Shemaiah, of the descendants of King Shechaniah (1 Chr 3:22).
Bariah: a Hebrew name meaning "fugitive or wanderer."

Neariah: a Hebrew name meaning "bearer of the shield of Yahweh," and he is the father of Elioenai, Hezekiah and Azrikam, one of the six sons of Shemaiah, of the descendants of Solomon (1 Chr 3:22-23).
Shaphat: a Hebrew name meaning "he has judged." A son of Shemaiah, of the descendants of King David of the tribe of Judah.
And the sons of Neariah; Elioenai, and Hezekiah, and Azrikam, three. [23]
Elioenai: a Hebrew name meaning "my eyes are toward Yahweh," and he is a son of Neariah of the tribe of Judah.
Hezekiah: a Hebrew name meaning "the Lord has strengthened" or "the Lord is strength." He is a son of Neariah, a relative of the royal family of Judah (1 Chr 3:23).
Azrikam: a Hebrew name meaning "my help has arisen," and he is a son of Neariah Elioenai, one of the descendants of David (1 Chr 3:23).
And the sons of Elioenai were,
Hodaiah, and Eliashib, and Pelaiah, and Akkub, and Johanan, and Dalaiah, and Anani, seven. [24]
Hod: a Hebrew name meaning "splendor," and Hodaiah means "splendor to Yahweh," and he is a son of Elioenai, one of the descendants of David (1 Chr 3:24).
Eliashib: a Hebrew name meaning "he whom God restores." He is a son of Elioenai, of the descendants of Zerubbabel.
Pelaiah: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh is wonderful," and it is the name of a man of Judah, of the descendants of Shechaniah.
Akkub: a Hebrew name meaning "follower or pursuer," a son of Elioenai from among the line of Shechaniah, of the descendants of David.
Dalaiah: a Hebrew name meaning "he whom the Lord has freed," and he is of the descendants of David, a son of Elioenai.
Anani: a Hebrew name, an abbreviation of the name "Ananiah," one of the seven sons of Elioenai, of the descendants of David.
Bring me into the eternal wedding, that I may enjoy fellowship in Your glories
v May Your Holy Spirit carry me with David to Hebron.
In amazement I stand to see my father David, while under the shadow of the Law, setting out to Hebron, the symbol of the wedding and union and clinging to You.
He is not preoccupied with all the events of his past; he remembers only his glorious works through You, and his weaknesses and bitter trials.
He no longer remembers King Saul's continual opposition to him.
His spiritual wedding and his enjoyment of the splendor of Your glory in him drew away all his feelings!
v As is his habit, he did not reproach You:
Where is Your promise to me, when I was a boy, that I would become king over all Israel?
What occupies him is to enjoy You, O King of kings.
He sees You by the spirit of prophecy on the cross as King!
Your love and glory drew all his thoughts and emotions and senses!
It suffices him to see You, O Savior of the world, uniting the heavenly and the human together.
v His meeting with You wrought wonder in all the mighty men.
The brothers of Saul the wicked and the commanders of his army withdrew to You.
They were turned into working energies for the sake of Your Kingdom.
They see in You the wonderful King who is in the bosom of the King of kings.
They see in You a fatherhood that is a shadow of the fatherhood of God, full of tenderness.
v In Hebron is the tomb of Sarah and Abraham and Jacob and Isaac.
They smell the fragrant and beautiful scent of Your resurrection, instead of the smell of death and corruption.
All the tribes saw You as they were coming to David.
They enjoyed You, You who shone with the splendor of the resurrection upon the heart of David.
Hebron is no longer a center for visiting the tombs of the great, but has become a shadow of the heavenly wedding.
The dead and the living enjoy it in the fellowship of the heavenly ones, no, rather in fellowship and enjoyment of the Holy Trinity!
v Hebron is no longer the dwelling of the priests and Levites, but has become a shadow of the bridal chambers of the heavenly High Priest and of the throne of the King of kings.
They see You as in the heavenly sanctuaries interceding with Your blood for humanity.
v Praise and thanks be to You, for You enter with me into Hebron.
My soul rests, not only because it is a city of refuge, but because it has become for me a place of meeting with You, O fortress of my life.
v Grant me, with David, to set out from Hebron to Jerusalem.
Truly, what shall I say? And of what shall I speak concerning the holy city of God?
Founded on mountains, not of stone, but heavenly.
What enemy can infiltrate it, and what harm can reach it!
v Anciently Jerusalem was called Salem, and its king was Melchizedek.
Grant me to enjoy the pledge of the Jerusalem above; You are its King, the Giver of true righteousness and heavenly peace.
v Jerusalem takes pride in its Temple, but the Jerusalem above, its temple is not made with human hands.
You are its sun and its light; there is no place in it for darkness.
You are the mystery of its glory and its delight and its joy.
Through You I cross over to it, and live in Your divine embrace.
v With my father David I sing, saying:
I have known You, O Son of David, Bridegroom of my soul!
You are the King of kings, You make me a king!
You are the Resurrection, You grant me victory over death!
You are the heavenly High Priest, You enter with me into the bosom of the Father!
You are my divine, heavenly refuge!
You carry me to heaven, the Jerusalem above!
Your divine peace descends upon me, and You cover me with Your righteousness, O Holy One!
I enjoy the splendor of the heavenly sanctuaries.
You shine upon me with Your light, so darkness will not surround me!
You are my glory and my joy, O delight of my soul!

entries.section: 1. Completion of the genealogies of Judah

paragraphs.text: 1 The sons of Judah; Pharez, Hezron, and Carmi, and Hur, and Shobal. 2 And Reaiah the son of Shobal begat Jahath; and Jahath begat Ahumai, and Lahad. These are the families of the Zorathites. 3 And these were of the father of Etam; Jezreel, and Ishma, and Idbash: and the name of their sister was Hazelelponi: 4 And Penuel the father of Gedor, and Ezer the father of Hushah. These are the sons of Hur, the firstborn of Ephratah, the father of Bethlehem. 5 And Ashur the father of Tekoa had two wives, Helah and Naarah. 6 And Naarah bare him Ahuzam, and Hepher, and Temeni, and Haahashtari. These were the sons of Naarah. 7 And the sons of Helah were, Zereth, and Zohar, and Ethnan. 8 And Coz begat Anub, and Zobebah, and the families of Aharhel the son of Harum. 9 And Jabez was more honorable than his brethren: and his mother called his name Jabez, saying, Because I bare him with sorrow. 10 And Jabez called on the God of Israel, saying, Oh that thou wouldest bless me indeed, and enlarge my coast, and that thine hand might be with me, and that thou wouldest keep me from evil, that it may not grieve me! And God granted him that which he requested. 11 And Chelub the brother of Shuah begat Mehir, which was the father of Eshton. 12 And Eshton begat Bethrapha, and Paseah, and Tehinnah the father of Irnahash. These are the men of Rechah. 13 And the sons of Kenaz; Othniel, and Seraiah: and the sons of Othniel; Hathath. 14 And Meonothai begat Ophrah: and Seraiah begat Joab, the father of the valley of craftsmen; for they were craftsmen. 15 And the sons of Caleb the son of Jephunneh; Iru, Elah, and Naam: and the sons of Elah, even Kenaz. 16 And the sons of Jehaleleel; Ziph, and Ziphah, Tiria, and Asareel. 17 And the sons of Ezra were, Jether, and Mered, and Epher, and Jalon: and she bare Miriam, and Shammai, and Ishbah the father of Eshtemoa. 18 And his wife Jehudijah bare Jered the father of Gedor, and Heber the father of Socho, and Jekuthiel the father of Zanoah. And these are the sons of Bithiah the daughter of Pharaoh, which Mered took. 19 And the sons of his wife Hodiah the sister of Naham, the father of Keilah the Garmite, and Eshtemoa the Maachathite. 20 And the sons of Shimon were, Amnon, and Rinnah the son of Hanan, and Tilon. And the sons of Ishi were, Zoheth, and Benzoheth. 21 The sons of Shelah the son of Judah were, Er the father of Lecah, and Laadah the father of Mareshah, and the families of the house of them that wrought fine linen, of the house of Ashbea, 22 And Jokim, and the men of Chozeba, and Joash, and Saraph, who had the dominion in Moab, and Jashubilehem. And these are ancient things. 23 These were the potters and the inhabitants of Netaim and Gederah: there they dwelt with the king for his work.
The sons of Judah; Pharez, Hezron, and Carmi, and Hur, and Shobal. [1]

Pharez was the son of Judah, and Hezron the son of Pharez (1 Chr 2:5); as for the Carmi mentioned here, he is Chelubai (1 Chr 2:9), and he is distinct from the Carmi mentioned in (1 Chr 2:7) and in (Josh 7:1); he was a son of Hezron.
Pharez: a Hebrew name meaning "breach."
Hezron: a Hebrew name meaning "siege or enclosure."
Carmi: a Hebrew name meaning "worker in vineyards."
Hur: it is thought to be an Egyptian name, taken from the name of the god "Horus."
Shobal: the son of Hur, of the house of Caleb, of the tribe of Judah, of the family of Hezron. From his descendants came the inhabitants of the village of Kirjath-jearim (1 Chr 4:2, 4).

entries.section: 1. Completion of the genealogies of Judah

paragraphs.text: And Reaiah the son of Shobal begat Jahath; and Jahath begat Ahumai, and Lahad.
These are the families of the Zorathites. [2]
Reaiah: it is thought that he is Haroeh (1 Chr 2:52), and the meaning is "the seer" or "Yahweh sees."
The Zorathites: Zorah was in the south of Judah on the border of the Philistines.

Jahath: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "he seizes." Two persons bore this same name: 1. A man of the tribe of Judah, of the family of Hezron (1 Chr 4:2). 2. A Levite, a Kohathite of the house of Izhar in the days of David (1 Chr 24:22).
Ahumai: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "Ahuma," and he was one of the heads of the clans of Judah.
Lahad: a Hebrew name meaning "load" or "burden," and he is a son of Jahath, of the descendants of Judah.

entries.section: 1. Completion of the genealogies of Judah

paragraphs.text: And these were of the father of Etam;
Jezreel, and Ishma, and Idbash: and the name of their sister was Hazelelponi: [3]

Etam: a Hebrew name meaning "lair of birds of prey." By the father of Etam is meant the builder of the city of Etam. It is the name of more than one city: 1. A town in Judea near Bethlehem, which Rehoboam fortified after the division between the tribes (2 Chr 11:6). Today it is called Khirbet al-Khokh at Solomon's Pool. Traces of water cisterns were found there, and the pools of Solomon near the village of Artas and Ain Etan. 2. A town in the southern part of Judea, which passed from the sons of Judah to Simeon (1 Chr 4:32). Perhaps it is present-day Aitun, eleven miles southwest of al-Khalil.
Jezreel: a Hebrew name meaning "God sows," and he is a man of the descendants of Judah [3].
Ishma: a Hebrew name, perhaps an abbreviation of the word Ishmael, and he is a man of Judah, the son of Hur.
Idbash: a Hebrew name meaning "sweet as honey," and he is a son of the father of Etam, a man of Judah.
Hazelelponi: a Hebrew name meaning "He gives shade upon me," the name of a girl of the sons of Judah. The names of some of her brothers, the men, are mentioned.

entries.section: 1. Completion of the genealogies of Judah

paragraphs.text: And Penuel the father of Gedor, and Ezer the father of Hushah.
These are the sons of Hur, the firstborn of Ephratah, the father of Bethlehem. [4]
Penuel: a Hebrew name meaning "face of God." It is the name of a man of Judah, the father of the inhabitants of Gedor.
Gedor: a Hebrew name meaning "fortress" or "walled place." More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. A son of Penuel (1 Chr 4:4). 2. A son of Jered by his Jewish wife (1 Chr 4:18).

There is also a place called Gedor between Seir and Judah, perhaps within the borders of the tribe of Simeon near the northwestern border of Palestine (1 Chr 4:39), and it appears in the Septuagint as "Gerar."
Ezer the father of Hushah: Ezer, a Hebrew name meaning "help." Of the descendants of Judah, from among Hadar.
Ephratah: a Hebrew word meaning "fruitful."
By his saying "the father of Bethlehem," he means its chief.

entries.section: 1. Completion of the genealogies of Judah

paragraphs.text: And Ashur the father of Tekoa had two wives, Helah and Naarah. [5]
Ashur the father of Tekoa: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "blackness."
Helah: a Hebrew name meaning "ornament, adornment, necklace, collar." One of the two wives of Ashur, the ancestor of the men of Tekoa, of the tribe of Judah.
Naarah: a Hebrew name meaning "girl," one of the two wives of Ashur and the mother of Ahuzam and his brothers.

entries.section: 1. Completion of the genealogies of Judah

paragraphs.text: And Naarah bare him Ahuzam, and Hepher, and Temeni, and Haahashtari. These were the sons of Naarah. [6]
Ahuzam: a Hebrew name meaning "the king or the owner," a son of Ashur of the clan of Hezron.
Hepher: a Hebrew name meaning "pit or well," of Judah, a son of Ashur of the clan of Hezron in the tribe of Judah.
Haahashtari: perhaps from Persian, meaning "follower of the queen," and he is a son of Ashur.

entries.section: 1. Completion of the genealogies of Judah

paragraphs.text: And the sons of Helah were, Zereth, and Zohar, and Ethnan. [7]
Zereth: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "splendor."
Zohar: a Hebrew name meaning "white," and it also appears in the form "Jezoar."

entries.section: 1. Completion of the genealogies of Judah

paragraphs.text: And Coz begat Anub, and Zobebah, and the families of Aharhel the son of Harum. [8]
Coz: a Hebrew name meaning "thorn," perhaps he was one of the sons of Helah.
Anub: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "bound," a son of Coz, one of the chiefs of Judah.
Zobebah: a Hebrew name meaning "hatred, anger," and he is a son of Coz, of the sons of Helah.
Aharhel the son of Harum: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "brother of Rachel" or "the last of strength." He is the son of Harum, and he was head of a clan in Judah.

entries.section: 1. Completion of the genealogies of Judah

paragraphs.text: And Jabez was more honorable than his brethren:
and his mother called his name Jabez, saying, "Because I bare him with sorrow." [9]

entries.section: 1. Completion of the genealogies of Judah

paragraphs.text: And Jabez called on the God of Israel:
"Oh that thou wouldest bless me indeed, and enlarge my coast, and that thine hand might be with me, and that thou wouldest keep me from evil, that it may not grieve me!"
And God granted him that which he requested. [10]
Jabez: a Hebrew name meaning "he causes pain," the name of a man of Judah whom his mother called Jabez because she bore him in pain.

His father's name is not mentioned, nor in what age he lived, but it was said of him that he was more honorable than his brethren. All we know about him, whether from the Bible or from Jewish tradition, is that he was a teacher of the Law, Doctor in Law, and that he was a godly man. For this reason the city where he lived was often called by his name (1 Chr 2:55). He was a man of faith, "but without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him" (Heb 11:6).

He was called "more honorable than his brethren"; the secret of his greatness and nobility is not that he performed a heroic deed more than his brothers, but that he made God the center of his life and work. He knew how to give God His right place in his life as the Lord, the giver of blessings, the giver of inner victory, the leader of life, and the true fortress against evil.
Sorrow no longer has a place in the heart of the man of God, for he knew what to ask, and God granted him what he asked.

The prayer of Jabez is regarded as unique, for the prayer, together with its answer, did not occupy more than one verse. He presents to us an ideal prayer accepted before God; he asked and received from God. It was answered quickly, so what is the secret of its acceptance?
His prayer included four matters, and revealed the role of God in the life of the believer:

The first petition: asking for blessing = the blessed, heavenly life. "Oh that thou wouldest bless me!" means: give me true happiness. God is the giver of blessings and true happiness. The second petition: asking for the enlargement of the border = the widening of the heart in love for God and people. He asks for an enlarged heart in which every person finds a place by love. God is the giver of true love.

The third petition: asking that the hand of God be with him = the enjoyment of the divine presence; he longs that He dwell in us, and work in us and through us and protect us. May the hand of God be with us! He asks for the protection of God and His care for him.

The fourth petition: asking to be kept from evil = victory over the devil and evil. Being kept from evil: He gives him authority over Satan and all his powers, and thereby removes from him the evil that robs him of his joy in the Lord.

Since the petitions came according to the will of God, or the vow that Jabez made, it was said: "And God granted him that which he requested" (1 Chr 4:10). It is stated in the Book of Jeremiah: "Then shall ye call upon me, and ye shall go and pray unto me, and I will hearken unto you. And ye shall seek me, and find me, when ye shall search for me with all your heart" (Jer 29:12-13).

Jabez became successful in all aspects of his life: in his works and studies and his relationship with others, and his struggle with the pagans. God was always ready to listen to all that was in his heart or mind.

entries.section: 1. Completion of the genealogies of Judah

paragraphs.text: And Chelub the brother of Shuah begat Mehir, which was the father of Eshton. [11]
Chelub: a Hebrew name meaning "basket or cage for birds," the name of the brother of Shuah. His lineage was not fully known, but he was reckoned among the descendants of Judah (1 Chr 4:11).
Shuah: a Hebrew name meaning "low," a man of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 4:11).
Mehir: a Hebrew name meaning "price," a man of the descendants of Judah (1 Chr 4:11).
Eshton: the meaning of the name is not known with certainty. It is the name of one of the sons of Mehir of the tribe of Judah.

entries.section: 1. Completion of the genealogies of Judah

paragraphs.text: And Eshton begat Bethrapha, and Paseah, and Tehinnah the father of Irnahash.
These are the men of Rechah. [12]
Rapha: a Hebrew name meaning "he healed, that is, God healed." Bethrapha: it was built by the son of Eshton.
Paseah: a Hebrew name meaning "lame," a man of Judah of the descendants of Chelub (1 Chr 4:12).
Tehinnah: a Hebrew name meaning "grace or supplication," of the tribe of Judah, the founder of the city of Nahash, and called its father; he is the son of Eshton (1 Chr 4:12).
Nahash: a Semitic name meaning "serpent or snake."
Rechah: a place in the portion of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 4:12).

entries.section: 1. Completion of the genealogies of Judah

paragraphs.text: And the sons of Kenaz; Othniel, and Seraiah: and the sons of Othniel; Hathath. [13]

Othniel: a Hebrew name meaning "God is strength," and it also means "the answering of the Lord," and also "the time of God for myself." Of the descendants of Kenaz, that is, of the clan of the Kenezites, and his father is Jephunneh. He is the younger brother of Caleb (Josh 15:17). The first of the judges of Israel, he reformed the affairs of the people and brought about peace in the country (Judg 1:9-15; 3:5-11).

It was said of him: "And Caleb said, He that smiteth Kirjathsepher, and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife. And Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, took it: and he gave him Achsah his daughter to wife" (Judg 1:12-13).

"And when the children of Israel cried unto the LORD, the LORD raised up a deliverer to the children of Israel, who delivered them, even Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother. And the Spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he judged Israel, and went out to war: and the LORD delivered Chushanrishathaim king of Mesopotamia into his hand; and his hand prevailed against Chushanrishathaim. And the land had rest forty years. And Othniel the son of Kenaz died" (Judg 3:9-11).
We have previously commented on these two texts in our commentary on the Book of Judges:

a. Othniel means "the answering of the Lord," so no one can seize Kirjathsepher (Judg 1:12), that is, enjoy the Holy Bible, except one to whom it is granted by God or whose request is answered; then he marries Achsah the daughter of Caleb, that is, he cleaves to the holy life and comes to know its secrets, not as a village in which he dwells, but as a bride whom he marries[1].

b. The choice of Othniel as a judge did not come at random, for God wanted him to be the first of the judges to declare that the secret of victory and salvation lies in God, since the word Othniel means "the answering of God" or "the strength of God"[2]. For salvation is not accomplished by human strength, but by the answer of the Lord, who hears the cries of His children and works in them by His divine power.

By him the land had rest forty years; if the land points to the body and the number 40 points to the blessed temporal life, then when we carry within us a soul that walks like this judge by the Spirit of the Lord and enjoys the word of God, our body rests in the Lord, and is holy in His sight all the days of our time. Let Othniel be a leader within us, that we may rest and be filled with surpassing peace!

v The Scripture speaks of the savior Othniel, whose name means "the time of the Lord for my benefit." According to this, these first people were delivered from humiliation and bondage by him, and peace returned to the people. The peace which they had lost for a short time in the past because of their pride and their various crimes.

It is possible to understand "Chushanrishathaim" in the spiritual sense, as one of the enemies and also "the prince of the power of the air" (Eph 2:2). Therefore it is logical that we follow Othniel, who was raised up from heaven to liberate the people (Lk 2:11). He is (a type) of one of the dwellers of heaven and of the angelic powers, the "ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation" (Heb 1:14). They are the angels of salvation whom Othniel or Ehud represents.
Truly the opposing powers fight us, but good divine powers are sent from God to help us.

Let us see who Othniel is, and from what noble family. He is the son of Kenaz the brother of Caleb, the wonderful man worthy of praise, who was a companion of Joshua the son of Nun. The Scripture says about Othniel: "And when the children of Israel cried unto the LORD," and "the Spirit of the LORD came upon" Othniel, "and he judged Israel" (Judg 3:9-10)...

I do not know whether there is any judge in the Church whom the Lord can consider worthy of being "filled with the Spirit of God" like Othniel himself, who was honored by the testimony of Holy Scripture. These are the leaders whom we desire to be worthy of this testimony. Therefore it says: "And the Spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he judged Israel, and went out to war: and the LORD delivered Chushanrishathaim king of Mesopotamia into his hand" (Judg 3:10). Why? Because "the Spirit of the LORD" was in him, and also "his hand prevailed against Chushanrishathaim" (Judg 3:10) "And the land had rest forty years." Behold, you see how great is the divine mercy.
[For eight years the people of Israel were slaves] (Judg 3:8), because of the sins of many. [And for forty years] (Judg 3:11) they had rest because of the righteousness of one person[3].
Origen Seraiah: a Hebrew name meaning "God has prevailed." He is the son of Kenaz and the younger brother of Othniel, and the father of Joab the father of the valley of craftsmen (1 Chr 4:13-14).
Hathath: a Hebrew name meaning "terror," a son of Othniel (1 Chr 4:13).

entries.section: 1. Completion of the genealogies of Judah

paragraphs.text: And Meonothai begat Ophrah: and Seraiah begat Joab, the father of the valley of craftsmen; for they were craftsmen. [14]
Meonothai: a Hebrew name meaning "my dwellings," a man of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 4:14).
Ophrah: a Hebrew name meaning "gazelle," the son of Meonothai, of the sons of Judah (1 Chr 4:14).

Joab: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh is father," the name of the son of Seraiah, the father of a company of craftsmen (1 Chr 4:14), in the valley of craftsmen, and it may be the "Valley of the Waterfall" that runs to the northwest of Lod toward Joppa.

It is observed that the land of Judah was less suitable for agriculture than the land of the northern kingdom, and so we find the proportion of farmers in it small, but we find in it many skilled craftsmen [14], and linen workers [21], and potters [23].
We notice that the whole family were craftsmen, skilled in their task, and artisans and merchants. They were creative and diligent above all their neighbors.
The father of the valley of craftsmen: that is, the people of the valley of craftsmen (Neh 11:35), which is near Lod, now called Wadi Razia; it was said that the craftsmen of the Temple were from it.

entries.section: 1. Completion of the genealogies of Judah

paragraphs.text: And the sons of Caleb the son of Jephunneh; Iru, Elah, and Naam:
and the sons of Elah, even Kenaz. [15]

Caleb: a Hebrew name meaning "heart," and he is the son of Jephunneh the Kenezite and the elder brother of Othniel. He is one of the twelve spies whom Moses the prophet sent to the Promised Land. Caleb, with Joshua the son of Nun, affirmed the fulfillment of God's promise to the people to take possession of the Promised Land (Num 13-14; Josh 14-15).

The majority of the spies (ten spies) stirred up a state of discouragement among the people, while Joshua and Caleb alone held fast to the promise of God, and believed in the power of God and the truthfulness of His promise to His people.
In every generation there is a holy remnant, a minority, who believe practically in the promise of God, and bear witness to Him by their lives.

Joshua was joined with Caleb in entering the Promised Land; if Jesus – the Lord of glory – is our leader in our entering the Promised Land, then there is no entering it for us unless our heart (Caleb) is earnest and sincere in entering. The joining of Joshua with Caleb is the union of the free divine work with the free human will that accepts the work in the inner depths.

In Eshcol Joshua and Caleb carried the one cluster on a pole to enter with it to the people, declaring the fulfillment of the promises of God. It is as though the life-giving Cross is carried by "Jesus" Christ our Lord and carried by the believer with a heart (Caleb) filled with sincerity. It is the Cross of Jesus Christ the Savior, which the believer carries as a fellowship of sufferings with his Lord, to enter with Him into the power of His resurrection.

St. John Chrysostom sees in this cluster a pledge of the heavenly life, saying: [Let us not despise heaven!... For He brought to us fruits from heaven, not a cluster of grapes carried on a staff, but "the earnest of the Spirit" (2 Cor 1:22), and citizenship in heaven (Phil 3:20), the things that Paul and the whole company of the Apostles, the wonderful vinedressers, taught us. It was not Caleb the son of Jephunneh nor Joshua the son of Nun who brought these fruits, but Jesus the Son of the [Father of mercies] (2 Cor 1:3), the Son of God who brings every virtue, and brings from heaven all its fruits, that is, its praises![4]]

St. Ambrose praised the two spies, for they preferred to speak the truth even if the price was their stoning (Num 14:10), rather than do as the rest of the spies who pleased the people at the expense of the truth. The Saint says: [They preferred to be stoned, as the people threatened them, rather than retreat from their steadfastness full of virtue[5].], [The two good men preferred (divine) glory to safety, but the wicked preferred safety to virtue[6].]
Iru: a Hebrew name meaning "cautious." He was the eldest son of Caleb the son of Jephunneh. His name appears as Ir in the Greek Septuagint and in the Vulgate.

Elah: a Hebrew name meaning "oak tree," and the name of a son of Caleb of the tribe of Judah is mentioned (1 Chr 4:15). He is distinct from Kenaz mentioned in [13]. The name Kenaz was beloved among the Kenezites.
Naam: a Hebrew name meaning "delight." He is a son of Caleb, head of a tribe. His descendants dwelt east of the Jordan.
Kenaz: a Semitic name, perhaps meaning "hunting," and it is the name of a son of Elah the son of Caleb.

entries.section: 1. Completion of the genealogies of Judah

paragraphs.text: And the sons of Jehaleleel; Ziph, and Ziphah, Tiria, and Asareel. [16]

entries.section: 1. Completion of the genealogies of Judah

paragraphs.text: And the sons of Ezra were, Jether, and Mered, and Epher, and Jalon:
and she bare Miriam, and Shammai, and Ishbah the father of Eshtemoa. [17]
Ezra: a Hebrew name meaning "help," of the sons of Judah.
Jether: a Hebrew name meaning "excellence."
Mered: a Hebrew name meaning "rebellion," and he is the son of Ezra and the husband of Bithiah the daughter of Pharaoh.
Epher or Ephar: a Hebrew name meaning "young gazelle," of the line of Ezra.
Jalon: a son of Ezra, recorded with the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 4:17).

entries.section: 1. Completion of the genealogies of Judah

paragraphs.text: Miriam: of the descendants of Judah (1 Chr 4:17). The mother of this Miriam was not mentioned previously, and perhaps she is Bithiah mentioned at the end of [18].
Ishbah: a Hebrew name meaning "he praises." He is an ancestor of the inhabitants of Eshtemoa (1 Chr 4:17).

entries.section: 1. Completion of the genealogies of Judah

paragraphs.text: (And his wife Jehudijah bare Jered the father of Gedor, and Heber the father of Socho, and Jekuthiel the father of Zanoah).
And these are the sons of Bithiah the daughter of Pharaoh, which Mered took. [18]

And his wife Jehudijah: it is thought that her husband is Mered [18], and it is thought that Bithiah was Egyptian, and a second wife of Mered. Her husband was one of the chiefs of Judah. The meaning of Bithiah is "daughter of the Lord"; perhaps she took this name when she became a Jewess, and her children are Miriam and Shammai and Ishbah, mentioned at the end of [17].
Jered or Jarad: a Semitic name, perhaps meaning "descent" or "rose," and he is of the descendants of Judah (1 Chr 4:18).
Heber: a Hebrew name meaning "fellowship, partner." Of the descendants of Ezra, and the father of the people of Socho.
Socho: a Hebrew word meaning "yearnings."
Jekuthiel: a Hebrew name meaning "God nourishes." He is the father of the inhabitants of Zanoah.
Zanoah: a Hebrew name meaning "marsh" or "thicket."

Bithiah: her name is Hebrew, meaning "daughter of Yahweh" or "worshiper of Yahweh," one of the few women whose names are mentioned in these genealogies. She was the daughter of Pharaoh, and the wife of Mered, a man of Judah. It is likely that she entered the worship of Yahweh with the chosen people.
Mered: a Hebrew name meaning "rebellion," son of Ezra of the tribe of Judah, and husband of Bithiah the daughter of Pharaoh.

entries.section: 1. Completion of the genealogies of Judah

paragraphs.text: And the sons of his wife Hodiah the sister of Naham, the father of Keilah the Garmite, and Eshtemoa the Maachathite. [19]
Naham: a Hebrew name meaning "consolation," a Jewish man, who married Hodiah his sister (1 Chr 4:19).
Keilah the Garmite: he is mentioned in the genealogies of the descendants of Caleb the son of Jephunneh.
Eshtemoa: a Hebrew name meaning "obedience." He is Eshtemoa the Maachathite, the son of Ishbah of the tribe of Judah.

entries.section: 1. Completion of the genealogies of Judah

paragraphs.text: And the sons of Shimon were, Amnon, and Rinnah the son of Hanan, and Tilon.
And the sons of Ishi were, Zoheth, and Benzoheth. [20]
Amnon: a Hebrew name meaning "faithful," the son of Shimon of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 4:20).
Rinnah the son of Hanan: a Hebrew name meaning "cry of joy," and he is a man from among Judah, the son of Shimon.
Tilon: a Hebrew name meaning "lofty." He was the son of Shimon, a man of the descendants of Judah.

Ishi: a Hebrew name meaning "savior." There are two with the same name: 1. A man of Judah, the father of Zoheth. 2. A Simeonite whose sons became the head of a band, and attacked the Amalekites in Mount Seir, and seized their settlement and dwelt in it (1 Chr 4:42).
Zoheth: a Hebrew name meaning "proud." He is the son of Ishi of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 4:20).
Benzoheth: a Hebrew name meaning "son of Zoheth," and he is of the descendants of Judah (1 Chr 4:20).

entries.section: 1. Completion of the genealogies of Judah

paragraphs.text: The sons of Shelah the son of Judah were, Er the father of Lecah, and Laadah the father of Mareshah, and the families of the house of them that wrought fine linen, of the house of Ashbea, [21]
Shelah: a Hebrew name meaning "dog," and he was the third of the sons of Judah (1 Chr 4:21).
Er: a Hebrew name meaning "cautious," and he is the son of Shelah, of the descendants of Judah (1 Chr 4:21); Shelah had a brother with the same name "Er" (1 Chr 2:3).
Lecah: a village in Judah, as may be inferred from the verse (1 Chr 4:21); its location is not known exactly.

Laadah: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "thick-necked." (See al-laghd in Arabic, which is the flesh in the throat and around the lower chin to the ear.) Of the family of Shelah, and the father of the inhabitants of Mareshah (1 Chr 4:21).
Mareshah: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "place of the head and the summit."

Ashbea: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "abundance" or "satiety." Of the descendants of Shelah. His family wove a fine, excellent kind of linen known as bazz. Some think that the house of Ashbea is the name of some place.

entries.section: 1. Completion of the genealogies of Judah

paragraphs.text: And Jokim, and the men of Chozeba, and Joash, and Saraph, who had the dominion in Moab, and Jashubilehem.
And these are ancient things. [22]
Jokim: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh establishes," one of the sons of Shelah of Judah (1 Chr 4:22).
The men of Chozeba: a Hebrew name meaning "lying," a village in Judah inhabited especially by the sons of Shelah (1 Chr 4:22). Most thought it is Chezib or Achzib.
Joash: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh has given," an abbreviation of Jehoash, a man of the descendants of Judah.
Saraph: a Hebrew name meaning "burning or serpent," of the descendants of Shelah, and he was of those who had dominion in Moab.

Jashubilehem: a Hebrew name meaning "he returns the bread," most probably the name of a person of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 4:22). But some translations consider the two words not a name but a phrase meaning (and they returned to Lehem).

entries.section: 1. Completion of the genealogies of Judah

paragraphs.text: These were the potters and the inhabitants of Netaim and Gederah:
there they dwelt with the king for his work. [23]
Netaim: a Hebrew name meaning "plantings," a place in Judah where the plantings of the king were.

Gederah or Gederi: a Hebrew name meaning "sheepfold." They dwelt in the king's possessions to serve him. They were not among those of great deeds, but gained their fame and honor because they "dwelt... with the king for his work."

The secret of the believer's strength, success and honor is to cleave to the King of kings and work for the sake of His Kingdom. Each of them has his gift, but what binds them together is their dwelling with the King to work in His vineyard. For on the Day of the Lord we shall enjoy the heavenly crown, not for the kind of work or service we practiced, but for our faithfulness, and we shall hear His divine voice: "thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things" (Mt 25:21). We shall find children reckoned as heroes, and people of fame scarcely saved as by fire. The reckonings of God rest on the extent of the believer's faithfulness and sincerity, not on his role in the work.

entries.section: 2. The genealogies of the sons of Simeon

paragraphs.text: 24 The sons of Simeon were, Nemuel, and Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul: 25 Shallum his son, Mibsam his son, Mishma his son. 26 And the sons of Mishma; Hamuel his son, Zacchur his son, Shimei his son. 27 And Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters; but his brethren had not many children, neither did all their family multiply, like to the children of Judah. 28 And they dwelt at Beersheba, and Moladah, and Hazarshual, 29 And at Bilhah, and at Ezem, and at Tolad, 30 And at Bethuel, and at Hormah, and at Ziklag, 31 And at Bethmarcaboth, and Hazarsusim, and at Bethbirei, and at Shaaraim. These were their cities unto the reign of David. 32 And their villages were, Etam, and Ain, Rimmon, and Tochen, and Ashan, five cities: 33 And all their villages that were round about the same cities, unto Baal. These were their habitations, and their genealogy. 34 And Meshobab, and Jamlech, and Joshah, the son of Amaziah, 35 And Joel, and Jehu the son of Joshibiah, the son of Seraiah, the son of Asiel, 36 And Elioenai, and Jaakobah, and Jeshohaiah, and Asaiah, and Adiel, and Jesimiel, and Benaiah, 37 And Ziza the son of Shiphi, the son of Allon, the son of Jedaiah, the son of Shimri, the son of Shemaiah; 38 These mentioned by their names were princes in their families: and the house of their fathers increased greatly, 39 And they went to the entrance of Gedor, even unto the east side of the valley, to seek pasture for their flocks. 40 And they found fat pasture and good, and the land was wide, and quiet, and peaceable; for they of Ham had dwelt there of old. 41 And these written by name came in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, and smote their tents and the Meunim that were found there, and destroyed them utterly unto this day, and dwelt in their rooms: because there was pasture there for their flocks. 42 And some of them, even of the sons of Simeon, five hundred men, went to mount Seir, having for their captains Pelatiah, and Neariah, and Rephaiah, and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi. 43 And they smote the rest of the Amalekites that were escaped, and dwelt there unto this day.

The genealogies of the sons of Simeon were recorded immediately after Judah, perhaps because of the clinging of his tribe to the tribe of Judah. The portion of the tribe of Simeon in the Promised Land was within the borders of the region of Judah (Josh 19:9). In any case, the tribe asked for additional land during the battles.

If the tribe of Benjamin joined the tribe of Judah when the schism occurred, many of the Levites were driven out of the northern kingdom and joined the southern kingdom (Judah), and also some of the godly of the tribes left the northern kingdom and joined Judah. Some see that many of the tribe of Simeon joined the land of Judah, especially since their portion in the Promised Land was near the land of Judah.
The sons of Simeon were, Nemuel, and Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul: [24]

The lands of the tribes of Reuben and Simeon lie in the south, therefore the two tribes were occupied with the political life of Judah, and the lists of the genealogies of the sons of Simeon came right after the kingdom of Judah.

entries.section: 2. The genealogies of the sons of Simeon

paragraphs.text: Shallum his son, Mibsam his son, Mishma his son. [25]
Shallum or Shallumi: a Hebrew name meaning "in peace."
Mishma: a Hebrew name meaning "report," the name of a son of Simeon (1 Chr 4:25).
Mibsam: a Hebrew name meaning "sweet fragrance," a son of Simeon (1 Chr 4:25).

entries.section: 2. The genealogies of the sons of Simeon

paragraphs.text: And the sons of Mishma; Hamuel his son, Zacchur his son, Shimei his son. [26]
Hamuel: a Hebrew name meaning "zeal of God or wrath of God." He was a Simeonite, a son of Mishma, and perhaps of the family of Shaul (1 Chr 4:26).
Zacchur: a Hebrew name meaning "remembering, attentive." He is a Simeonite who came in the line of Mishma.

entries.section: 2. The genealogies of the sons of Simeon

paragraphs.text: Shimei: (with a kasra on the ayn), a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh hears," he is a Simeonite, who had 16 sons and 6 daughters (1 Chr 4:26-27).
And Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters;
but his brethren had not many children, neither did all their family multiply, like to the children of Judah. [27]

entries.section: 2. The genealogies of the sons of Simeon

paragraphs.text: And they dwelt at Beersheba, and Moladah, and Hazarshual, [28]
Simeon was small in number; their number at the Exodus was 59,300 (Num 1:23), and after forty years they became only 22,200 (Num 26:14).
Moladah: a Hebrew name meaning "birth," inhabited by Shimei of the descendants of Simeon (1 Chr 4:28).
Shual: a Hebrew name meaning "fox."

entries.section: 2. The genealogies of the sons of Simeon

paragraphs.text: And at Bilhah, and at Ezem, and at Tolad, [29]

Ezem or Azem: a Hebrew name meaning "great." It is a village near the border of Edom, from the portion of the sons of Judah, which became part of the portion of Simeon. Perhaps it was Khirbet "Umm al-Azm."
Bilhah: a Hebrew name meaning "foolish or naive," and it is the name of a place in Simeon.
Tolad: a Hebrew name meaning "birth," and it is a city in the south of Judah.

entries.section: 2. The genealogies of the sons of Simeon

paragraphs.text: And at Bethuel, and at Hormah, and at Ziklag, [30]
Hormah: a Hebrew name meaning "devoted place or ruin," and the city of Zephath was called Hormah after its destruction. The Simeonites dwelt in it after it was destroyed.
Ziklag: a city in the extreme south of Judah, which was given after a time to Simeon.
Bethuel: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "house of God." The name of a place that was in the portion of Simeon.

entries.section: 2. The genealogies of the sons of Simeon

paragraphs.text: And at Bethmarcaboth, and Hazarsusim, and at Bethbirei, and at Shaaraim.
These were their cities unto the reign of David. [31]

Susim: plural of Hazar-susah, a Hebrew name meaning "village of horses." It is a village of the Simeonites. Some thought that its place was the stables of Abu Susin, near Tell al-Fari'a, and it may be Susiyah, which lies at a distance of two miles north of Eshtemoa.
Bethbirei: a Hebrew name meaning "house of my creation," and it is the name of a city in the land of Simeon.
Shaaraim: a Hebrew name meaning "two gates," and it is a city in Simeon.

entries.section: 2. The genealogies of the sons of Simeon

paragraphs.text: And their villages were, Etam, and Ain, Rimmon, and Tochen, and Ashan, five cities: [32]

Ain: a city in Judea, in the southern part of Palestine near Rimmon, which was of the portion of Judah, then given to Simeon, then to the Levites. Perhaps it was Umm al-Ramamin, nine miles northeast of Beersheba.
Rimmon: a Hebrew name meaning "pomegranate." A city in the south of Judah near Ain.
Tochen: a Hebrew name meaning "measure or weight." A city in the possession of the sons of Simeon, whose place is not known now with certainty.
Ashan: a Hebrew name meaning "smoke." It is a town on the coast of Judah, afterward granted to Simeon.

entries.section: 2. The genealogies of the sons of Simeon

paragraphs.text: And all their villages that were round about the same cities, unto Baal.
These were their habitations, and their genealogy. [33]

entries.section: 2. The genealogies of the sons of Simeon

paragraphs.text: And Meshobab, and Jamlech, and Joshah, the son of Amaziah, [34]
Meshobab: a Hebrew name meaning "returned," one of the heads of the sons of Simeon who received pasture near the Arabs, from Gedor (1 Chr 4:34-41).
Jamlech: a Hebrew name meaning "he reigns," and he is a Simeonite chief.
Joshah: he is a Simeonite chief, the son of Amaziah.

entries.section: 2. The genealogies of the sons of Simeon

paragraphs.text: And Joel, and Jehu the son of Joshibiah, the son of Seraiah, the son of Asiel, [35]
Joel: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh is God," and it is the name of a Simeonite chief.
Jehu: a Hebrew name meaning "He is Yahweh," and he is of the descendants of Simeon.

Seraiah: a Hebrew name meaning "God has prevailed." More than one person bears this name: 1. The son of Kenaz and brother of Othniel, and father of Joab the father of the valley of craftsmen (1 Chr 4:13-14). 2. The grandfather of Jehu, who was of the tribe of Simeon (1 Chr 4:35).
Asiel: a Hebrew name meaning "God has made," one of the forefathers of Joel and Jehu, whose names are mentioned in the division and census of the Hebrews (1 Chr 4:35), and he is a "Simeonite."

entries.section: 2. The genealogies of the sons of Simeon

paragraphs.text: And Elioenai, and Jaakobah, and Jeshohaiah, and Asaiah, and Adiel, and Jesimiel, and Benaiah, [36]
Elioenai: a Hebrew name meaning "my eyes are toward Yahweh," the name of a head of a house in the tribe of Simeon.
Jaakobah: a Hebrew name meaning "he takes hold of the heel," and he is a Simeonite chief.
Jeshohaiah: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "he makes him bow down." He is a Simeonite chief.
Asaiah: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh has made," and he is a Simeonite chief in the days of King Hezekiah.
Adiel: a Hebrew name meaning "ornament of God," and he is a man of the sons of Simeon, of the heads of the clans.
Jesimiel: a Hebrew name meaning "God sets up," and he is a chief of the tribe of Simeon.
Benaiah: a Hebrew name meaning "whom Yahweh has built," and he is one of the chiefs of the sons of Simeon.

entries.section: 2. The genealogies of the sons of Simeon

paragraphs.text: And Ziza the son of Shiphi, the son of Allon, the son of Jedaiah, the son of Shimri, the son of Shemaiah; [37]
Shiphi: a Hebrew name meaning "abundant." The father of the prince of the Simeonites in the days of Hezekiah.
Allon: a Hebrew name meaning "oak," and it is the name of a son of Jedaiah of the tribe of Simeon.
Jedaiah: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh does good," a Simeonite from the ancestors of Ziza (1 Chr 4:7).
Shimri: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh guards and preserves," and he is a Simeonite.
Shemaiah: it means "Yahweh hears," and he is a Simeonite.

entries.section: 2. The genealogies of the sons of Simeon

paragraphs.text: These mentioned by their names were princes in their families: and the house of their fathers increased greatly, [38]

entries.section: 2. The genealogies of the sons of Simeon

paragraphs.text: And they went to the entrance of Gedor, even unto the east side of the valley, to seek pasture for their flocks. [39]

entries.section: 2. The genealogies of the sons of Simeon

paragraphs.text: And they found fat pasture and good, and the land was wide, and quiet, and peaceable; for they of Ham had dwelt there of old. [40]
Ham: a Hebrew name meaning "protector, that is, hot, or one who protected with protection."

entries.section: 2. The genealogies of the sons of Simeon

paragraphs.text: And these written by name came in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah,
and smote their tents and the Meunim that were found there, and destroyed them utterly unto this day, and dwelt in their rooms: because there was pasture there for their flocks. [41]
The events recorded here will be clarified in (2 Chr 20).
The Meunim: a tribe of Hamitic origin, whom the sons of Simeon smote in the days of Hezekiah.

entries.section: 2. The genealogies of the sons of Simeon

paragraphs.text: And some of them, even of the sons of Simeon, five hundred men, went to mount Seir, having for their captains Pelatiah, and Neariah, and Rephaiah, and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi. [42]
Pelatiah: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh has set free," and it is the name of a Simeonite chief. He entered a war in which the tribe of Simeon was victorious over the Amalekites (1 Chr 4:42-43).
Neariah: a Hebrew name meaning "bearer of the shield of Yahweh," and he is one of the sons of Simeon, chief of a tribe, who went to Mount Seir to fight the Amalekites in the days of King Hezekiah.
Rephaiah: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh has healed," and he is a commander of the sons of Simeon, who lived in the days of Hezekiah.

Ishi: a Hebrew name meaning "savior." More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. A man of Judah, the father of Zoheth (1 Chr 4:20). 2. A Simeonite, whose sons walked at the head of a band, and attacked the Amalekites in Mount Seir, seized their settlement, and dwelt in it.

entries.section: 2. The genealogies of the sons of Simeon

paragraphs.text: And they smote the rest of the Amalekites that were escaped, and dwelt there unto this day. [43]
They smote the Amalekites who had escaped, after Saul had smitten them (1 Sam 14:48; 15:7-8).
That I may meet You through the people of God
v With every righteous just man or holy woman, I see You manifested, pouring out Your blessings in my depths.
With Jabez, who rose above sorrows and so became, through You, more honorable than his brethren, grant me to enjoy meeting You, and to realize that You are the First and the Last in my life.
There is no blessing I could possess without You, O Source of happiness.
Bless me, that my heart may be enlarged to love the heavenly beings and human beings.
Let every heavenly and human being have a place in my heart.
I love everyone, and so I become, with You, a lover of mankind!
Let Your hand be with me, You work by me and in me and with me!
Accompany me all the days of my sojourning, that evil may have no place in me.
You grant me authority over the devil and all his powers.
v That I may meet You with Othniel, the first of the judges.
You kindle my heart with Your Holy Spirit, so I am filled with strength and wisdom, with peace and joy.
I will not cease to meet with You for the peace of my brethren.
v You give me the spirit of sincere leadership, so pride will not creep into my heart, nor will slackness gain control over me!
In You I strive for the victory of my brethren and their peace.
With every success of theirs I count myself successful.
And with every groan of heart that comes from them my heart groans!
I will not rest until the whole world rests in You.
When shall I see all humanity as a rejoicing procession, passing over to You and cleaving to You eternally?!
v Allow me to cleave to Caleb the son of Jephunneh, to accompany him as I accompany his friend Joshua the son of Nun.
I cross over with them, not to spy out the passing Promised Land, but to set out with You and through You to the heavenly Canaan.
I taste the sweetness of the heavenly life, and carry with them the unique cluster of grapes on a pole.
I carry You, who have become the grape that passes through the winepress alone for my sake.
You carried the staff of the Cross, that the Cross might carry You.
You accepted the shame and disgrace of the Cross, to pour Your surpassing glory upon my depths.
I long to cleave to You as a bride with her bridegroom.
The more I cleave to You, the more my heart opens to humanity.
I love You with all my heart, as though there were no one in it but You.
And lo, I find a place for every person in my depths.
When shall I see all humanity, in the day of Your coming, cleaving to You?!
Yes, hasten, O Lord, to every heart.
