Knock upon it with Your wounded hand, and call every soul to receive You within, so that all may become a holy temple for You!

1 Now the sons of Issachar were, Tola, and Puah, Jashub, and Shimrom, four. 2 And the sons of Tola; Uzzi, and Rephaiah, and Jeriel, and Jahmai, and Jibsam, and Shemuel, heads of their father's house, to wit, of Tola: they were valiant men of might in their generations; whose number was in the days of David two and twenty thousand and six hundred. 3 And the sons of Uzzi; Izrahiah: and the sons of Izrahiah; Michael, and Obadiah, and Joel, Ishiah, five: all of them chief men. 4 And with them, by their generations, after the house of their fathers, were bands of soldiers for war, six and thirty thousand men: for they had many wives and sons. 5 And their brethren among all the families of Issachar were valiant men of might, reckoned in all by their genealogies fourscore and seven thousand.

Jacob likened his son Issachar to a strong ass (Gen 49:14); the tribe of Issachar is constantly at work and finds its delight in its tents (Deut 33:18). Here it is said of them that they multiplied wives and sons [4], and that their clans were mighty men of valour and great in number [5]. The multitude of their number caused them no trouble, because they were creative; there was no idle person among them.
Ben Sira often urges us to work diligently, however old we may be. Among his words are these:
[Do not hate laborious work, nor work in the field which the Most High created] (Sir 7:16).

[Stand in thy covenant, and be occupied therein, and grow old in thy work... Do not say, "What need have I? And what good things shall come to me from now on?"... Do not say, "I have enough for myself; what evil can befall me in the future?"] (Sir 11:21, 25-26).
[The slothful man is like a filthy stone; everyone hisses at his disgrace... The slothful man is like dung; everyone that gathers it shakes his hand from it] (Sir 22:1-2).
v Idleness is the teacher of every sin.

St. John Chrysostom v It befits a Christian not to be without order. Whoever is able to work must not eat the bread of idleness, and whoever is occupied with work, let him do so well, to the glory of Christ[1].

St. Basil the Great v The Apostle says, "That ye study to be quiet," meaning that you should remain in your cell and not be troubled by the rumors that usually arise from the idle and their chatter, so that they are restless and cause restlessness to others[2].

v "Every sluggard shall be clothed with rags and worn-out garments" [(Prov 23:21) Septuagint]... It is certain that the sluggard does not deserve to be adorned with the robe that will not wear out nor decay, of which the Apostle speaks: "Put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ" (Rom 13:14). And also: "putting on the breastplate of faith and love" (1 Thess 5:8), and of which the Lord Himself spoke by the mouth of the prophet, addressing Jerusalem: "Awake, put on thy strength, O Zion" (Isa 52:1). So whoever is overpowered by the sleep of slackness or weariness should be clothed not with his work and toil, but with the rags of sloth[3].
St. John Cassian Now the sons of Issachar were, Tola, and Puah, Jashub, and Shimrom, four. [1]
The details concerning the tribe of Issachar come from (Gen 46:13) and (Num 26:23-25). The numbers given here are slightly higher than those in the census (Num 1; 26).
They were characterized by the following:

a. "They multiplied wives and sons, so the number of fighting men in this tribe kept increasing continually from the founding of the monarchy. In the days of David they were 22,600 men, which increased to 36,000, and in the end reached 87,000.
b. They were careful to register their genealogies [5].
c. The tribes of Issachar, Benjamin and Asher were bound together, so that they became able to go up to war.
Tola: a Hebrew name, meaning "worm or crimson cloth". He was the firstborn of Issachar, the ancestor of the Tolaites.
Puah: a Hebrew name, meaning "madder, or the roots of the dyers". He was a son of Issachar and the forefather of the clan of the Punites (1 Chr 7:1). The name is also written Puvah.
Jashub: a Hebrew name, meaning "he returns". He was one of the sons of Issachar (1 Chr 7:1).
Shimron: a Hebrew name, meaning "watcher or guard". He was the founder of the clan of the Shimronites.
And the sons of Tola:
Uzzi, and Rephaiah, and Jeriel, and Jahmai, and Jibsam, and Shemuel, heads of their father's house, to wit, of Tola: they were valiant men of might in their generations.
Whose number was in the days of David two and twenty thousand and six hundred. [2]
Uzzi: a Hebrew name, meaning "Jehovah is strength". Two bore this name, and they are:
The son of Tola son of Issachar, a head of a house and a mighty man of valour (1 Chr 7:2-3).
The son of Bela, of the sons of Benjamin, and a head of a house (1 Chr 7:7).
Rephaiah: a Hebrew name, meaning "Jehovah has healed". He was a man of the sons of Issachar (1 Chr 7:2).
Jeriel: a Hebrew name, meaning "God sees". He was a man of the sons of Issachar (1 Chr 7:2).
Jahmai: a Hebrew name, meaning "he protects". He was a man of the sons of Issachar (1 Chr 7:2).
Jibsam: a Hebrew name, meaning "God is strength". It is the name of a grown son of the sons of Issachar (1 Chr 7:2).

Shemuel: a Hebrew name, meaning "his name is God". In the Hebrew original this name is the same as the one that appears in the Arabic translations as (Samuel). He was a chief of Issachar of the family of Tola (1 Chr 7:2).
Some think that the word "thousand (eleph)" in the Hebrew mind means a division of the tribe, whatever its number, equivalent to military terms such as battalion, regiment, brigade or company[4].
And the son of Uzzi; Izrahiah: and the sons of Izrahiah; Michael, and Obadiah, and Joel, Ishiah, five.
All of them chief men. [3]
Izrahiah: a Hebrew name, meaning "Jehovah shines". He was a head of Issachar and a son of Uzzi (1 Chr 7:3).
Michael: a Hebrew name, meaning "Who is like God". He was a head of Issachar in the days of David.
Obadiah: a Hebrew name, meaning "servant of Jehovah". He was the son of Izrahiah son of Uzzi, of the descendants of Tola, a head of a house in Issachar (1 Chr 7:3).
Joel: a Hebrew name, meaning "Jehovah is God". It is the name of one of the offspring of Issachar (1 Chr 7:3).
Ishiah: a Hebrew name, meaning "Jehovah forgets". He was a man of Issachar of the house of Tola.
And with them, by their generations, after the house of their fathers, were bands of soldiers for war, six and thirty thousand men: for they had many wives and sons. [4]
And their brethren among all the families of Issachar were valiant men of might, reckoned in all by their genealogies fourscore and seven thousand. [5]

Issachar: a Hebrew name, meaning "he works for hire". He was the ninth son of Jacob, and the fifth from Leah. Jacob's prophecy concerning him was fulfilled, for the people of Issachar toiled in the labours of farming. Nomadic tribes used to raid it. In the census in the days of David their number was eighty-seven thousand (1 Chr 7:5).

6 The sons of Benjamin; Bela, and Becher, and Jediael, three. 7 And the sons of Bela; Ezbon, and Uzzi, and Uzziel, and Jerimoth, and Iri, five; heads of the house of their fathers, mighty men of valour; and were reckoned by their genealogies twenty and two thousand and thirty and four. 8 And the sons of Becher; Zemira, and Joash, and Eliezer, and Elioenai, and Omri, and Jerimoth, and Abiah, and Anathoth, and Alameth. All these are the sons of Becher. 9 And the number of them, after their genealogy by their generations, heads of the house of their fathers, mighty men of valour, was twenty thousand and two hundred. 10 And the son of Jediael; Bilhan: and the sons of Bilhan; Jeush, and Benjamin, and Ehud, and Chenaanah, and Zethan, and Tharshish, and Ahishahar. 11 All these the sons of Jediael, by the heads of their fathers, mighty men of valour, were seventeen thousand and two hundred soldiers, fit to go out for war and battle. 12 Shuppim also, and Huppim, the children of Ir, and Hushim, the son of Aher.
Although this tribe grew weak, its number becoming 600 men because of its folly (Judg 20:46-48), it seems that it grew strong again and increased in size.

In this chapter he focused on Benjamin with regard to his relationship with the people, whereas in the next chapter he spoke of Benjamin in his relationship with Saul and Jerusalem. It was said of Benjamin that he is a wolf that ravens (Gen 49:27), and perhaps Jacob here points to Saul son of Kish the Benjamite, who became the first king of Israel and was not faithful to God, so he tyrannized over the people and devoured them like a wolf attacking lambs, instead of caring for them as a father who looks after his children. Yet many of the men of valour who were around him, being Benjamites, were drawn to David and showed him all loyalty and devotion (1 Chr 12), and when the kingdom was split, Benjamin joined Judah in the southern kingdom, or the kingdom of Judah. David did not shut the door in the face of the tribe of Benjamin because of the actions of King Saul, but won his son Jonathan to his side, and won many men of valour.
v Among those who oppose us most strongly are people appointed to be our friends.

St. Augustine v By loving a person who is your enemy you become a friend of God; in truth not only His friend but also His son, as the Lord Himself says: "Love your enemies... do good to them that hate you... [This proves that you are the sons of your Father in heaven]" (cf. Mt 5:44-45)[5].

Father Caesarius, Bishop of Arles v When he says "Be kindly affectioned one to another" (Rom 12:10), he means, be friends and be warm as well. Do not wait for others to love you, but leap toward them yourself and be the one who begins. By this you also reap the reward of their love. He showed why we must love one another and told us of the way in which steadfast affection is kindled, when he added, saying: "in honour preferring one another" (Rom 12:10). This is the way that produces affection, and in which affection dwells once it has been produced. Nothing creates friends like zealously striving to honour one's neighbor.
v It is no small effort; it requires an active soul and a great mind for us to endure separation from a person whom we love in Christ.

St. John Chrysostom Some think that what is mentioned here about the tribe of Benjamin [6-11] came by an error in copying, the word "Benjamin" being copied instead of "son of Zebulun," and in one of the Greek manuscripts "Zebulun" appears instead of Benjamin. Moreover, no mention of Zebulun has come in 1 Chronicles unless the text here is about him.

Also, as stated in (Gen 49:13), Zebulun is situated on the seashore below Phoenicia; this fact seems to be reflected in the mention of Tharshish [10], which is the name of an ancient port (Cadiz), where ships came from the western side of the Mediterranean Sea (Spain)[6].
The sons of Benjamin; Bela, and Becher, and Jediael, three. [6]
Bela: a Hebrew name, meaning "swallowing or the ark".
Becher: a Hebrew name, meaning "the firstborn, that is, the first and the early one".
Jediael: a Hebrew name, meaning "known in God". He was a Benjamite and the head of a clan (1 Chr 7:6, 10, 11).
And the sons of Bela; Ezbon, and Uzzi, and Uzziel, and Jerimoth, and Iri, five.
Heads of the house of their fathers, mighty men of valour; and were reckoned by their genealogies twenty and two thousand and thirty and four. [7]
Ezbon: a Hebrew name; the meaning of this name is not known with certainty, and it is the name of a son of Bela son of Benjamin (1 Chr 7:7).
Jerimoth: a Hebrew name, meaning "swollen or huge or tall". Two bore this name, and they are:
A Benjamite, son of Bela (1 Chr 7:7).
A Benjamite, son of Becher (1 Chr 7:8).
Iri: a Hebrew name, meaning "watchman". He was a son of Bela, of the sons of Benjamin. He was also called Ir.
And the sons of Becher; Zemira, and Joash, and Eliezer, and Elioenai, and Omri, and Jerimoth, and Abiah, and Anathoth, and Alameth.
All these are the sons of Becher. [8]
Zemira: a Hebrew name, meaning "a song, or an elegant beardless youth, or small in size," and he was a man of the descendants of Benjamin (1 Chr 7:8).
Joash: a Hebrew name, meaning "Jehovah has come to aid". He was the name of a son of Becher, and a head of a Benjamite clan in the days of David (1 Chr 7:8).
Eliezer: a Hebrew name, meaning "God is help". He was a chief of the sons of Benjamin (1 Chr 7:8).
Elioenai: a Hebrew name, meaning "my eyes are toward Jehovah". It is the name of a head of a house in the tribe of Benjamin.
Omri: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "prosperous". He was a son of Becher, of the sons of Benjamin.
Abiah: a Hebrew name, meaning "the Lord is father or the Lord is my father".
Anathoth: a Canaanite name, the plural of "Anath". He was the son of Becher the Benjamite and a head of a house in his tribe.
Alameth: a Hebrew name, meaning "concealment". He was a son of Becher of Benjamin (1 Chr 7:8).
And the number of them, after their genealogy by their generations, heads of the house of their fathers, mighty men of valour, was twenty thousand and two hundred. [9]

They were careful to register their genealogies [9], besides their strong and constant attachment to the tribe of Judah. When the kingdom was split and they set up a separate kingdom, the tribe of Benjamin did not join them, but clung to Judah and never separated from it.
They point to those who cling to the Lion that came out of the tribe of Judah, our Lord Jesus Christ.
And the son of Jediael; Bilhan: and the sons of Bilhan;
Jeush, and Benjamin, and Ehud, and Chenaanah, and Zethan, and Tharshish, and Ahishahar. [10]
Bilhan: it means "his night, or inexperienced". He is the name of a chief of Benjamin of the clan of Jediael (1 Chr 7:10).
Jeush: a Hebrew name, meaning "he helps". A head of a house of Benjamin in the days of David (1 Chr 7:10).
Benjamin: a Hebrew name, meaning "son of the right hand, or son of the right," and he was a chief (1 Chr 7:10).
Ehud: a Hebrew name, perhaps an abbreviation of the name Abihud, and he was a son of Bilhan of the tribe of Benjamin.
Chenaanah: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "toward Canaan". He was a Benjamite, of the descendants of Jediael.
Zethan: a Hebrew name, meaning "olive tree," and he was a head of Benjamin (1 Chr 7:10).
Tharshish: a Phoenician name, meaning "a refinery". He was a man of the sons of Benjamin, son of Bilhan.
Ahishahar: it means "brother of the dawn or the daybreak". He was the son of Bilhan son of Jediael son of Benjamin.
All these the sons of Jediael, by the heads of their fathers, mighty men of valour, were seventeen thousand and two hundred soldiers, fit to go out for war and battle. [11]
Shuppim also, and Huppim, the children of Ir, and Hushim, the son of Aher. [12]
Shuppim or Shupham or Shephuphan: a Hebrew name, meaning "serpent". He was the son of a Benjamite, the head of the clan of the Shuphamites.
Huppim or Hupham: a Hebrew name, the meaning of which is not known, and he was a son, or a distant grandson, of Benjamin and the founder of a clan in that tribe (1 Chr 7:12, 15).

Hushim: a Hebrew name, meaning "haste, agitation". He was a Benjamite, a head of a clan, the son of Aher. Some think that it refers to the tribe of Dan, instead of what is said of him in (Gen 46:23) that he was the son of Dan[7].
Aher: a Hebrew name, meaning "another". It is the name of a Benjamite man (1 Chr 7:12).
The sons of Naphtali; Jahziel, and Guni, and Jezer, and Shallum, the sons of Bilhah. [13]

Only the first generation of the fathers of this tribe is mentioned. None of their descendants is mentioned; perhaps the records of their sons were lost. His father Jacob likens him, in his love of freedom, to a hind let loose in an open wilderness and in the valley without obstacles, moving lightly and swiftly wherever she wishes. For he says of him: "Naphtali is a hind let loose (a female deer): he giveth goodly words" (Gen 49:21).

But this freedom was not an opportunity for dissoluteness and evil; rather, the tribe kept good relations with the rest of the tribes, offering "goodly words". And in the Book of Judges Deborah sang, saying: "Zebulun and Naphtali were a people that jeoparded their lives unto the death in the high places of the field" (Judg 5:18), perhaps pointing to the extent of their striving in war. Moses the prophet blessed them before his death: "O Naphtali, satisfied with favour, and full with the blessing of the LORD: possess thou the west and the south" (Deut 33:23)... Thus Naphtali became a type of the gentle soul in its dealings with its brethren, enjoying the blessing of the Lord[8].

v We do not consider as free those who are free by their position, but those who are truly free in their life and nature... The freedom of the soul and its blessedness are the result of true purity and contempt for temporal things[9].
v The free man is he whom pleasures do not enslave, but who governs the body with good discernment and chastity, content with what God gives, however little, thanking Him with all his heart[10].

St. Anthony The following is observed in this tribe: 1. One of them married a Syrian or Aramean concubine [14]. 2. "Machir" came as the fruit of this marriage; and this son learned from his father's mistake and married a Benjamite girl [15].

Naphtali, the son of Bilhah: the book showed no interest in his genealogy [13]; his lineage is rarely mentioned, and the number of his fighting men is small. The list of Naphtali agrees with what is in (Gen 46:24); (Num 26:48).
Jahziel: a Hebrew name, meaning "God divides," and he was the firstborn of Naphtali (1 Chr 7:13).
Guni: a Hebrew name, meaning "anointed or light red". He was the founder of the clan of the Gunites.
Shallum: a Hebrew name, meaning "recompense". He is also called Shillem, which means "the Lord has made a recompense".
Jezer: a Hebrew name, meaning "he created, he purposed". He was one of the sons of Naphtali, and the head of a clan.
Bilhah: a Hebrew name, meaning "simple-minded or unwary".

14 The sons of Manasseh; Ashriel, whom his concubine the Aramitess bare; she bare Machir the father of Gilead. 15 And Machir took to wife the sister of Huppim and Shuppim, whose name was Maachah. And the name of his second son was Zelophehad: and Zelophehad had daughters. 16 And Maachah the wife of Machir bare a son, and she called his name Peresh; and the name of his brother was Sheresh; and his sons were Ulam and Rakem. 17 And the son of Ulam; Bedan. These were the sons of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh. 18 And his sister Hammoleketh bare Ishod, and Abiezer, and Mahalah. 19 And the sons of Shemida were, Ahian, and Shechem, and Likhi, and Aniam.
The descendants of Manasseh who were east of the Jordan, in Gilead and Bashan, were spoken of earlier (1 Chr 5:23-24). Here the talk is of those who lived in Canaan, west of the Jordan.
Of the descendants of Manasseh was Zelophehad, who had no son, but all his offspring were daughters, so they claimed their right to the inheritance (Josh 17:3).
The sons of Manasseh; Ashriel, whom his concubine the Aramitess bare.
She bare Machir the father of Gilead. [14]
The list of Manasseh includes both sides of the tribe, and points to the relationship with Syria.

It is clear that some Hebrew women also became wives of Syrian rulers. The list indicates that the half-tribe of Manasseh that was living on the east bank of the Jordan became something like a political extension of Syria, and suffered the same fate as Syria when the army of Tiglath-pileser appeared in 734 BC[11].

It is noted in these few verses [14-19] that the genealogies refer to women, because of the devastation that befell Israel in the period of the captivity. Thirteen women are mentioned here, among them the five daughters of Zelophehad [15].

Ashriel or Israel: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "God strives". He was a son of Gilead of the tribe of Manasseh, head of the house of the Israelites. Here his name appears in the Arabic as "Ashriel," but in the Hebrew it is "Israel".
And Machir took to wife the sister of Huppim and Shuppim, whose name was Maachah.
And the name of his second son was Zelophehad: and Zelophehad had daughters. [15]
Machir: a Hebrew name, meaning "purchaser". It is the name of the firstborn of Manasseh, and his only son by an Aramean concubine.
Maachah: a Semitic name meaning "zalam". The name of a woman of the descendants of Benjamin who married Machir son of Manasseh.
Zelophehad: a Hebrew name, meaning "shadow against fear, that is, protection from fear".
Zelophehad was the son of Hepher son of Gilead son of Machir son of Manasseh (Josh 17:3).

The daughters of Zelophehad have special importance, since they had no brother, and it was feared that the family name would be blotted out, so they claimed their father's inheritance before Moses and Eleazar the high priest and before the princes and all the congregation by the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, and boldly asked that their father's name not be taken away because he had no son. And the Law came giving the right to daughters to inherit from their fathers as long as they had no brother to raise up his father's name (Num 27:1-11). It was judged that the females should inherit if there was no heir other than they among the males, on condition that they not marry outside their tribe, so that the inheritance would not pass to another tribe.
The daughters of Zelophehad are mentioned five times in the Bible (Num 26:33; 27:1-11; 36:3-12; Josh 17:3-6; 1 Chr 7:15).
Their names are: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah (Num 26:33).

These daughters acknowledged that their father, although he did not take part in the company of Korah, yet died in the wilderness in his own sin, and he died and had no sons (Num 27:3). Yet they wanted their father's name to remain.

As true daughters of Israel who value their genealogies, they asked Moses to bring their cause before the Lord, and indeed the Lord answered their petition because of their zeal. And He made of their petition a statute of judgment for the children of Israel.
In (Num 36) the whole tribe of Manasseh is seen interceding on their behalf.

So it is fitting for the believer to marry from his own tribe, that is, from the daughters of God, or for believing women to marry the sons of God, so that believers do not lose their heavenly inheritance.
Indeed they married their cousins, and they asked Joshua to receive his portion as the Lord commanded.
v Hear, O penitent, do not delay your return, for you gladden the Father and the inheritance that awaits you.
The Father does not wait for you to offer Him a petition, but only wants you to return so that He may receive you.
The petition does not pay the bond of your debt; mercies will come forth and receive you if you repent.
Supplication cannot wipe out your iniquity, but tenderness walks the road by itself without your asking.
What you lack is to remind yourself of your stumblings, and the mercies of the Father take the place of all these (things) and you are made perfect.
Behold, Baptism gives you the robe of glory, and behold, faith is the king's ring on your hand.
The fatted calf of life has been slain for you that you may delight spiritually; all these things are yours, and you alone refrain from returning[12].
St. Mar Jacob of Serugh
And Maachah the wife of Machir bare a son, and she called his name Peresh; and the name of his brother was Sheresh; and his sons were Ulam and Rakem. [16]
Peresh: a Hebrew name, meaning "separation, distinction, dung". He was a son of Machir son of Manasseh (1 Chr 7:16).
Sheresh: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "root or shoot". In the family of Machir, of the line of Manasseh.
Ulam: a Hebrew name, meaning "first". He was a son of Peresh of the tribe of Manasseh (1 Chr 7:16-17).
Rakem: a Hebrew name, meaning "embroidering, shaping, colouring". He was a man of the descendants of Manasseh.
And the son of Ulam; Bedan.
These were the sons of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh. [17]
Bedan: perhaps he is the same Bedan referred to as one of the deliverers of Israel (1 Sam 12:11).
And his sister Hammoleketh bare Ishod, and Abiezer, and Mahalah. [18]

Hammoleketh: a Hebrew name, meaning "the queen". She was the sister of Gilead, and the daughter of Machir son of Manasseh, and she was the mother of Ishod, Abiezer and Mahalah [this is (1 Chr 7:17-18)]. Her sons had importance in the history of the Hebrews.
Ishod: a Hebrew name, meaning "man of splendour". He was a man of the tribe of Manasseh, and his mother was Hammoleketh.

Abiezer: a Hebrew name, meaning "father of help or father of aid or the father is help". He was the father of a clan of importance, from which came Gideon the judge who delivered Israel from the Midianites (Judg 6-8).
Mahalah: a Hebrew name, meaning "sickness". It is the name of a man of the tribe of Manasseh, the son of the sister of Gilead.
And the sons of Shemida were, Ahian, and Shechem, and Likhi, and Aniam. [19]
Shemida: a Hebrew name, meaning "the name will know". Of Manasseh. A head of the clan of the Shemidaites.
Ahian: a Hebrew name, meaning "my brother or a little brother". A man of the tribe of Manasseh of the clan of Shemida.
Shechem: a Hebrew name, meaning "shoulder, or the point of the shoulder". He is the son of Shemida, a man of Manasseh.
Likhi: of the descendants of Manasseh and the family of Shemida (1 Chr 7:19).
Aniam: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "I am an uncle, or a lament of the people". A son of Shemida of Manasseh.

20 And the sons of Ephraim; Shuthelah, and Bered his son, and Tahath his son, and Eladah his son, and Tahath his son, 21 And Zabad his son, and Shuthelah his son, and Ezer, and Elead, whom the men of Gath that were born in that land slew, because they came down to take away their cattle. 22 And Ephraim their father mourned many days, and his brethren came to comfort him. 23 And when he went in to his wife, she conceived, and bare a son, and he called his name Beriah, because it went evil with his house. 24 And his daughter was Sherah, who built Beth-horon the nether, and the upper, and Uzzen-sherah. 25 And Rephah was his son, and Resheph, and Telah his son, and Tahan his son, 26 Laadan his son, Ammihud his son, Elishama his son, 27 Non his son, Jehoshuah his son. 28 And their possessions and habitations were, Beth-el and the towns thereof, and eastward Naaran, and westward Gezer, with the towns thereof; Shechem also and the towns thereof, unto Gaza and the towns thereof: 29 And by the borders of the children of Manasseh, Beth-shean and her towns, Taanach and her towns, Megiddo and her towns, Dor and her towns. In these dwelt the children of Joseph the son of Israel.

We read of great things for the tribe of Ephraim when it reached maturity. Through the genealogies of Ephraim the writer brought out the position of Joshua son of Nun [27], who was the most prominent person in this huge tribe and was a type of the person of Jesus Christ in many respects [20-29]. In this section we find the only woman of whom the Bible says that she built a city [24][13].
And the sons of Ephraim; Shuthelah, and Bered his son, and Tahath his son, and Eladah his son, and Tahath his son [20]
Shuthelah: two bore this name, and they are: 1. A son of Ephraim, and the founder of the clan of the Shuthalhites (1 Chr 7:20). 2. Another of the descendants of Ephraim (1 Chr 7:21).

Bered: when the clouds suddenly pass into a very cold current, their pieces turn into frozen ice. Sometimes hail is a drizzle, because freezing overtakes the droplets of water falling as rain. And sometimes the pieces grow large, harming man, animals and crops.
Tahath: a Hebrew name, meaning "what is beneath". Two bore this name, and they are:
An Ephraimite, the son of Bered, of the clan of Shuthelah (1 Chr 7:20).
The son of Eladah, of the descendants of Tahath son of Bered (1 Chr 7:20).
Eladah: a Hebrew name, meaning "whom God has adorned". He was the son of Tahath of the tribe of Ephraim.
And Zabad his son, and Shuthelah his son, and Ezer, and Elead, whom the men of Gath that were born in that land slew, because they came down to take away their cattle. [21]

The Bible does not refer to this event elsewhere, and opinions differ concerning it; we mention the following: 1. Some think that this event took place at the beginning of the tribe of Ephraim in Egypt, and that what happened was in the days of Ephraim himself, the son of Joseph. Others think that Ephraim here means another person of the same tribe, and that those who were killed were descendants of Ephraim, and not his direct sons. 2. Who were those who began the aggression against the other side? Some think that the sons of Ephraim thought that the time had come for the fulfilment of the divine promise, so they went down to Gath and plundered them in order to possess Canaan. And God allowed the men of Gath to kill them, because they moved rashly, in haste, and did not consult the Lord, nor wait for the time appointed by Him. Therefore the men of Gath executed judgment on them and killed them.

It is clear that the sons of Ephraim were shepherds of sheep in Goshen and had no military experience, so it is hard to imagine that they went down to Gath to plunder them. Rather, the people of Gath came to Egypt and killed the sons of Ephraim in order to drive away their cattle.
Later God gave the faithful men of Benjamin to drive out the inhabitants of Gath (1 Chr 8:13).

This tree of the tribe of Ephraim grew, and the divine promise on the lips of Jacob was fulfilled for them: "But his younger brother (Ephraim) shall be greater than he (than Manasseh), and his seed shall become a multitude of nations" (Gen 48:19).
Zabad: a Hebrew name, meaning "God has given, or a gift". He was an Ephraimite whom the men of Gath killed when he tried to steal their cattle (1 Chr 7:21).
Ezer: a Hebrew name, meaning "help". A son of Ephraim. He was killed in an attack on the Philistines.
Gath: a Hebrew name, meaning "winepress".
Most likely those whom the men of Gath killed were Ezer and Elead and their servants. And their father Ephraim mourned many days.
And Ephraim their father mourned many days, and his brethren came to comfort him. [22]

Nothing grieves the heart of the aged father like the death of his sons, especially if the death comes by the shedding of their blood; therefore it is said: "And Ephraim their father mourned many days".

When the sons of Ephraim were killed, their father mourned many days and was not comforted, so his brethren came to comfort him, as Job's friends did when his sons and daughters died. Man's consolations are powerless and deficient, as Job said to his friends: "miserable comforters are ye all" (Job 16:2).

Most likely they comforted him with Jacob's blessing of him, when he laid his right hand on his head, and refused to move it to the head of Manasseh, the elder brother. He assured Joseph that his seed would become a multitude of nations (Gen 48:19).
And when he went in to his wife, she conceived, and bare a son, and he called his name Beriah, because it went evil with his house. [23]
God gave Ephraim a son, and although the birth of the son gave him some relative comfort, his affliction was very harsh, so he called the newborn Beriah.

Beriah: a Hebrew name, meaning[14] "in trouble or a gift". There are four persons in the Bible who bear this name. Moreover, in God's gift of a son to him, He did not give him on behalf of those whom he thought he had lost. No person takes the place of another, but each person has his unique personality, gifts and mission. Therefore when God restored to Job double what he had lost, He did not give him double the sons and daughters who had died, because they exist and are not lost!

Among the mistaken phrases that some often repeat in the case of the death of a son or daughter is: "May the Lord compensate you for him or for her." God compensates us for what we lose of possessions or honour, but those who have fallen asleep we do not lose, such that the Lord should compensate us for them with others.
And his daughter was Sherah, who built Beth-horon the nether, and the upper, and Uzzen-sherah. [24]

Beth-horon the upper: it is a Hebrew name, meaning "house of the cave". This name is given to two villages situated on the borders of Ephraim and Benjamin, twelve miles north of Jerusalem, and they were also called Upper Beth-horon and Lower Beth-horon. It is inferred from this that the one was built on high ground and the other on low ground.
Sherah: a Hebrew name, meaning "kinswoman". The daughter of Ephraim, who built Lower and Upper Beth-horon and Uzzen-sherah (1 Chr 7:24).

Uzzen-sherah: a Hebrew name, meaning "portion of Sherah". It is the name of a village built by Sherah, the daughter of a man in Ephraim whose name was also Ephraim (1 Chr 7:24). It is mentioned together with Lower and Upper Beth-horon. Its place is "Beit Sira", three miles southwest of Lower Beth-horon.
And Rephah was his son, and Resheph, and Telah his son, and Tahan his son [25]
Rephah: a Hebrew name, meaning "wealth". He was a man of the descendants of Ephraim (1 Chr 7:25).
Resheph: a Hebrew name, meaning "flame". He was a man of the descendants of Ephraim (1 Chr 7:25).
Telah: a Hebrew name, meaning "a wound or a fracture". He was a man of the sons of Ephraim, probably from the line of Beriah (1 Chr 7:25).
Tahan: a Hebrew name, meaning "camp". He was a man of the sons of Ephraim and the founder of a tribe.
Laadan his son, Ammihud his son, Elishama his son [26]
Laadan: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "fat of neck". It is the name of an Ephraimite, among the ancestors of Joshua.
Ammihud: a Hebrew name, meaning "my uncle is majestic". He was the father of Elisha, the grandfather of Joshua, a head of the sons of Ephraim in the wandering of the children of Israel (1 Chr 7:26).

Elishama: a Hebrew name, meaning "God has heard". He was the son of Ammihud, and one of the heads of Ephraim at the beginning of their journeying in the wilderness. He was one of the ancestors of Joshua (1 Chr 7:26).
Non his son, Jehoshuah his son. [27]
Nun: a Hebrew name, meaning "fish". He was of the sons of Ephraim (1 Chr 7:27).
Jehoshua or Joshua son of Nun: a Hebrew name, meaning "Jehovah is salvation". He was an eyewitness of God's work with Moses and Aaron during the plagues in Egypt and the exodus from it.

He was a disciple of Moses the prophet, his special assistant throughout the period of the wilderness. He took over the leadership after him (Josh 1:1). God is the One who raised him up as successor to Moses (Num 27:18-23). He brought the people into the Promised Land and drove out the pagans. He most likely points to Jesus Christ who alone opens for us the gates of heaven, brings us into the heavenly Canaan, and has given us the right of eternal inheritance.

Moses chose him with the rest of the spies who entered the Promised Land; he returned with Caleb son of Jephunneh, both of them instilling the spirit of hope in the people, unlike the rest of the spies who stirred up terror among the people.
He divided the Promised Land, and received his own portion after the tribes had received theirs, for the living, successful leader gives priority to others.
v Joshua son of Nun the righteous, who became a perfect disciple of the great Teacher (Moses), was also beautiful.
He also wanted love of life to triumph in him, and to draw near to God in perfection.
He kept purity while serving in the tabernacle of time (the tabernacle of the congregation), and became for the people a second Moses before God.
He fought to establish the word of the Lord among the peoples, and the mighty works he did made known how exalted his beauty was[15].
v Come and behold all the public beauty of Joshua son of Nun: the mighty deeds and great and astonishing works that were done.
When he cried out to the swift river and stopped its flowing, and its floods stood as though in an alley without flowing.
When he cleaved the river, and crossed as though on dry land, and led the forces behind him with great wonder (Josh 3:17).
When he fought against famous Jericho, and shouted with a voice at the high walls, and they fell before him (Josh 6:2).
When he prevailed over the kings of the Amorites, and the Lord arrayed Himself with him to destroy them (Josh 2:10).
When he commanded the height and it obeyed him, and sent him hailstones to stone the Canaanites (Josh 10:11).
When he commanded the sun, and it veiled its great power, and the moon heard his word and stopped in its course (Josh 10:13).
When he directed his voice to the galaxy, full of speed, and stopped it, and it stopped and the world ceased from its ordering[16].
St. Mar Jacob of Serugh
And their possessions and habitations were,
Beth-el and the towns thereof, and eastward Naaran, and westward Gezer, with the towns thereof; Shechem also and the towns thereof, unto Gaza and the towns thereof: [28]
Naaran: a town in Ephraim (1 Chr 7:28). It is called today Ain Duq. It is in the Jordan Valley, five miles north of Jericho.
Gezer: a Hebrew name, meaning "portion or dowry of the bride".
Gaza, which is not the Gaza known today in the far south and west, because the portion of Ephraim did not extend to the south, but rather the portion of Judah.

And by the borders of the children of Manasseh, Beth-shean and her towns, Taanach and her towns, Megiddo and her towns, Dor and her towns. In these dwelt the children of Joseph the son of Israel. [29]

Beth-shean: a Hebrew name, meaning "house of quiet". A city five miles to the west of the Jordan River. It first belonged to the tribe of Issachar, and was finally attached to the possessions of the tribe of Manasseh (1 Chr 7:29). After the captivity it became the capital of the ten cities, and was called Scythopolis.

Taanach: a Canaanite name, meaning "sandy land". It was a city of the Canaanites mentioned around 1600 BC, when Thutmose III advanced against Megiddo. Its king was defeated and Joshua son of Nun slew him. It lies within the borders of Issachar, but was given to Manasseh (1 Chr 7:29).
Megiddo: a city of Manasseh, within the borders of Issachar, formerly a royal city of the Canaanites, which Joshua conquered with its towns (1 Chr 7:29).
Dor: a Canaanite name, meaning "dwelling".

entries.section: 6. Asher who enjoys the oil of grace

paragraphs.text: 30 The sons of Asher; Imnah, and Isuah, and Ishuai, and Beriah, and Serah their sister. 31 And the sons of Beriah; Heber, and Malchiel, who is the father of Birzavith. 32 And Heber begat Japhlet, and Shomer, and Hotham, and Shua their sister. 33 And the sons of Japhlet; Pasach, and Bimhal, and Ashvath. These are the children of Japhlet. 34 And the sons of Shamer; Ahi, and Rohgah, Jehubbah, and Aram. 35 And the sons of his brother Helem; Zophah, and Imna, and Shelesh, and Amal. 36 The sons of Zophah; Suah, and Harnepher, and Shual, and Beri, and Imrah, 37 Bezer, and Hod, and Shamma, and Shilshah, and Ithran, and Beera. 38 And the sons of Jether; Jephunneh, and Pispah, and Ara. 39 And the sons of Ulla; Arah, and Haniel, and Rezia. 40 All these were the children of Asher, heads of their father's house, choice and mighty men of valour, chief of the princes. And the number throughout the genealogy of them that were apt to the war and to battle was twenty and six thousand men.

His father Jacob prophesied of him an abundance of good things, as Moses prophesied of him that he would "dip his foot in oil" (Deut 33:24), and both prophecies were fulfilled, for the tribe of Asher enjoyed a fertile land rich in olive trees from which oil is extracted. The yield of his land was plentiful, so it was said that his bread is fat, and he exported from it to the other tribes, besides his dwelling beside the sea, which enabled him to import goods and sell them to the rest of the tribes. This tribe points to the abundance of grace in the lives of the spiritual strugglers.
His portion, geographically, was in a location considered farther from Jerusalem than the rest of the tribes. The men of Asher, like Benjamin, were "mighty men of valour".
v May Your grace, O Lord, be the living Spirit, and the harpist who plays upon my strings, to bring forth a melody for Your sake, Your teaching[17].

v Grace has an eternal home, and she is a compassionate mother who cares for him, as a mother cares for her child, and she cannot leave him, because a woman does not leave her unborn child. And the child thinks that there is no other woman in the world but the one who nurses him. So the soul that loves God thinks of Him as its place... Wherever the true Christian is found, he dwells in God, and God dwells in him[18].

v Grace became a mother for the earth.. so she besought the Lord, saying: Enough of this madness for the earth! Come down and save it from error. The petition of grace entered before the divine Majesty, who sent the compassionate Physician to the sick[19].

v Grace - the mother of mercies - built the world, and she carries it; if she left it, it would fall. The hen spreads her wings over her chicks to gather them, to cherish them and to keep them. She sketches a type of the divinity that spread its mercies over the creatures like two wings, and protected them[20].
St. Mar Jacob of Serugh The sons of Asher; Imnah, and Isuah, and Ishuai, and Beriah, and Serah their sister. [30]
Imnah: a Hebrew name, meaning "good fortune, success". He was the firstborn of Asher and the head of a tribe (1 Chr 7:30).
Isuah: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "equals". He was the second son of Asher (1 Chr 7:30).
Ishuai: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "equals". He was the third son of Asher (1 Chr 7:30).
Beriah: a Hebrew name, meaning "excellent".

Serah: a Hebrew name, meaning "one who explains". Serah is the daughter of Asher, and it was said that she was the only daughter, and it was also said that she was distinguished by her personality and beauty, and this was the reason her name is mentioned (1 Chr 7:30).

entries.section: 6. Asher who enjoys the oil of grace

paragraphs.text: And the sons of Beriah; Heber, and Malchiel, who is the father of Birzavith. [31]
Heber: a Hebrew name, meaning "fellowship, partner".
Malchiel: a Hebrew name, meaning "God is king". He was a grandson of Asher (1 Chr 7:31).
Birzavith or Birzaith: a Hebrew name, meaning "fountain of the olive". The name of an Asherite man, the son of Malchiel.

entries.section: 6. Asher who enjoys the oil of grace

paragraphs.text: And Heber begat Japhlet, and Shomer, and Hotham, and Shua their sister. [32]
Japhlet: a Hebrew name, meaning "he delivers". He was an Asherite of Heber (1 Chr 7:32-33).
Shomer: a Semitic name, meaning "keeper or guard". He is also called Shamer (1 Chr 7:34).
Hotham: a Hebrew name, meaning "seal or signet ring". He was an Asherite, the son of Heber, of the line of Beriah.
Shua: a Semitic name, meaning "the wealth of Shua," and she was an Asherite woman, the daughter of Heber. The name appeared in the form "Shua".

entries.section: 6. Asher who enjoys the oil of grace

paragraphs.text: And the sons of Japhlet; Pasach, and Bimhal, and Ashvath. These are the children of Japhlet. [33]
Pasach: probably this name is Aramaic, and its meaning is "divider". He was an Asherite man of the line of Beriah.
Bimhal: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "at my leisure". He was a man of the tribe of Asher.
Ashvath: the son of Japhlet, of the descendants of Heber, of the sons of Asher (1 Chr 7:33).

entries.section: 6. Asher who enjoys the oil of grace

paragraphs.text: And the sons of Shamer; Ahi, and Rohgah, Jehubbah, and Aram. [34]
Ahi: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "my brother". Or perhaps it is an abbreviation of "Ahijah". The name of a man of the tribe of Asher appears (1 Chr 7:34).
Rohgah: a Hebrew name, meaning "dust, uproar". He is a head of the sons of Asher and is one of the sons of Shamer.
Jehubbah: a Hebrew name, meaning "he hides". An Asherite chief. This name appears in some copies as "Hubbah".

entries.section: 6. Asher who enjoys the oil of grace

paragraphs.text: And the sons of Helem his brother; Zophah, and Imna, and Shelesh, and Amal. [35]
Helem: a Hebrew name, meaning "strength". Perhaps he was "Hotham" mentioned in (1 Chr 7:32).
Zophah: a Hebrew name, meaning "pitcher or jar". He was a chief of the tribe of Asher.
Imna: a Hebrew name, meaning "he prevents". An Asherite, son of Helem (1 Chr 7:35).
Shelesh: a Hebrew name, meaning "obedient". He was one of the heroes of the tribe of Asher, son of Helem (1 Chr 7:35).
Amal: a Hebrew name, meaning "work". He was a son of Helem, an Asherite, a contemporary of David.

entries.section: 6. Asher who enjoys the oil of grace

paragraphs.text: The sons of Zophah; Suah, and Harnepher, and Shual, and Beri, and Imrah [36]
Suah: a Hebrew name, meaning "sweepings". A son of Zophah of the tribe of Asher (1 Chr 7:36).
Harnepher: perhaps an Egyptian name, meaning "Horus is peace". An Asherite, son of Zophah.
Shual: a Hebrew name, meaning "fox". An Asherite, son of Zophah (1 Chr 7:36).
Imrah: a Hebrew name, meaning "he resists". A man of Asher and son of Zophah (1 Chr 7:36).

entries.section: 6. Asher who enjoys the oil of grace

paragraphs.text: Bezer, and Hod, and Shamma, and Shilshah, and Ithran, and Beera. [37]
Bezer: a Hebrew name, meaning "fortress".
Hod: a Hebrew name, meaning "glory". Of the sons of Asher, and he was the son of Zophah. He was a head of a house, a mighty man of valour and a commander of a division in war (1 Chr 7:37).
Shamma: a Hebrew name, meaning "destruction". He was the son of Zophah, a chief in Asher (1 Chr 7:37).
Shilshah: a Hebrew name, meaning "triple or triangular". He was the son of Zophah, a chief of the Asherites.
Ithran: a Semitic name, meaning "excellence". He is Jether himself (1 Chr 7:38).
Beera: a Hebrew name, meaning "well".

entries.section: 6. Asher who enjoys the oil of grace

paragraphs.text: And the sons of Jether; Jephunneh, and Pispah, and Ara. [38]

Jether: a Hebrew name, meaning "excellence". Two bore this name, and they are: 1. A man whose name was entered in the genealogy of Judah, whose trace disappeared after Ezra (1 Chr 4:17). 2. One of the sons of Asher (1 Chr 7:30, 38). It is likely that he is Ithran son of Zophah (1 Chr 7:37).
Jephunneh: a Hebrew name, meaning "he prepares". An Asherite chief (1 Chr 7:38).
Ara: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "lion". A man among the chiefs in the tribe of Asher (1 Chr 7:38).

entries.section: 6. Asher who enjoys the oil of grace

paragraphs.text: And the sons of Ulla; Arah, and Haniel, and Rezia. [39]
Ulla: a head in a house in Asher (1 Chr 7:39), of the sons of Helem (1 Chr 7:35).
Arah: a Hebrew name, meaning "traveler". The name of a chief of Asher, and he was one of the sons of Ulla.
Haniel: a Hebrew name, meaning "grace of God, tenderness of God". An Asherite, son of Ulla (1 Chr 7:39).
Rezia: a Hebrew name, meaning "delightful". A chief of the sons of Asher (1 Chr 7:39).

entries.section: 6. Asher who enjoys the oil of grace

paragraphs.text: All these were the children of Asher, heads of their father's house, choice and mighty men of valour, chief of the princes. And the number throughout the genealogy of them that were apt to the war and to battle was twenty and six thousand men. [40]
Beyut: a Hebrew name, meaning "owner of a well".

The number of fighting men of the whole tribe cannot be compared with the numbers of fighting men in the other tribes. However, some see that the tribe of Asher was marked by wisdom, for what concerned them was that their heads were chosen and mighty men of valour, and not that the number be large.
Your comforts delight my soul!
v The tribe of Issachar was marked by strength together with diligence in work.
It is no shame to him that his father likened him to an ass.
For he is strong, and does not cease from work.
None of them knows the spirit of idleness and sloth.
I do not ask for a particular work.
But grant me constant faithfulness in my practice of work.
That I may hear Your voice: You have been faithful over a few things, I will make you ruler over many things.
v You do not disdain the work of any person, but You set at Your right hand in Your Kingdom him who is faithful and sincere!
Let me work by Your Holy Spirit, that He may grant me the spirit of faithfulness.
v I will not suffer discouragement because of my position in society or in the Church.
Nor will I fall into pride because of an authority You have given me.
Rather I take pride in faithfulness and sincerity, in love and fellowship.
I take pride in You, O Source of every virtue!
v If King Saul turned into a ravening wolf, by sincere love without hypocrisy David won Jonathan son of Saul.
As he also won many men of valour, kinsmen of Saul.
Grant me, O Lord, to love all humanity.
For You are able to turn ravening wolves into gentle lambs.
Let me trust in Your grace, that it brings forth meat out of the eater, and sweetness out of the harsh.
Grant me not to judge anyone hastily.
For many have become like Your angels in the last moments.
Grant me to imitate You, O Son of David.
So that I may not shut the door of friendship before anyone!
In You I leap with love into the hearts of many, that they may truly become friends to You and to me!
v The brothers of Ephraim could not comfort their brother when his sons were killed.
You gave him a son, not as a compensation for his slain sons.
For they are alive; death does not kill their souls.
v How wonderful! Wild beasts often cooperate with others of their kind.
They cooperate together and support one another.
But the sons of men prey upon one another.
In Your tenderness You did not give us the fangs of lions, lest we destroy one another.
Nor did You grant us the hugeness of elephants, lest we smother one another's breath.
Wild beasts live in peace with their own kind, but man's enemies are those of his own household!
v Grant me, O Lord, true freedom, together with the tribe of Naphtali.
May I soar with the wings of the Spirit as though to heaven.
The ancient serpent cannot leap to swallow me, nor can the love of the world hinder me.
That I may fly to You with my brethren, and that we may all rest in Your divine embrace.
v Grant me, together with the daughters of Zelophehad of the descendants of Manasseh, to claim the eternal inheritance.
Nothing occupies You now except that I settle in Your embrace forever.
v Grant me, together with Joshua son of Nun of the tribe of Ephraim, to hear Your voice: As I was with Moses, so I will be with you.
I will not be disturbed by tribulations, nor confused because of the weak.
For the Church is Your body, through which You cross to Your heavens.
You pour out Your radiance upon her, so that she becomes a wonder and amazement in the eyes of the heavenly ones.
v Let me cleave to You, for Your fatherly embrace radiates warmth in my life.
You pour the oil of Your grace into my depths.
Like a mother to me, You do not leave me in want of anything.
The motherhood of Your grace is wonderful; it embraces every true believer as though he were her only son.
Let Your grace work in me, that I may bear a spirit of tender motherhood toward people!

1 Now Benjamin begat Bela his firstborn, Ashbel the second, and Aharah the third, 2 Nohah the fourth, and Rapha the fifth. 3 And the sons of Bela were, Addar, and Gera, and Abihud, 4 And Abishua, and Naaman, and Ahoah, 5 And Gera, and Shephuphan, and Huram. 6 And these are the sons of Ehud: these are the heads of the fathers of the inhabitants of Geba, and they removed them to Manahath: 7 That is, Naaman, and Ahiah. And Gera, he removed them, and begat Uzza, and Ahihud. 8 And Shaharaim begat children in the country of Moab, after he had sent away his two wives, Hushim and Baara. 9 And he begat of Hodesh his wife, Jobab, and Zibia, and Mesha, and Malcham, 10 And Jeuz, and Shachia, and Mirma. These were his sons, heads of the fathers. 11 And of Hushim he begat Abitub, and Elpaal. 12 And the sons of Elpaal; Eber, and Misham, and Shamer, who built Ono, and Lod, with the towns thereof: 13 Beriah also, and Shema. These were heads of the fathers of the inhabitants of Aijalon, who drove away the inhabitants of Gath. 14 And Ahio, Shashak, and Jeremoth, 15 And Zebadiah, and Arad, and Ader, 16 And Michael, and Ispah, and Joha, the sons of Beriah; 17 And Zebadiah, and Meshullam, and Hezeki, and Heber, 18 Ishmerai also, and Jezliah, and Jobab, the sons of Elpaal; 19 And Jakim, and Zichri, and Zabdi, 20 And Elienai, and Zilthai, and Eliel, 21 And Adaiah, and Beraiah, and Shimrath, the sons of Shimhi; 22 And Ishpan, and Heber, and Eliel, 23 And Abdon, and Zichri, and Hanan, 24 And Hananiah, and Elam, and Antothijah, 25 And Iphedeiah, and Penuel, the sons of Shashak; 26 And Shamsherai, and Shehariah, and Athaliah, 27 And Jaresiah, and Eliah, and Zichri, the sons of Jeroham. 28 These were heads of the fathers, by their generations, chief men. These dwelt in Jerusalem. 29 And at Gibeon dwelt the father of Gibeon; and his wife's name was Maachah: 30 And his firstborn son Abdon, and Zur, and Kish, and Baal, and Nadab, 31 And Gedor, and Ahio, and Zacher. 32 And Mikloth begat Shimeah. And these also dwelt with their brethren in Jerusalem, over against their brethren.
Now Benjamin begat Bela his firstborn, Ashbel the second, and Aharah the third [1]
Bela: a Hebrew name, meaning "swallowing" or "the ark".
Ashbel: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning a form of the name "Eshbaal", and he was a son of Benjamin and the founder of a family bearing his name (1 Chr 8:1).
Aharah: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "follower of the brother", and he was the third son of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:1).
Nohah the fourth, and Rapha the fifth. [2]

Nohah: a Hebrew name, meaning "rest". He was the fourth son of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:2). He did not found a clan as his brothers did. His name is not mentioned among those who accompanied Jacob to Egypt, and perhaps he was born in Egypt.
Rapha: a Hebrew name, meaning "he has healed, that is, God has healed". A man of the descendants of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:2).
And the sons of Bela were, Addar, and Gera, and Abihud [3]

Addar: a Hebrew word, perhaps meaning "breadth or greatness". It is the name of a Benjamite man, son of Bela (1 Chr 8:3). This name appears in some Hebrew and Greek manuscripts as "Ard," and it is likely that this is the correct form.
Gera: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "sojourner with God". The name of a man among the sons of Benjamin, and the name of a grandson of Benjamin son of Bela (1 Chr 8:3, 5, 7).
Abihud: a Hebrew name, meaning "my father is majesty or the Father is majesty". He was the son of Bela, the firstborn of Benjamin.
And Abishua, and Naaman, and Ahoah [4]
Abishua: a Hebrew name, meaning "father of salvation". The name of a Benjamite man of the house of Bela.
Naaman: a Hebrew name, meaning "pleasantness".

Ahoah: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "brotherly". It is the name of a son of Bela of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:4). It is possible that he is the same person mentioned as Ahiah in [7] of the same chapter.
And Gera, and Shephuphan, and Huram. [5]
Shephuphan or Shupham: a Hebrew name, meaning "serpent". He was a Benjamite, head of the clan of the Shuphamites.
Huram: a Phoenician and Hebrew name, meaning "the brother is exalted". A Benjamite, perhaps the son of Bela.
And these are the sons of Ehud.
These are the heads of the fathers of the inhabitants of Geba, and they removed them to Manahath: [6]
Ehud or Ahud: a Hebrew name, meaning "union". He was a left-handed judge, of the tribe of the sons of the right hand, "Benjamin" (Judg 3:12-30).
The scholar Origen links the cry of the people after eighteen years with God's sending Ehud the left-handed as a deliverer for them, saying:

v It is written: "So the children of Israel served Eglon the king of Moab eighteen years" (Judg 3:14). Note that the Scripture points to the measure of the punishment when it mentions "eight years" (Judg 3:8) the first time, and here "eighteen years". It is certain that the duration of the punishment was fixed according to the measure of the sin and the delay of repentance. As for the eighteen years in bondage, it is not mentioned during this period that they cried to the Lord, or turned from their evils. But it is said again that after these eighteen years "the children of Israel cried unto the LORD, the LORD raised them up a deliverer, Ehud the son of Gera, a Benjamite, a man lefthanded" (Judg 3:15).
What kind of man is this who was raised up to deliver the people of Israel?
He has nothing in himself that is of the left to do. Rather he has a right hand on both sides that work, and for this reason he was called left-handed: he has a right hand on both sides[1].

He was qualified to be a leader of the people and a judge of the Church. He does not do what is of the left, and also [his left hand does not know what his right hand does] (Mt 6:3); he is right-handed in faith and in works. He has nothing of what belongs to those on the left, of whom it is written: "Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels" (Mt 25:41). If we consider the possibility of connecting what preceded[2], I believe, from the point of view of spiritual understanding, that all the saints should be called "left-handed," and on the contrary Satan and his princes can be called "those of the left," because everything they do is of the left and leads to the eternal fire which belongs to those on the left...

Let us see what this left-handed judge did. "And by him the children of Israel sent a present unto Eglon the king of Moab. But Ehud made him a dagger which had two edges, of a cubit length; and he did gird it under his raiment upon his right thigh" (Judg 3:15-16).

Behold, you see that everything done by "this left-handed Ehud" is "right-handed"[3], is good in both hands and in the foot. For he carries the sword on his right thigh to come to "the king of Moab" and kill him. As we said before, these are the ones whom their God raised up for the deliverance of the people, and these deliverers or judges, who bear the image of leaders from "the heavenly host" (Lk 2:13) and of the higher powers whom God sends to help those who cry to Him with all their heart, set the people of Israel free; these are the ones who, through their change by repentance, are overtaken by divine mercy.

This agrees with other events in the Bible; in the book of Exodus, when our fathers the people of Israel were serving the Egyptians and the very cruel king Pharaoh for a long time in making "mortar and brick" (Ex 1:14), [they cried to the Lord] (Ex 2:23), "and their cry came up unto God" (Ex 2:23).

God brought them out by means of Moses before all, and the Bible mentions that the destroying angel was sent to destroy all the firstborn in Egypt, and did not touch any of the Israelites (Ex 11:5-7). It was made known that there was a heavenly power that led the people away from the yoke of bondage and destruction and overthrew the Egyptians. And something similar happened through history in the days of the Assyrians with King Sennacherib; where "an angel of God" was sent, and delivered the people from the siege and from imminent annihilation; the angel of the Lord smote 185,000 of the enemies in a single night (2 Kgs 19:35).

Therefore now, for the same reasons, we must take heed when we are delivered to captivity because of our sins, "we must cry to the Lord." But we do not cry with the mouth but from the heart[4], so that even if our heart grieves, [a fountain of tears may be produced from the eyes] (Jer 9:1), "All the night make I my bed to swim; I water my couch with my tears" (Ps 6:6). If we turn from the ways of evil so that we do not touch works of evil again, if we cease from pride, so that there is no more pride and we know no vanity, then God sends us His heavenly power by which we are freed from the grip of the Satan of bondage; this power provides us with everything good and useful, and we forsake "the broad way that leads to destruction" (Mt 7:13). God calls us to the right way, of which He said of Himself: "I am the way, the truth, and the life" (Jn 14:6), Jesus Christ our Lord, "to whom be praise and dominion for ever and ever. Amen" (1 Pet 4:11)[5].
Origen Geba: a Hebrew name, meaning "hill".
That is, Naaman, and Ahiah. And Gera, he removed them, and begat Uzza, and Ahihud. [7]
Ahiah: a Hebrew name, meaning "my brother".
Uzza: a Hebrew name, meaning "strength, that Jehovah is strength". He is the name of a son of Gera, of the descendants of Ehud the Benjamite (1 Chr 8:7).

Ahihud: a Hebrew name, meaning "brother of union". He was of the descendants of Ehud of the tribe of Benjamin, from the town of Gibnah (1 Chr 8:7). This man is mentioned in some manuscripts as Ahihod.
And Shaharaim begat children in the country of Moab, after he had sent away his two wives, Hushim and Baara. [8]
(Shajrayim) or Shaharaim: a Hebrew name, meaning "the two dawns". A Benjamite, father of a large family (1 Chr 8:8).

The Old Testament sometimes refers to divorce and polygamy without comment, but this does not mean God's pleasure in it. For He declared that He hates divorce (Mal 2:15-16), and the Lord Christ affirms: "Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives: but from the beginning it was not so" (Mt 19:8).
Hushim: a Hebrew name, meaning "haste, agitation". One of the wives of Shaharaim the Benjamite (1 Chr 8:8, 11).
Baara: a Hebrew name, meaning "burning". She was a wife of Shaharaim of the tribe of Benjamin.
And he begat of Hodesh his wife, Jobab, and Zibia, and Mesha, and Malcham. [9]
Hodesh: a Hebrew name, meaning "the crescent". It is the name of the wife of Shaharaim (1 Chr 8:9).
Jobab: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "shouting". It is the name of two Benjamite chiefs (1 Chr 8:9, 18).
Zibia: a Hebrew name, meaning "gazelle". A Benjamite, son of Shaharaim (1 Chr 8:9).
Malcham: a Hebrew name, meaning "their king". He was a Benjamite chief (1 Chr 8:9).
And Jeuz, and Shachia, and Mirma. These were his sons, heads of the fathers. [10]
Jeuz: a Hebrew name, meaning "the admonished". A Benjamite chief, son of Shaharaim by his wife Hodesh.
Shachia: a Hebrew name, likely meaning "Return, O Jehovah," and he is a Benjamite, son of Shaharaim (1 Chr 8:10), and this name appears in the form "Sakia" in some manuscripts.
Mirma: a Hebrew name, meaning "deceit". He was a Benjamite born to Shaharaim in Moab by his wife Hodesh.
And of Hushim he begat Abitub, and Elpaal. [11]
Abitub: a Hebrew name, meaning "my father is good, or goodness". It is the name of a Benjamite man, son of Shaharaim, whose mother's name was Hushim (1 Chr 8:11).
Elpaal: a Hebrew name, meaning "God has done". He was a Benjamite man, son of Shaharaim, and a head of a house among the houses of the fathers (1 Chr 8:1, 8, 11, 12, 18).
And the sons of Elpaal; Eber, and Misham, and Shamer, who built Ono, and Lod, with the towns thereof: [12]
Eber: a Hebrew name, meaning "crossing". There are two Benjamites with the same name: one the son of Elpaal, the other the son of Shashak (1 Chr 8:12, 22, 25).
Misham: a Hebrew name, meaning "swift," and he was a Benjamite (1 Chr 8:12).
Shamer: a Hebrew name, meaning "guard". He was of the sons of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:12).
Ono: a Hebrew name, meaning "strong". The name of a city in Benjamin. It was built by a Benjamite called Shamer.
Ono and Lod: they are not mentioned with the cities of Benjamin in (Josh 18:21-28). Lod is Lydda in (Acts 9:32).
Beriah also, and Shema. Temple, they were heads of the fathers of the inhabitants of Aijalon, who drove away the inhabitants of Gath. [13]
Shema: a Hebrew name, meaning "report". A Benjamite, one of the heads of the fathers who drove away the inhabitants of Gath.
Aijalon: a Hebrew name, meaning "oak". It belonged to the tribe of Dan (Josh 19:40-43), then became Benjamin's, then Judah's and Benjamin's in the time of Rehoboam (2 Chr 11:10).
And Ahio, Shashak, and Jeremoth [14]

Ahio: a Hebrew name, meaning "brotherly or brother of Jehovah". More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. A man of Benjamin, of the sons of Elpaal (1 Chr 8:14). 2. Another man of Benjamin, the son of Jeuel (Jeiel), by his wife Maachah (1 Chr 8:29-31).
Shashak: a Hebrew name, meaning "desire". He was one of the sons of Elpaal of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:14, 25).
Jeremoth: a Hebrew name, meaning "swollen, huge, tall," and he was the head of a Benjamite family (1 Chr 8:14). Perhaps he was the same as Jeroham.
And Zebadiah, and Arad, and Ader [15]

Zebadiah: a Hebrew name, meaning "Jehovah has given," a name borne by nine persons in the Old Testament, who were of little importance. Two of them are of the sons of Benjamin: the son of Beriah [15-16] and the son of Elpaal [17].
Arad: a Hebrew name, meaning "wild ass," and he was a man of the line of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:15).
Ader: a Hebrew name, meaning "flock," and he was the son of Elpaal, of the sons of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:15).
And Michael, and Ispah, and Joha, the sons of Beriah; [16]
Michael: a Hebrew name, meaning "Who is like God". It is the name of a Benjamite (1 Chr 8:16).
Ispah: a Benjamite chief, the son of Beriah (1 Chr 8:16).
Joha: he is the son of Beriah and a Benjamite chief (1 Chr 8:16), and his name appears in some translations in the form Yoha.
Beriah: a Hebrew name, meaning "excellent". It is the name of a Benjamite chief (1 Chr 8:13).
And Zebadiah, and Meshullam, and Hezeki, and Heber [17]
Meshullam: a Hebrew name, meaning "one who has received his recompense". It is the name of three persons of the descendants of Benjamin.
Hezeki: a Hebrew name, meaning "my strength," or an abbreviation of Hezekiah. A Benjamite, the son of Elpaal.
Heber: a Hebrew name, meaning "fellowship, partner". A Benjamite, the son of Shaharaim by Elpaal.
Ishmerai also, and Jezliah, and Jobab, the sons of Elpaal. [18]
Ishmerai: a Hebrew name, meaning "Jehovah guards". A Benjamite, the son of Elpaal (1 Chr 8:18).
Jezliah or Jezlia: a Hebrew name, meaning "eternal". He was a Benjamite who dwelt in Jerusalem.
Jobab: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "shouting," the name of two Benjamite chiefs.
And Jakim, and Zichri, and Zabdi [19]
Jakim: a Hebrew name, meaning "he raises up". He was a Benjamite (1 Chr 8:19).
Zabdi: a Hebrew name, meaning "God has given," and he was a man among the Benjamites (1 Chr 8:19).
And Elienai, and Zilthai, and Eliel [20]
Elienai: a Hebrew name, and it is likely an abbreviation of "Elihoenai," meaning "his eyes are toward Jehovah". He was the son of Shimhi, one of the chiefs of the sons of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:20).
Zilthai: a Hebrew name, meaning "Jehovah is shade or refuge". A Benjamite of the sons of Shimhi (1 Chr 8:20).
Eliel or Elieel: they are one name in the original Hebrew, meaning "El is God": the name of a Benjamite man, the son of Shimhi (1 Chr 8:21-22).
And Adaiah, and Beraiah, and Shimrath, the sons of Shimhi. [21]
Adaiah or Adaia: a Hebrew name, meaning "adornment of Jehovah". He was a son of Shimhi, of the sons of Benjamin.
Beraiah: a Hebrew name, meaning "whom Jehovah created". He was a Benjamite chief and a son of Shimhi.
Shimrath: a Hebrew name, meaning "the watcher or the guard". A Benjamite, the son of Shimhi (1 Chr 8:21).
Shimhi: (with a kasra under the ain) a Hebrew name, meaning "Jehovah hears". He was a Benjamite, head of a house in Eglon (1 Chr 8:21). He is called Shema in (1 Chr 8:13).
And Ishpan, and Heber, and Eliel [22]
Ishpan: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "he is bald". He was a Benjamite chief, the son of Shashak.
And Abdon, and Zichri, and Hanan [23]
Abdon: a Hebrew name, meaning "the enslaved," and two bear the same name: 1. A Benjamite, the son of Shashak (1 Chr 8:23). 2. A Benjamite, the son of Jeuel the Gibeonite (1 Chr 8:30; 9:36).
And Hananiah, and Elam, and Antothijah [24]
Hananiah: a Hebrew name, meaning "Jehovah has shown favour" or "has been gracious". A Benjamite, the son of Shashak.
Elam: a Hebrew name, of Akkadian origin, meaning "highlands". He was a son of Shashak, a head of a house in Benjamin (1 Chr 8:24).
Antothijah: a Hebrew name, perhaps ascribed to "Anathoth". He was a son of Shashak, of the sons of Benjamin.
And Iphedeiah, and Penuel, the sons of Shashak. [25]
Iphedeiah: a Hebrew name, meaning "Jehovah redeems". He was a Benjamite, the son of Shashak (1 Chr 8:25).
Penuel: a Hebrew name, meaning "face of God". It is the name of a Benjamite man, of the sons of Shashak.
And Shamsherai, and Shehariah, and Athaliah [26]
Shamsherai: a Benjamite, of the sons of Jeroham (1 Chr 8:26).
Shehariah: a Hebrew name, meaning "Jehovah is the dawn". He was a Benjamite, the son of Jeroham (1 Chr 8:26).
Athaliah: a Hebrew name, meaning "Jehovah is exalted". It is the name of a son of Jeroham, of the sons of Benjamin.
And Jaresiah, and Eliah, and Zichri, the sons of Jeroham. [27]
Jaresiah: a Hebrew name, meaning "Jehovah plants". He was a Benjamite, the son of Jeroham (1 Chr 8:27).
Eliah: a Hebrew name, meaning "my God is Jehovah". The Greek form of this name is Elias, and it is sometimes used in Arabic. It is the name of a son of Jeroham of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:27).
Zichri: a Hebrew name, meaning "remembered," and it is the name of three of the chiefs of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:19; 23:27).
Jeroham: a Hebrew name, meaning "he whom God has mercy upon, or whom He pleases". He was a Benjamite, two of whose sons were leaders, and he dwelt in Jerusalem (1 Chr 8:27).
These were heads of the fathers, by their generations, chief men.
These dwelt in Jerusalem. [28]
Here, as in [32], he referred to Jerusalem, and will speak of it in detail in the next chapter.
And at Gibeon dwelt the father of Gibeon; and his wife's name was Maachah: [29]

What the writer aimed at here is to speak of the ancestors of Saul and his descendants indirectly. The relation that links the names mentioned here is to present the family that was rejected, and in whose place the family of David took over.
Gibeon: a Hebrew name, meaning "hill". The ancestors of Saul dwelt there for a time, and they had influence.
The father of Gibeon: that is, the chief of the city of Gibeon (1 Chr 9:35). Gibeon is mentioned in (Josh 9-10).
Maachah: a Semitic name, meaning "injustice," and she was the wife of Jeuel the father of Gibeon, from whom Saul descended.
And his firstborn son Abdon, and Zur, and Kish, and Baal, and Nadab [30]
Zur: a Semitic name, meaning "rock". He was a son of the founder of Gibeon (1 Chr 8:30).

Nadab: a Hebrew name, meaning "generous". He was a son of Jeuel, and his mother's name was Maachah. He was of the sons of Benjamin. He used to live in Gibeon. He was the head of his house (1 Chr 8:30).
And Gedor, and Ahio, and Zacher. [31]
Gedor: a Hebrew name, meaning "fortress" or "walled place". He was a son of Jeuel, and the brother of Ner and Kish, ancestors of Saul (1 Chr 8:30-31).
Zacher: a Hebrew name, meaning "remembrance," a man of the sons of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:31).
And Mikloth begat Shimeah.
And these also dwelt with their brethren in Jerusalem, over against their brethren. [32]
Mikloth: a Hebrew name, meaning "staff". It is the name of a Benjamite (1 Chr 8:32).
Shimeah or Shimeam: a Benjamite, the son of Mikloth. He was dwelling in Jerusalem.

33 And Ner begat Kish, and Kish begat Saul, and Saul begat Jonathan, and Malchishua, and Abinadab, and Esh-baal. 34 And the son of Jonathan was Merib-baal; and Merib-baal begat Micah. 35 And the sons of Micah were, Pithon, and Melech, and Tarea, and Ahaz. 36 And Ahaz begat Jehoadah; and Jehoadah begat Alemeth, and Azmaveth, and Zimri; and Zimri begat Moza, 37 And Moza begat Binea: Rapha was his son, Eleasah his son, Azel his son: 38 And Azel had six sons, whose names are these, Azrikam, Bocheru, and Ishmael, and Sheariah, and Obadiah, and Hanan. All these were the sons of Azel. 39 And the sons of Eshek his brother were, Ulam his firstborn, Jehush the second, and Eliphelet the third. 40 And the sons of Ulam were mighty men of valour, archers, and had many sons, and sons' sons, an hundred and fifty. All these are of the sons of Benjamin.
And Ner begat Kish, and Kish begat Saul, and Saul begat Jonathan, and Malchishua, and Abinadab, and Esh-baal. [33]
Ner: a Hebrew name, meaning "light, lamp". He was a Benjamite, the son of Jeuel and Maachah, and the father of Kish the father of Saul (1 Chr 8:33).

Saul: Saul son of Kish was appointed the first king over Israel. He had an ideal appearance as a king in stature and bodily form, and he showed a kind of humility, courage and generosity when he was chosen king (1 Sam 9).

As king he obeyed God at the beginning of his reign, so he achieved great victories and success. He soon fell into pride, and usurped the work of the priesthood. His reliance on himself and his concern for his popularity rather than for conduct according to God's will isolated him from his people and cost him much, and even shattered his personality.
He tried to draw every man of valour to work with him, but not for the glory of God, rather for the sake of the growth of his popularity, so even some of his relatives turned away from him.
He tried to kill David more than once. His envy of David and his directing all his energies and capabilities to get rid of him led to the failure of Saul, not of David.

Jehonathan or Jonathan son of Saul: a Hebrew name, meaning "Jehovah has given". He was the opposite of his father; he was the lawful heir to the throne, and he was convinced that God had chosen David for the throne, and he became his close friend, and saved his life from his father's attempts to kill him (1 Sam 14-31). His soul was knit to David and he loved him greatly as his own soul. Despite Saul's warning to him about David, that he would take the throne, he did not envy David his victories and popularity.
He was marked by courage, loyalty and good leadership together with reliance on God.
Malchishua: a Hebrew name, meaning "the king is salvation".
Abinadab: a Hebrew name, meaning "the father is generous or delegated".
Esh-baal: a Hebrew name meaning "man of Baal," and it is the first name of Ish-bosheth son of Saul (1 Chr 8:33), that is, "man of shame". The purpose of changing the name was contempt for Baal.
And the son of Jonathan was Merib-baal; and Merib-baal begat Micah. [34]

Merib-baal, who is Mephibosheth son of Jonathan and grandson of Saul, because the word Baal was replaced by the word "bosheth" out of contempt. Mephibosheth: a Hebrew name, meaning "removal of idols".
There are two names connected with the idol god "Baal," namely Esh-baal and Merib-baal. These two names were changed in (2 Sam 2:8; 9:6), and they are Ish-bosheth and Mephibosheth[6].

When he was five years old he fell from the hands of his nurse, and was lamed, which stayed with him all his life. David sought out this Mephibosheth after he became king, and made him dwell in his palace, and restored to him what had belonged to his father; but since some signs of treachery appeared from him during the rebellion of Absalom, he took back from him at first all that he had, and gave it to Ziba his servant. Then afterward he took pity on him, and gave half to Ziba and restored to him the other half. He is also called Meribaal (1 Chr 8:34).
Why was the change of the two names mentioned in Second Samuel, and not in Chronicles?

Second Samuel was in the Hebrew Bible in the second division, Nebiim (the Prophets) Nebiwim. These books were read in the synagogue, where it is not fitting to mention the name of a pagan god, "Baal," so the reader replaces the word "Baal" with "bosheth," which means "naked". This change was used in the text of the book, whereas in the two books of Chronicles there was no need for this change, since the two books were in the third division, "Ketubim," meaning "the Writings." The books of this division were not read in the synagogue until a late time. This explains that the texts of the Bible were connected with worship.
Micah: a Hebrew name, meaning "like Jehovah". He was the son of Mephibosheth or Meribaal and a grandson of Jonathan.
And the sons of Micah were, Pithon, and Melech, and Tarea, and Ahaz. [35]
Pithon: the son of Jonathan son of Saul (1 Chr 8:35).
Melech: a Hebrew name, meaning "king".
Tarea or Tahrim: a Hebrew name, meaning "crafty". He was a man of the descendants of Saul through Jonathan.
Ahaz: a Hebrew name, meaning "he held," that is, "the Lord held". He was the son of Micah, of the descendants of Jonathan.
And Ahaz begat Jehoadah; and Jehoadah begat Alemeth, and Azmaveth, and Zimri.
And Zimri begat Moza [36]
Jehoadah: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "Jehovah has numbered". He was the son of Ahaz, of the descendants of Jonathan son of Saul (1 Chr 8:36).
Alemeth: a Hebrew name, meaning "concealment," and he was the son of Jehoadah, of the sons of Benjamin, of the grandsons of King Saul (1 Chr 8:36; 9:42).
Azmaveth: a Hebrew name, meaning "death is strong". He was the son of Jehoadah, and one of the grandsons of Jehonathan.

Zimri: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "he who resembles the wild ox". More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. A Benjamite of the descendants of Jonathan son of Saul (1 Chr 8:36). 2. A commander in the army of Israel, who was over half of the chariots of Elah son of Baasha king of Israel. Then he conspired against his lord and killed him, fulfilling the divine judgment on the house of Baasha. Some thought that he was of the descendants of Saul, trying to recover the old kingship (1 Kgs 16:10-11).
Moza: a Hebrew name, meaning "exit," the name of a man of the descendants of Saul.
And Moza begat Binea: and Rapha was his son, Eleasah his son, Azel his son [37]
Binea: he is the son of Moza, of the descendants of Jonathan son of Saul (1 Chr 8:37).
Rapha: a Hebrew name, meaning "Jehovah has healed, that is, God has healed". He was a man of the descendants of Saul.
Eleasah: a Hebrew name, meaning "God has made". He is the name of a man of the descendants of Saul and of his son Jonathan (1 Chr 8:33-37). His name appears in this latter text in the form "Elasah".
And Azel had six sons, whose names are these:
Azrikam, Bocheru, and Ishmael, and Sheariah, and Obadiah, and Hanan.
All these were the sons of Azel. [38]
Azel: a Hebrew name, meaning "noble or well-born". It is the name of a man of the descendants of Jonathan son of Saul.

Azrikam: a Hebrew name, meaning "my help has risen". More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. A son of Azel, one of the descendants of Jehonathan son of Saul (1 Chr 8:38). 2. A son of Gera, of the descendants of Ehud the Benjamite (1 Chr 8:6).
Bocheru: a Hebrew name, meaning "firstborn". He was a son of Azel (1 Chr 8:38).
Ishmael: a Hebrew name, meaning "God hears". He was a Benjamite called Ishmael son of Azel.
Sheariah: a Hebrew name, meaning "power of Jehovah". He was a man of the descendants of Saul (1 Chr 8:38).
Obadiah: a Hebrew name, meaning "servant of Jehovah," and he was the son of Azel, of the grandsons of Jehoshaphat son of Saul (1 Chr 8:38; 9:44).

Hanan: a Hebrew name, meaning "gracious, compassionate, generous". More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. A famous man of Benjamin, the son of Shashak (1 Chr 8:23). 2. A son of Azel, of the descendants of Jonathan son of Saul (1 Chr 8:38).
And the sons of Eshek his brother were, Ulam his firstborn, Jehush the second, and Eliphelet the third. [39]
Eshek: a Hebrew name, meaning "cruelty". He was a man of the line of Saul, of the Benjamites.
Ulam: a Hebrew name, meaning "first". He was the son of Eshek of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:39). The sons of Ulam were heroes of war (1 Chr 8:40).
Jehush: a Semitic name, meaning "God helps," and he was the head of a Benjamite house of the descendants of Saul.
